leaf_description: Leaves 10--15, to 4 m long, straight, but lower ones tending to droop | leaf sheath to 150 cm long, light green suffused with lilac, with dense grey tomentum | Pinnae 80--120 each side of rachis, regularly arranged, to 127 cm long, acuminate, laxly pendulous, green on both surfaces
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence to 125 cm long, branched to 2 orders, rachillae to 62 cm long, flexuose, at first erect but pendulous in fruit
flower_description: Flowers white, opposite, protogynous | Staminate flower to 10 mm long, pistillode lacking | Pistillate flower globose, to 3 mm high
fruit_description: Fruit ovoid, to 10 mm long, to 5 mm diam., deep maroon with few blue grey longitudinal stripes, epicarp smooth, mesocarp thin, fleshy, fibres dense and thick | endocarp crustose
seed_description: Seed globose to ovoid, to 4 mm diam
habitat_description: Grows on various soiltypes in rainforest and swampforest at sea-level.
distribution_description: Occurs in Qld, distributed from just W of Somerset, Cape York Penin., S to Mt Carter, S of Iron Ra., and on some Torres Strait islands; also in New Guinea and Aru and Bismarck Is.
notes: The combination Gulubia costata (F.M.Bailey) Becc. appears in the Australian Plant Name Index (A.Chapman, 1991) but it has not been validly published. For a discussion of the interesting nomenclatural history of this name, see W.J.Baker & A.H.B.Loo, Kew Bull. 59: 61--68 (2004) and J.L.Dowe, Austral. Palms 243 (2010).

habit_description: Solitary palm to 35 m tall
leaf_description: Leaves 9--12, to 2.5 m long, arching, with apex recurved | leaf sheath elongate, yellow-green with white to grey tomentum | Pinnae 50--60 each side of rachis, erect, regularly arranged, linear, to 90 cm long, acute, coriaceous, grey-green on both surfaces
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence to 50 cm long, branched to 2 orders, rachillae at first erect but pendulous with fruit
flower_description: Flowers white to cream-yellow, opposite, lemon-scented, protandrous | Staminate flower to 10 mm long, pistillode lacking | Pistillate flower conical, to 5 mm high
fruit_description: Fruit ellipsoid to cylindric, to 15 mm long, to 8 mm diam., brick red, epicarp smooth, mesocarp thin, dry, densely fibrous, fibres thin | endocarp thin
seed_description: Seed elongate, to 14 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in open forest on sandy soils or sandstoneescarpments.
distribution_description: Endemic to the N.T., on Croker and Melville Is, and throughout the Top End from Adelaide R. E to Arnhem Land, and S to the headwaters of the South Alligator R.

habit_description: Moderate clustering palm to 25 m tall
stem_description: stems to 12 cm diam | axes light green, erect at first, becoming pendulous with fruit, rachillae straight
leaf_description: Leaves to 2 m long | leaf sheath elongate, green with moderate whitish tomentum | Pinnae 7--17 each side of rachis, irregularly arranged and grouped, linear, erect, to 45 cm long, truncate and praemorse apically, dark green on both surfaces, apical pinnae basally united
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence to 35 cm long, branched to 1 order
flower_description: Flowers decussate, cream, protogynous | Staminate flower to 9 mm long, to 4 mm diam., pistillode lacking | Pistillate flower globose, much smaller than staminate
fruit_description: Fruit ovoid to globose, to 10 mm long, red, epicarp smooth, mesocarp dry, fibres thin | endocarp crustose
seed_description: Seed globose, to 8 mm diam
habitat_description: Grows on various soil types in rainforest, monsoon forest and swamp forest at 0--200 m alt.
distribution_description: Occurs in the N.T. on Bathurst, Melville and Croker Is, and across the Top End from Moyle R. E to Groote Eylandt, and in Qld from northern Cape York Peninsula to Mission Beach.

habit_description: Solitary or clustering palm to 8 m tall
leaf_description: Leaves to 2.5 m long, arching | Pinnae 10--30 each side of rachis, ascending to horizontal, to 40 cm long, dark green adaxially, lighter green abaxially
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence to 1.5 m long | peduncle to 40 cm long
flower_description: Staminate flowers broadly bullet-shaped, to 9 mm long | Pistillate flowers to 5 mm high
fruit_description: Fruit to 18 mm long
habitat_description: Grows on various soil types in rainforest at 100--1600 m alt.
distribution_description: Endemic to NE Qld, from Mt Spurgeon to Paluma Ra.

common_name: Little Mountain Palm, Moorei Palm, Mountain Palm.
habit_description: Palm with sturdy trunk to 2 m high
leaf_description: leaf scars 1--2 cm apart | Leaves stiff, arcuate, 1--1.5 m long | petiole stout, 20--30 cm long | pinnae 25--40 cm long
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 30--50 cm long, spreading stiffly, with 100 or more ultimately slender branches
flower_description: Male flowers developing first | petals c. twice as long as sepals | anthers dorsifixed, pistillode cylindrical | Female flowers cream-coloured, 8 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit c. 1 cm diam., red
ecology_description: Prolific seed producer (Department of Environment and Climate Change (NSW) 2007: 175).
habitat_description: Confined to the dwarf forest mainly above 750 m on Mounts Gower and Lidgbird (Green 1994: 411); sheltered closed forest of the mountain summits, rarely lower, a conspicuous component of the Mount Gower cloud forest (Department of Environment and Climate Change (NSW) 2007: 175).
distribution_description: Endemic to Lord Howe Island.
seedling_description: A stout, dwarf palm with trunk to 2 m high and leaves to 1.5 m long, arching and sometimes twisted, forming a cone-shaped crown.

common_name: Native Fan Palm, Mission Beach Fan Palm.
habit_description: Solitary or rarely clustered bisexual palm
leaf_description: Leaves numerous, erect to semi-drooping, 200--400 cm long | sheath with brown to blackish fibres | petiole 150--200 cm long, 2--3.5 cm diam., armed with marginal spines throughout or only in basal parts | leaf blade nearly circular, 120--180 cm diam., dark green adaxially, pale abaxially | segments elongate-obcuneate, 80--120 cm long, 10--40 cm wide
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 200--500 cm long, arcuate to pendulous, longer than leaves | prophyll to 20 cm long, glabrous, peduncular bracts narrow, glabrous, rachillae glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, in pairs or sympodial clusters of 3 or 4, white to yellow
fruit_description: Fruit ovoid, 8--15 mm long, 8--13 mm diam., orange-red
habitat_description: Grows in rainforest and swamp forest at 0--1100 m alt., on various soil types; sometimes forms almost pure stands.
distribution_description: Two varieties occur in Queensland from Torres Strait Islands to Herbert River.

leaf_description: Leaf sheaths disintegrating into a thick, light brown mat of fibres that sometimes slides down the stem after detachment | Petiole conspicuously armed on lower half
flower_description: Flowers mostly in pairs or sympodial clusters of 3 or 4, but solitary in rachillae apices
distribution_description: Occurs from N of Cooktown to Herbert River, Qld.

leaf_description: Leaf sheath disintegrating into a dark brown to blackish, fibrous mesh | Petiole inconspicuously armed at base only
flower_description: Flowers mostly solitary throughout rachillae
distribution_description: Occurs from Moa Is. in Torres Strait to Wenlock River in the west, and south to about Cooktown, Qld.

habit_description: Clustering palm to 5 m tall
leaf_description: Leaves 6--14, to 90 cm long, most commonly bifid, very infrequently partially segmented or paripinnate | leaf sheath green, moderately fibrous on margins | petiole 0--2 cm long | Pinnae 2--12 each side of rachis, single or united, rigid, to 30 cm long, 5--900 mm wide, dull or semi-glossy green adaxially, lighter green abaxially | veins raised on both surfaces
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence to 80 cm long | peduncle to 40 cm long | rachis to 40 cm long
flower_description: Staminate flowers symmetric, broadly bullet-shaped in bud, to 4 mm long, green | stamens 4--7, with connective not extending beyond anther
fruit_description: Fruit elongate to cylindric, 10--15 mm long, 5--6 mm wide, yellow or red
habitat_description: Grows on granitic soils in rainforest at 400--1300 m alt.
distribution_description: Endemic to NE Qld, confined to Mts Spurgeon and Lewis.

habit_description: Clustering palm to 3 m tall
leaf_description: Leaves 5--9, to 70 cm long, irregularly or regularly paripinnate | leaf sheath green, moderately fibrous on margins | petiole 1--23 cm long | Pinnae 2--12 each side of rachis, single or united, lax, to 37 cm long, 1--8 mm wide, light green to mid green adaxially, lighter green abaxially | veins raised on both surfaces
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence to 90 cm long | peduncle to 40 cm long | rachis to 40 cm long
flower_description: Staminate flowers symmetric, globose to broadly bullet-shaped, to 2--5 mm long, cream to dull yellow | stamens 8--12, with connective not extending beyond anther
fruit_description: Fruit globose to turbinate, 5--9 mm long, 5--8 mm wide, yelloworange, or pink to red
habitat_description: Usually ongranitic soils, in rainforest from near sea-level to 1600 m alt.
distribution_description: Endemic to NE Qld, from Mt Spurgeon to Palmerston Ra.

common_name: Clustered Walking-stick Palm, Minor Walking Stick Palm.
habit_description: Clustering palm to 5 m tall
leaf_description: Leaves 7--12, to 110 cm long, irregularly or regularly paripinnate | leaf sheath green, moderately fibrous on margins | petiole 4--51 cm long | Pinnae 2--12 each side of rachis, single or united, lax, to 51 cm long, 10--40 mm wide, chartaceous, semi-glossy dark green adaxially, lighter green abaxially | veins prominent only on adaxial surface
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence to 80 cm long | peduncle to 40 cm long | rachis to 40 cm long
flower_description: Staminate flowers symmetric, broadly bullet-shaped in bud, to 3 mm long, green | stamens 7--20, with connective not extending beyond anther
fruit_description: Fruit elongate to cylindric, 8--18 mm long, 3--8 mm wide, yellow or red
habitat_description: Grows on many soil types in rainforest 0--1200 m alt.
distribution_description: Endemic to NE Qld; in southern McIlwraith Ra. where it is rare, and commonly between Mt Amos and Mission Beach, and inland to Windsor Tableland.

habit_description: Solitary palm to 2--6 m tall
leaf_description: Leaves 5--10, to 130 cm long, irregularly or regularly pinnate | leaf sheath green, moderately fibrous on margins | petiole 24--80 cm long | Pinnae 5--15 each side of rachis, single or united, lax, to 30 cm long, 5--200 mm wide, glossy mid to dark green adaxially, lighter green abaxially | veins raised on both surfaces
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence to 100 cm long | peduncle to 60 cm long | rachis to 50 cm long
flower_description: Staminate flowers asymmetric, angled to pyramidal in bud, to 13 mm long | perianth green | stamens 8--12, with connective extending beyond anther
fruit_description: Fruit globose to ovoid to elongate to cylindric, 12--15 mm long, 5--10 mm wide, red
habitat_description: Usually on basaltic soils, in rainforest, 0--1200 m alt.
distribution_description: Endemic to S Qld and northern N.S.W., from near Gympie to Taree.

habit_description: Clustering palm to 3 m tall
leaf_description: Leaves 8--12, to 60 cm long, irregularly or regularly paripinnate | leaf sheath green, moderately fibrous on margins | petiole 6--13 cm long | Pinnae 2--12 each side of rachis, single or united, rigid, to 30 cm long, 5--200 mm wide, dull to semi-glossy dark green adaxially, lighter green abaxially | veins prominent on both surfaces
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence to 60 cm long | peduncle to 30 cm long | rachis to 30 cm long
flower_description: Staminate flowers globose to broadly bullet-shaped in bud, symmetric, to 3 mm long | stamens 6--9, with connective not extending beyond anther
fruit_description: Fruit elongate to cylindric, 10--15 mm long, 5--7 mm wide, yellow or red
habitat_description: Usually on granitic soils, in rainforest at 300--1600 malt.
distribution_description: Endemic to NE Qld, confined to Bellenden Ker Ra, Murray Prior Ra. and SW Atherton Tablelands.

leaf_description: Leaves 25--30 in a rigid dense crown | petiole 90--130 cm long, 25--30 mm wide, smooth or with marginal spines | leaf blade nearly circular, 90--140 cm long, rigid, pale green to glaucous, waxy, dull, abaxially glabrous, divided for more than 1/2 its length | segments 50--66, rigid, deeply bifurcate, with attenuate lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 150--270 cm long, branched to 3 orders | bracts glabrous to sparsely scaly, rachillae minutely warty
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in pairs, cylindric, cream to yellowish | sepals triangular, 0.8--1 mm long, acute | petals triangular, 2--3 mm long, acute to mucronate | stamens c. 2 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit globose, 25--40 mm diam., dark brown
seed_description: Seed globose, 14--20 mm diam
habitat_description: Grows in moist areas close to streams.
distribution_description: Endemic to the Hamersley Region, W.A., mainly in the upper reaches of the Fortescue, Robe and Ashburton Rivers. A small disjunct population occurs in the Cape Ra., North West Cape Peninsula, on the W side of Exmouth Gulf.

common_name: Australian Cabbage Palm, Cabbage Palm, Cabbage Tree.
leaf_description: Leaves 35--60 in an open to dense crown | petiole 150--250 cm long, 10--20 mm wide, smooth or with short recurved marginal thorns | leaf blade circular, 100--130 cm long, chartaceous, dark green, glossy, abaxially glabrous, divided to c. 1/2 its length | segments 80--100, drooping distally, deeply bifurcate, with acute lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 100--250 cm long, branched to 5 orders | bracts densely floccose, rachillae glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in sympodial clusters of 2--4, funnel-shaped, cream to pale yellow | sepals triangular, 1.2--2 mm long, acute, fleshy | petals triangular to ovate, 2--3.5 mm long, subacute to obtuse, fleshy | stamens c. 2.5 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit globose, 12--22 mm diam., reddish brown to dull black
seed_description: Seed globose, 10--16 mm diam
habitat_description: Grows in wet areas of open forest, swamp forest, along stream banks and in rainforest. Often locally common and may grow in large colonies.
distribution_description: Endemic to eastern Australia where distributed S from Paluma Ra., Qld, to far eastern Vic. In the northern part of its range it is confined to high elevations but over most of its distribution it occurs in coastal and near-coastal lowland areas.

leaf_description: petiole stubs elongate, persistent | Leaves 30--50 in a dense rounded crown | petiole 120--200 cm long, 10--18 mm wide, with sharp thorns on proximal margins | leaf blade circular, 90--160 cm diam., chartaceous, dark green, abaxially glabrous, glossy, divided for c. 1/2 its length | segments 50--80, drooping distally, deeply bifurcate, with acute lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 120--210 cm long, branched to 2 orders | bracts with scattered appressed silver scales, rachillae minutely pubescent
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in sympodial clusters of 2 or 3, tubular, cream to pale yellow | sepals triangular, 0.8--2 mm long, acute, membranous | petals broadly triangular, 1--1.3 mm long, acute, fleshy | stamens c. 1 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit obovoid to pyriform, 9--13 mm long, c. 10 mm diam., purple-black, pruinose
seed_description: Seed ovoid, 8--9 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in swamp forests, on alluvial flats, on the leeward side of mangroves and in moist to wet areas in monsoonal thickets and gallery forests.
distribution_description: Occurs in northern Northern Territory from Daly River across the Top End to E Arnhem Land and N Queensland from Moa Island, Torres Strait and Cape York Peninsula to McIlwraith Ra.; also in southern New Guinea.

leaf_description: Leaves 50--65 in a globose to hemispherical crown, rigid, arcuate to drooping | petiole 120--300 cm long, with scattered short thorns on proximal margins | leaf blade nearly circular, 155--165 cm long, coriaceous, green, abaxially glabrous, divided for slightly more than 1/2 its length | segments 60--78, apically pendulous, deeply bifurcate, with attenuate lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescences moderately sexually dimorphic, male 120--180 cm long, branched to 4 orders, female 160--250 cm long, branched to 5 orders | bracts and rachillae glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in sympodial clusters of 2--4, funnel-shaped, white to cream | sepals triangular, c. 1.5 mm long, acute, membranous | petals narrowly ovate, c. 2.0 mm long, acute | stamens c. 1.0 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit globose, 9--12 mm long, shiny black
seed_description: Seed globose to subglobose, c. 9 mm diam
habitat_description: Grows in alluvium as a riparian element along seasonal streams, and on the inland margins of mangroves.
distribution_description: Endemic to NE Qld on the Kennedy River and its tributaries and in the Cooktown area.

common_name: Weeping Cabbage Palm, Ribbon Fan Palm.
leaf_description: Leaves 30--60, in a broad, flattish crown | petiole 150--280 cm long, 18--24 mm wide, with small thorns on proximal margins | leaf blade circular, 120--185 cm long, coriaceous, yellowish green, abaxially glabrous, divided nearly to base | segments 70--84, distally pendulous, deeply bifurcate, with attenuate lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 100--350 cm long, branched to 4 orders | bracts glabrous to papillose, rachillae minutely papillose
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in sympodial clusters of 2--6, funnel-shaped, yellow | sepals ovate-triangular, c. 1.3 mm long, obtuse, membranous | petals broadly ovate, 1.5--1.8 mm long, obtuse, fleshy | stamens c. 1.5 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit globose, 12--18 mm diam., black, shiny
seed_description: Seed globose, c. 10 mm diam
habitat_description: Grows in coastal and near-coastal lowlands, and infrequently inland at moderate elevation, usually in small groups, in open forest, littoral rainforest and dry rainforest; also along streams and on swamp margins.
distribution_description: Endemic to E Qld between Black River and Rainbow Beach.

leaf_description: Leaves 30--60 in an open rounded or inverted-conical crown | petiole 150--230 cm long, 15--25 mm wide, smooth or with small marginal thorns | leaf base purple | leaf blade circular, 100--150 cm long, coriaceous, dark green, glossy, abaxially glabrous, divided to near middle or more | segments 60--84, drooping distally, deeply bifurcate, with attenuate lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 150--300 cm long, branched to 3 orders | bracts sparsely scaly, rachillae minutely pubescent
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in sympodial clusters of 2--5, funnel-shaped, cream | sepals narrowly triangular, 0.7--1.5 mm long, subacute, fleshy | petals broadly ovate, 1.2--2 mm long, thickened at apex, fleshy | stamens c. 1.5 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit globose to pyriform, 10--12 mm diam., purple-black
seed_description: Seed ellipsoid, 8--9 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in coastal and near-coastal regions on the landward side of mangroves, open forest and seasonally dry swamp forest on coastal plains and adjacent foothills, and along the margins of streams and estuaries.
distribution_description: Endemic to NE Qld between Kurrimine Beach and the Conway Ra.

leaf_description: leaf bases often persistent | Leaves 9--20 in an open crown | petiole 50--200 cm long, 1.4--2 cm wide, arcuate, thorny on margins | leaf blade nearly circular, 60--90 cm long, coriaceous, pale greyish green, pruinose, abaxially glabrous, divided for more than 1/2 its length | segments 40--50, rigid, deeply bifurcate, with acute lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 100--200 cm long, branched to 4 orders | bracts with appressed scales, rachillae glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in sympodial clusters of 2--4, campanulate, cream to yellow | sepals broadly ovate, 0.2--1 mm long, acute, fleshy | petals narrowly ovate, 0.5--1.9 mm long, acute, thick | stamens c. 1.5 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit ellipsoid to obovoid, 12--16 mm long, glossy, purple-black
seed_description: Seed ellipsoid, 10--13 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in open woodland, usually on flat sites or depressions and forms extensive colonies.
distribution_description: Endemic to the Kimberley Region, W.A., from Mitchell Plateau to Doongan Station.

leaf_description: Leaves 25--35 in an open rounded crown | petiole 150--250 cm long, 12--15 mm wide, with basal marginal thorns | leaf blade circular, 90--100 cm long, coriaceous, greyish green to glaucous adaxially, with coppery brown floccose tomentum abaxially, divided for c. 1/2 its length | segments 60--66, rigid, shallowly bifurcate, with acute to acuminate lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 100--230 cm long, branched to 4 orders | bracts with orange-brown scales, rachillae densely papillose
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in sympodial clusters of 2 or 3, funnel-shaped, yellow | sepals narrowly triangular, 1--1.3 mm long, acute, membranous | petals broadly ovate, 1.6--2 mm long, acute, thick | stamens c. 1.6 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit globose, 12--16 mm diam., black, pruinose
seed_description: Seed globose, 10--13 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in moist sites in open forest and woodland, especially in gullies and gorges near streams and waterfalls at cliff bases.
distribution_description: Endemic on the Blackdown Tableland, Qld.

leaf_description: Leaves 8--15 in an open crown | petiole 40--70 cm long, 6--14 mm wide, with small marginal thorns | leaf blade circular, 30--50 cm long, chartaceous, dark green, glossy, abaxially glabrous, divided to more than 1/2 its length | segments 30--44, rigid, bifurcate, with acuminate lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescences sexually dimorphic, male arcuate, to 180 cm long, with 4--7 partial inflorescences branched to 4 orders, female erect, to 230 cm long, with a single distal partial inflorescence branched to 3 orders | bracts with small appressed scales, rachillae pubescent
flower_description: Flowers, male and female similar, solitary or in sympodial clusters of 2--4, globose, yellow | sepals broadly ovate, 0.7--1.4 mm long, cuspidate, membranous | petals broadly ovate, 1.5--1.9 mm long, acute, fleshy | stamens c. 1.3 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit ellipsoid, pyriform or obovoid, 10--19 mm long, shiny, black
seed_description: Seed ellipsoid, 7--9 mm long
habitat_description: Widely distributed in sparse forest and woodland growing in deep sandy soils. Usually occurs in extensive populations.
distribution_description: Endemic to the northern parts of N.T. from near Fitzmaurice R. across the Top End to Cape Arnhem and islands in western Gulf of Carpentaria, and as far inland as Katherine.
notes: This species shows strong inflorescence dimorphism between plants, which are apparently functionally male or female. Both types however have basically similar floral morphology.

leaf_description: Leaves 10--30 in an open rounded crown, usually arcuate to drooping | petiole 60--90 cm long, 6--10 mm wide, smooth or with small marginal thorns proximally | leaf blade suborbicular, 30--70 cm long, light green to grey, pruinose, abaxially glabrous, divided almost to base | segments 24--48, widely spaced, rigid, deeply bifurcate, with acuminate-filiform lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 40--90 cm long, branched to 3 orders | bracts pubescent, rachillae glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in sympodial clusters of 2 or 3, funnel-shaped, cream to white | sepals narrowly triangular, 0.7--1.4 mm long, acute, membranous | petals broadly ovate, 1.5--1.9 mm long, apiculate, thick | stamens c. 1.5 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit obovoid to pyriform, 10--13 mm long, black, pruinose
seed_description: Seed ellipsoid, 8--9 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in open forest and woodland and in sandstone gorges and on outcrops.
distribution_description: Endemic to northern N.T. and far NW Qld, including islands in W Gulf of Carpentaria. Distributed from the headwaters of the Daly River across the Top End and into Qld to Westmoreland Station.

leaf_description: Leaves 35--45 in an open rounded crown | petiole 150--200 cm long, 30--35 mm wide, densely floccose, with sharp thorns on basal margins | leaf blade circular, 130--190 cm long, coriaceous, pale green to glaucous, strongly pruinose, waxy, abaxially glabrous, divided for c. 1/2 its length | segments 70--92, pendulous distally, deeply bifurcate, with acuminate-attenuate lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 140--220 cm long, branched to 4 orders | bracts and rachillae densely lanuginose
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in pairs, funnel-shaped, cream | sepals narrowly triangular, c. 1.5 mm long, acuminate to aristate, fleshy | petals triangular, 2.8--3 mm long, acute, thick | stamens c. 2 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit globose, 25--36 mm diam., purple-brown to black
seed_description: Seed globose, 18--22 mm long
habitat_description: Grows along the margins of streams and in gullies which only flow seasonally.
distribution_description: Endemic to NE Qld where restricted to a few small populations on tributaries of the Burdekin River.

leaf_description: Leaves 25--40 in an open crown, arcuate to drooping | petiole 70--200 cm long, 10--17 mm wide, with small scattered marginal thorns | leaf blade circular, 60--100 cm long, coriaceous, pale green, glaucous to glossy, abaxially glabrous, divided almost to base | segments 34--50, widely spaced, distally drooping, deeply bifurcate, with attenuate-filiform lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 20--160 cm long, branched to 3 orders | bracts tomentose, rachillae glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in sympodial clusters of 2--4, broadly funnel-shaped, cream | sepals triangular, 0.7--1.8 mm long, acute, membranous | petals broadly ovate, 1.2--3 mm long, acute to cuspidate
fruit_description: Fruit obovoid, 8--14 mm long, black
seed_description: Seed ellipsoid, 7--9 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in open forest and on sandstone outcrops and in gorges.
distribution_description: Endemic to the N Kimberley region of W.A. from Sir Graham Moore Is. to Sale River and inland to King Leopold and Durack Ranges with a disjunct population in the Victoria R. valley, N.T., near the W.A. border.

habit_description: See subspecies profiles
distribution_description: N.T., Qld.

common_name: Palm Valley Livistona, Central Australia Livistona.
leaf_description: Leaves 30--50 in a dense crown, obliquely erect to drooping | petiole 150--250 cm long, 20--45 mm wide, with small basal marginal thorns | leaf blade circular, 100--220 cm diam, coriaceous, grey-green and glossy adaxially, pruinose and glabrous abaxially, divided for c. 1/2 its length | segments 50--86, drooping distally, deeply bifurcate with attenuate lobes | distal segments overlapping | outer margin of distal segments prickly
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 125--250 cm long, branched to 4 orders | bracts with dense white appressed scales, rachillae glabrous
flower_description: Flowers in sympodial clusters of 3--6, campanulate, greenish cream | sepals ovate, 0.8--1 mm long, bluntly acute, membranous | petals broadly oblong, 1.2--1.5 mm long, acute | stamens c. 1.2 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit globose, 12--18 mm diam., semi-glossy, black
seed_description: Seed oblate, 8--12 mm long
habitat_description: Grows close to water along the banks of the river, which in this locality runs mainly through a sandstone gorge.
distribution_description: Endemic to Palm Valley on the Finke River system, Macdonnell Ra., N.T.
notes: New leaves of young plants of this species characteristically are tinged red.

leaf_description: Leaves 30--50 in a dense crown | petiole 150--250 cm long, 20--30 mm wide, with hard black marginal thorns | leaf blade circular, 100--150 cm diam., coriaceous, semi-glossy mid-green adaxially, glabrous and grey to glaucous abaxially, divided for c. 1/3 its length | segments 50--78, drooping distally, deeply bifurcate, with acuminate lobes
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 100--250 cm long, branched to 4 orders | bracts with sparse to dense white scales, rachillae glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in sympodial clusters of 2--8, globose, cream | sepals broadly ovate, c. 2 mm long, thin, acute | petals triangular, 1.0--1.4 mm long, obtuse | stamens c. 1.2 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit globose, 12--14 mm diam., purple-black
seed_description: Seed globose, 9--11 mm long
distribution_description: Endemic, with the main population occurring in far NW Qld on the stream systems of the Gregory, Leichhardt, Nicolson and Albert Rivers; smaller populations occur in the N.T. near Mataranka on the Roper River and on the South Alligator River.

common_name: Cairns Fan Palm, Northern Cabbage Tree Palm.

Its drift seeds (propagules adapted to float and tolerate immersion in sea water, allowing them to be dispersed long distances by ocean currents) are illustrated in Pike & Leach (1997: 138) and Claussen (2005: 134). The disseminule is occasionally found as flotsam at Ashmore, and is described and illustrated by Pike & Leach (1997: 128, 138).

habitat_description: Grows in open forest.

habitat_description: Grows in open forest or fringing forest situations.
distribution_description: Occurs from near Kalpowar to Beenleigh, southeastern Queensland, and possibly to Port Macquarie, northeastern New South Wales (pers. comm. D. Sands).

habit_description: Robust climber
leaf_description: Leaves, pseudo-stipules absent | petiole 3--6 cm long | lamina broadly triangular-ovate, 6--14 cm long, 6--10 cm wide, glabrous above, sparsely puberulent below | base deeply cordate | apex acuminate to rounded

habit_description: Slender vine

habit_description: Robust vine

ecology_description: This species is a food plant of the Richmond Birdwing Butterfly, Troides richmondius (Gray). Richmond Birdwing Butterflies are said to have occurred in the Many Peaks Range area west of Miriam Vale, Queensland, though there are no specimen records of either the butterfly or the host to support this observation.
habitat_description: Grows in notophyll vine forest, now rare due to clearing of lowland riverine and littoral closed forest.
distribution_description: Recorded from southeast Queensland (with 2 specimens recorded from the Atherton Tableland, north Queensland) and northeast New South Wales, between the Mary and Clarence Rivers.

leaf_description: Leaves oblong to broadly oblong, very obtuse, pubescent to puberulent with multicellular hairs on both surfaces, densely glandular dotted below
habitat_description: Grows in open forest or on rocky areas, scree slopes, etc.

habitat_description: Generally grows in open forest or woodland, or rocky areas.
distribution_description: Occurs from northeastern Northern Territory and from Cape York Peninsula to near Rockhampton, Queensland, though there is one old record stated to be from 'Elliot R' (between Bundaberg and Maryborough).

habit_description: Stout vine, glabrous
stem_description: stems to 5 m long | young branches glaucous

habitat_description: Recorded from forested area on roadside.
distribution_description: Native of tropical America. Recorded near Cairns, north Queensland.

habit_description: Slender twiner
stem_description: stems to 10 m long | young branches minutely pubescent, glabrescent
leaf_description: Leaves | petiole 1--2.5 cm long | lamina oblong-triangular or sagittate, 7--15 cm long, 2--5 cm wide, glabrous on both surfaces | base cordate to sagittate | apex acuminate

fruit_description: utricle 8--13 mm long | tube 16--22 mm long | lobes erect, remaining joined together at apices, semi-circular, 10--12 mm long, yellow inside | apex filiform | 5--7 mm long | Fruit elongate-ovoid, 4--5.5 cm long, c. 2.5 cm diam
seed_description: Seed not seen
ecology_description: Recorded as a host of the larvae of the Cairns Birdwing Butterfly, Troides euphorion.
habitat_description: An understorey vine in rainforest.
distribution_description: Known only from near Mount Lewis, north Queensland, at 1100--1300 m.

flowering_time_description: Flowers January-February; fruits February-October, probably in response to rain
fruiting_time_description: Flowers January-February; fruits February-October, probably in response to rain
fruiting_cues_description: fruits February-October, probably in response to rain
habit_description: Slender twining vine, dying back to perennial rootstock
stem_description: stems to 1 m long, sparsely to moderately pubescent or rarely glabrous

inflorescence_description: pedicels 0.2--0.3 cm long

phenology_text: Flowers January-February; fruits February-October, probably in response to rain.
ecology_description: Recorded as a host for the larvae of the Redbodied Swallowtail, Atrophaneura polydorus queenslandicus, and the Big Greasy, Cressida cressida cressida.
habitat_description: Grows in vine forest or open forest.
distribution_description: Occurs from near Gove, northern Northern Territory, through Cape York Peninsula extending south to Rockhampton, Queensland.

stem_description: Primary stems to 50 cm long | branches divaricate to erect
leaf_description: Leaves of branches | lamina divergent to divaricate, 3--15 mm long, pungent, medium to deep green | margins scabrid | nerves 3--5 | rounded, grooves open, glabrous to scabrid | auricles not or shortly produced | scarious sheath margins remaining entire, lamina of primary-stem leaves 15--45 mm long

seed_description: Seed 3 mm diam., slightly rugose
habitat_description: Grows in sand and sandy clay, sometimes with granite or laterite, in depressions and along watercourses, in shrubland and woodland.
distribution_description: Widespread in south-western W.A. from Yuna to Pinjarra, extending inland to Wilroy and Tammin.
notes: The most widespread and variable of the taxa formerly included in Acanthocarpus preissii , this may be recognised by the darker green leaves with 3--5 nerves and open grooves, by the larger flowers and by the capsules that have short, flattened tubercles. In one collection from Tammin (R.D.Royce 9378 , PERTH), the fruit is smooth.

stem_description: Stems to 20 cm long, simple or sparsely branched

inflorescence_description: pedicels 3--5 mm long
flower_description: Flowers terminal | Sepals and petals 6--7 mm long, white with brown midrib | Stamens 5 mm long | Pistil 6 mm long, slender
fruit_description: Capsule 4--5 mm long, verrucose | tubercles rounded, to c. 0.3 mm long
seed_description: Seed 4 mm long, finely reticulate
habitat_description: Grows in loamy sand over limestone in Triodia steppe.
distribution_description: Restricted to an area from Point Cloates to the Lyndon R., S of Exmouth Gulf, W.A.
notes: Recognised by the small habit, 5--9-nerved leaves, large flowers and short rounded tubercles of the fruit.

stem_description: Stems to 40 cm long | branches divaricate
leaf_description: Leaves of branches, crowded | lamina divaricate, 3--10 mm long, pungent, dark green | margins finely scabrid | nerves 5 decreasing to 3 below apex | rounded, grooves open, smooth or slightly scabrid | auricles narrowly triangular, less than 1 mm long, entire or slightly lacerated | primary-stem leaves not seen

fruit_description: Capsule 4--5 mm long, verrucose | tubercles obtuse, to 0.3 mm long
seed_description: Seed ellipsoidal, 3.5--4 mm long, finely reticulate
habitat_description: Grows in sand among sandstone rocks.
distribution_description: Known only from the lower Murchison River, south-western W.A.
notes: Distinguished especially by the small crowded leaves with few open grooves and by the small flowers.

stem_description: Stems to 70 cm long, sometimes longer | branches ascending or divaricate
leaf_description: Leaves of branches | lamina spreading, 1--3 cm long, pungent, grey-green, sometimes dark green | margins smooth or finely scabrid | veins 7--12 | flattened, grooves narrow, scabrid | auricles not or shortly produced | scarious sheath margins lacerating, lamina of primary-stem leaves usually 2--7 cm long
inflorescence_description: pedicels 1 mm long
flower_description: Flowers terminal | Sepals and petals 3--4 mm long, white with fine purple-brown midrib | Stamens c. 1.5 mm long | Pistil 1.5 mm long, thick

seed_description: Seed 4--5 mm diam., slightly rugose
habitat_description: Usually grows on coastal dunes, sometimes in limestone or sandstone, in shrubland.
distribution_description: Widespread and often locally common in coastal areas from Quobba, N of Carnarvon, to Cape Leeuwin, W.A.
notes: Recognised by the usually grey-green leaves with 7--12 veins and very narrow grooves, by the size of the flowers and by the capsules with long, uncinate tubercles.

stem_description: Stems to 70 cm long | branches erect to spreading
leaf_description: Leaves of branches | lamina divergent, 10--30 mm long, pungent, yellowish green | margins scabrid | nerves 9--13 | slightly rounded, grooves closed, scabrid | auricles triangular, 4--6 mm long, becoming lacerated | lamina of primary-stem leaves 30--50 mm long

seed_description: Seed 4--5 mm long, irregularly reticulate
habitat_description: Grows in sand in Triodia steppe and low heath.
distribution_description: Occurs in coastal and adjacent areas from North West Cape to Shark Bay.
notes: May be recognised by the robust habit, medium-sized flowers with small stamens, and large fruit. Foliage dries yellow-green. Collections resembling this species, but with smaller leaves and fruit, from farther south (e.g. Ajana, C.A.Gardner 8596 , PERTH) may represent another, unnamed species.

stem_description: Stems to 50 cm long | branches divaricate
leaf_description: Leaves of branches | lamina divaricate, 7--25 mm long, slender, pungent, dark green | margins finely scabrid | nerves 5 | flattened, grooves almost closed, scabrid | auricles triangular to ovate, 1 mm long, lacerating | primary-stem leaves not seen
inflorescence_description: pedicels 1--1.5 mm long

fruit_description: Capsule 4--4.5 mm long, verrucose | tubercles irregularly conical, obtuse, to 0.4 mm long
seed_description: Seed 2.5 mm diam., somewhat rugose
habitat_description: Grows in red sand with limestone, in Triodia -shrub steppe, sometimes by creek-lines.
distribution_description: Endemic in the Cape Range, S of North West Cape, W.A.
notes: A small-flowered species, characterised also by the slender leaves and shortly verrucose fruit. The foliage dries pale green.

stem_description: Stems to 50 cm long, rarely longer | branches divaricate
leaf_description: Leaves of branches | lamina ascending to spreading, 10--70 mm long, acuminate, slightly bluish green | margins finely scabrous | nerves 6--8 | rounded, grooves narrow, finely scabrid | auricles narrowly triangular, acute or obtuse, 3--5 mm long, becoming lacerated | lamina of primary-stem leaves usually 30--80 mm long

seed_description: Seed 4 mm long, reticulate
habitat_description: Grows in sandy loam, clay-loam and limestone soils, in Triodia -shrub steppe.
distribution_description: Occurs near the coast from North West Cape to Shark Bay, and on Barrow and the Monte Bello Is., W.A.
notes: A robust plant, recognised by the verticillate inflorescence and large flowers.

habit_description: Plant large, succulent, freely suckering
leaf_description: Leaves lanceolate, straight or reflexed (often at apex), 100--200 cm long, 15--25 cm wide, light grey-glaucous to light green | margin undulate | straight or crenate, toothed | teeth 5--10 mm long | 2--6 cm apart, brown to pruinose-grey, terminal spine conical to subulate, 3--5 cm long, shiny brown to pruinose-grey
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 5--9 m high | scape with triangular bracts | panicles with 15--35 umbellate branches in upper ½-⅓ of scape

fruit_description: Capsule oblong, 4--6 cm long, 2--2.5 cm diam., shortly beaked
seed_description: Seeds 7--8.5 mm long, 5--7 mm wide, shiny black
vegetative_reproduction_description: Often propagating itself by suckers (Green 1994)
ecology_description: Often propagating itself by suckers (Green 1994).
distribution_description: Native of Mexico. A garden escape in mainly eastern and southern Australia. Naturalised in all States and Territories, also Norfolk and Lord Howe Islands.
notes: For treatment of Agave americana on Lord Howe Island see Green (1994: 523--524). Occasional garden escape. The sap is a skin irritant and can cause dermatitis (Shepherd 2004, Richardson et al. 2016). Hazardous spines on leaves.

habit_description: Plants medium to large, freely suckering
leaf_description: Leaves linear to lanceolate, 90--130 cm long, 9--12 cm wide, green | margin toothless on mature leaves and with minute teeth on young leaves | or sometimes with antrorsely hooked teeth 2.5--3 mm long, 6--24 mm apart, shiny brown to blackish, terminal spine subulate, 2--2.5 cm long, dark brown

distribution_description: Native to Mexico, Central America. Naturalised mainly in coastal districts and offshore islands of eastern Queensland (occurs in or near abandoned experimental sisal fibre plantations in central Queensland and as a garden escape elsewhere), and locally naturalised on Rottnest Island west of Perth, Western Australia; also reported from Bournda National Park in southeastern New South Wales. (Queensland Government 2016).
notes: For weed properties see Navie & Adkins (2008) and Queensland Government (2016).

common_name: Caribbean Agave, Garden Sisal, Century Plant.
habit_description: Plants large, freely suckering
leaf_description: Leaves linear to lanceolate, 60--120 cm long, 3.5--10 cm wide (leaf size can vary with age and size of the plant with smaller plants having shorter and narrower leaves than more mature plants), light green to glaucous-grey (with whitish or yellowish margins in a variegated cultivar), fleshy | margin toothed | the teeth 10--20 (-30) mm apart | 2--5 mm long, curved, reddish brown, terminal spine conical to subulate, 1.5--3.5 cm long, dark brown to dark purplish brown
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 3--5 m high | scape with narrowly triangular bracts | panicle with 10--20 umbellate branches in upper ⅓ of scape
flower_description: Flowers 5--6.5 cm long, shortly pedicellate, greenish yellow | Perianth tube 8--16 mm long, funnel-shaped to slightly urceolate | sepals and petals unequal, 18--24 mm long, obtuse, cucullate at apex | Filaments 35--45 mm long | anthers 20--30 mm long | Ovary 20--30 mm long
fruit_description: Capsule broadly ovoid, c. 5 cm long, raggedly beaked
seed_description: Seeds 9--12 mm long, 7--8 mm wide, dull black
vegetative_reproduction_description: Localised, spreading via rhizomes
ecology_description: Localised, spreading via rhizomes. Probably distributed partly by the dumping of garden refuse. An invasive environmental weed in SE Queensland (see Queensland Government 2016).
habitat_description: A weed of roadsides, railway lines, embankments, cliffsides, disturbed sites and waste areas, usually near settlement; also grows in open woodlands, disturbed open eucalypt forest, in coastal environs (e.g. sand dunes, beach scrub, sea cliffs, offshore islands), on creekbanks and in vegetation along watercourses.
distribution_description: Native to Mexico. A garden escape in coastal eastern Queensland; also locally naturalised in the Perth area, southwestern Western Australia, and in northeastern (near Yamba) and central near-coastal New South Wales.
notes: The taxon naturalised in Western Australia and Queensland is currently treated as Agave angustifolia Haw. (Agave angustifiolia in Florabase, accessed June 2023; Forster 2022: 10), indicating that the status of A. angustifolia as a synonym of A. vivipara requires re-assessment in the Australian Plant Census. The cultivar Agave 'Marginata' is sparingly naturalised in Australia, at least in SE Queensland and in New South Wales. For weed properties, illustrations, etc. see Queensland Government (2016) where treated as Agave angustifolia Haw.

habit_description: See Agave vivipara
notes: Since publication of the Flora of Australia Volume 46 (1986) the Australian Plant Census recognises var. vivipara for Australia.

common_name: Pregnant Onion, Pregnant Sea Onion, False Sea Onion.

inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a large erect cylindrical raceme to 120 cm long | bracts lanceolate, much longer than flowers, lower fruiting pedicels 5--15 mm long, upper pedicels shorter

fruit_description: Capsule ovoid to obovoid, 3-angled
vegetative_reproduction_description: Plants spread rapidly via asexually produced bulbils, producing dense colonies of thousands of plants
ecology_description: Plants spread rapidly via asexually produced bulbils, producing dense colonies of thousands of plants.
distribution_description: Native to southern Africa, commonly cultivated in Australia; naturalised in W.A., N.S.W. and Vic.; possible adventive plants recorded in S.A. In New South Wales a common garden escape in the Brogo River Reserve and Nowra district (Godden 1993). In Victoria, populations have established from nearby gardens around Bacchus Marsh, Black Rock and Prahran (Messina 2014).

common_name: Natal Lily, Candelabrum Lily, Nelson's Slime Lily.
biostatus: Introduced. Doubtfully naturalised (Australian Plant Census, CHAH 2021, accessed 12 March 2026).

The rainfall in this area is high, averaging 1369 mm per year at Walpole.

Variegatum (C. variegatum Hort.), the form with yellow- or white-striped leaves, is apparently more common in cultivation than the green-leaved form. Plants are characterised by the leafy tufts, equivalent to adventitious plantlets, that develop distally in the inflorescence which then bends down under their weight, and the plantlets take root. In South Africa, not all plants of this species produce such plantlets (A.A.Obermeyer, Bothalia 7: 700 (1962)).

(= Xerotes banksii f. neocaledonica Guillaumin), e.g. by N.Hallé, Adansonia ser. 2, 20: 21--28 (1980). There are certain vegetative differences but the supposed floral distinction does not hold. P.F.Stevens, J. Arnold Arbor. 59: 150--152 (1978), described the New Guinean plant in detail. This species shares with Lomandra ordii the ability, when well developed, to attain shrub or small tree stature by means of a long woody stem. The disarticulation of leaf blades is unique to L. banksii . From the related L. multiflora and L. patens it differs further in flower colour, but shares with L. patens a well developed pistillode c. 1.5 mm long in male flowers.

leaf_description: Leaves flat or nearly so, coriaceous or firm, usually 15--30 cm long, 2.5--3 mm wide, smooth or scabrid | apex usually entire

habitat_description: Appears to be more common in soils from shale or igneous rocks than in sands.
distribution_description: Occurs in the southern part of the species range, i.e. widespread in Vic. and in south-eastern N.S.W., chiefly in coast and tableland districts, intergrading with subsp. filiformis at their junction and appearing erratically in northern N.S.W. and rarely in Qld; gradually replaced by subsp. flavior to the west.

stem_description: branches irregularly alternate or occasionally some whorled | axes quite smooth, or slightly papillose especially distally
leaf_description: Leaves very fine, channelled, folded, inrolled or rarely flat, usually flexible, usually less than 10 cm to more than 30 cm long, 0.5--3 mm wide, occasionally to 5 mm, smooth or rarely scaberulous, especially on margins | apex minutely 1--3-pointed
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence sometimes only 2--5 cm long and unbranched, but mostly with a few short branches c. 10--20 cm long, to well-branched and over 30 cm long, usually slightly less than half to as long as leaves | scape similar to rachis in length, usually whitish | Female inflorescence similar but slightly smaller | Bracts all small
distribution_description: Occupies the northern part of the species range, especially in coastal and tableland districts, intergrading erratically with subsp. flavior to the west, and with subsp. coriacea to the south, extending from northern Qld to central N.S.W.; occasionally also in southern N.S.W. and Vic.

stem_description: axes smooth to scabrid, often yellowish
leaf_description: Leaves rolled or flat, usually very tough, 30--40 cm long, c. 2 mm wide, smooth to scabrid | apex minutely 1--3-pointed
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence c. 3--7 cm long, 1/4--1/3 as long as leaves, well branched, branching obscure or branches irregularly whorled | scape shorter than rachis, sometimes partly hidden by leaf bases | Female inflorescence more condensed, as little as one-seventh as long as leaves | Bracts subtending branches large, white or whitish, smaller at upper nodes
distribution_description: Occurs on the western slopes of the Great Dividing Ra. in N.S.W., essentially in the inland part of the species range.
notes: Specimens from the southern part of the range tend to have scabrid inflorescence axes, and although now within the circumscription of subsp. flavior (see A.T.Lee, Contr. New South Wales Natl Herb. 3: 152 (1962)), they thus show a similarity to subsp. coriacea , a similarity also evident in the leaf forms of some southern subsp. flavior .

habit_description: Plant tufted
leaf_description: Leaves concavo-convex or channelled, 25--75 cm long, 0.5--2.5 mm wide | apex 2- or 3-toothed | lateral teeth usually longest | sheath margins lacerated, dark reddish brown
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence ⅓ to nearly as long as leaves, branched | scape usually 2--3 times as long as rachis, flattened | Female inflorescence often unbranched | the scape longer in relation to rachis, otherwise similar to male inflorescence | bract and inner bract golden brown
flower_description: flower clusters whorled | Flowers as in Lomandra longifolia
habitat_description: Grows typically in creek beds.
distribution_description: Occurs in a restricted area of central coastal N.S.W.
notes: Suspected hybrids between this species and Lomandra longifolia have been found near Sydney.

habit_description: Plant caespitose, or stems shortly decumbent in small dense mats
leaf_description: Leaves flat or slightly concave, erect to spreading, often crowded towards the stem apex, usually 8--20 cm long, 1--1.5 mm wide, glaucous | apex shortly acute to rounded-truncate | sheath margins (at least of sterile shoots) abruptly narrowed at the top, readily lacerated, lattice-like, white or pale brown
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence at least n of leaf length, usually 10 cm long, occasionally up to 15 cm | scape usually not exposed above leaf bases, rarely exposed up to 2.5 cm | rachis branched or unbranched, the lowest node often with 2 or 3 whorled branches | Female inflorescence to 1.5 cm diam. | scape concealed or exposed for up to 2.5 cm | Bracts and flowers as in Lomandra obliqua
habitat_description: Usually grows on sandy soils, from deep coastal sandy heaths to open forests on sandstones.
distribution_description: Occurs in coastal and tableland areas of N.S.W., from N of Newcastle S to Braidwood; common in the Sydney area.
notes: Lomandra glauca is distinguished from its closest relatives by its leaf-length and relative leaf and inflorescence lengths, its readily lacerating and lattice-like sheath margins abruptly narrowed at the top, its shortly acute leaf apex, and its male scape usually not exposed above leaf bases. It appears to be replaced northwards by L. elongata (with some intergradation) and by L. obliqua (maintaining distinctness). The taxa L. collina and L. nana , earlier treated as subsp. collina and subsp. nana of L. glauca , are probably more distant morphologically than the northern relatives and are probably never sympatric with L. glauca , but all are part of a complex bordering the continent, with L. tropica providing a northern complement.

habit_description: Tussocks sparse
leaf_description: Leaves channelled to almost semiterete with narrow marginal bands and coarse venation, usually c. 40 cm long, 1--2 mm wide, glabrous | apex acute | sheath margins lacerated, dark purplish brown
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence with several irregularly alternate branches (sometimes a few whorled) | Male inflorescence often nearly as long as leaves | Female inflorescence smaller | Bracts as in Lomandra cylindrica, but inner bract absent | pedicel 3--5 mm long
flower_description: flowers separate, well-spaced | Male flowers usually 2.5--3 mm long, to 4 mm diam., yellow | sepals thinner and shorter than the fleshy petals | Female flowers on pedicel 1--2 mm long
habitat_description: Often grows in rocky situations with sandy soils in dry sclerophyll forest.
distribution_description: Occurs in the Blue Mountains and central coast areas of N.S.W. and in southern Qld.

habit_description: Tussock robust
leaf_description: Leaves flat, 30--60 cm long, 4--5 mm wide | apex entire or minutely 2- or 3-toothed | sheath margins somewhat lacerated, pale to bright brown
inflorescence_description: Inflorescences about as long as leaves | pedicel of male flowers 1.5--2 mm long
flower_description: flower clusters or individual flowers distichous | Sepals and petals purple-black
fruit_description: Capsule slightly wrinkled
seed_description: Seeds orange
habitat_description: Grows in sandy soil.
distribution_description: Occurs in south-western W.A., in near-coastal areas between Kalbarri and Israelite Bay.

habit_description: Tussocks sparse
leaf_description: Leaves flat, 15--45 cm long, 1--2 mm wide, glabrous, old leaves loosely coiled and purplish to reddish-brown | apex apiculate or truncate | sheath margins lacerated, white to straw-coloured
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence c. 3--8 cm long, branched | scape equal to rachis or shorter, often largely hidden | Female inflorescence similar but smaller | Bracts shorter to slightly longer than pedicels, acute to acuminate | inner bract present
flower_description: flowers separate or 2 or 3 together | Male flowers globular or ovoid, 2--4 mm long, pedicellate | sepals and petals incurved, tapering | sepals shorter, thinner, purple | petals fleshy, yellowish | Female flowers similar, ovoid, 4--6 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in laterite in eucalypt forest or sand in eucalypt or banksia woodland or in heath, but not close to the coast where the similar species Lomandra maritima is found.
distribution_description: Occurs in south-western W.A. from near Jurien to Denmark.
notes: Despite the epithet this species is usually dioecious, although occasional flowers have a large pistillode or are possibly hermaphrodite.

habit_description: Plant robust, tufted
leaf_description: Leaves flat, rather thin, usually 90--130 cm long, 5--10.5 mm wide, glabrous | apex acute with 2--4 often minute lateral teeth usually well below apex | rarely the laterals longest | sheath margins intact, white or occasionally brown to reddish-brown
inflorescence_description: scape half to twice as long as rachis, flattened | Bract | inner bract and flowers as in Lomandra longifolia
flower_description: flower clusters whorled
habitat_description: Grows near streams.
distribution_description: Occurs in two apparently widely disjunct areas of eastern Australia east of the Great Divide: in northern Qld from S of Cooktown to Townsville, and in the south from Nambour in Qld to N of Taree in N.S.W.
notes: This species is closely related to Lomandra longifolia but differs in leaf apex form, in lacking conspicuous marginal sclerenchyma bands on leaves, and in inflorescence branching characteristics. In northern Qld on mountains such as Thornton Peak there occur plants similar to L. hystrix but differing in inflorescence dimensions, appearance of male flowers, and occurrence at high rather than low altitude.

habit_description: Tussocks narrow
leaf_description: Leaves glabrous, dimorphic, sometimes on the one plant, erect, channelled to semiterete, long and narrow (20 cm long, c. 1 mm wide), or erect or spreading, usually flat, short and broad (c. 7--15 cm long, 3 mm wide) | apex rounded | sheath margins intact, white to light brown
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence | bracts and flowers as in Lomandra nigricans
habitat_description: Grows on lateritic soils in Jarrah (Eucalyptus marginata ) forest and sandy clay soils in Karri (E. diversicolor ) forest.
distribution_description: Occurs in south-western W.A., from near Perth to Albany.
notes: See note under Lomandra nigricans regarding past taxonomic confusion of this species.

habit_description: Tussock robust
leaf_description: Leaves terete, rigid, 20--50 cm long, 1--1.5 mm diam. | apex pungent | sheath margins absent
inflorescence_description: Inflorescences much shorter than the leaves, usually interrupted, the male with 3--7 spherical segments, the female with l or 2 | pedicels of male and female flowers embedded among hairs of modified bracts
flower_description: Perianth 5 mm long | Sepals white | Petals yellowish | Stamens of outer whorl inserted on rim of perianth tube, inner whorl on lobes
habitat_description: Grows in sandy soils.
distribution_description: Occurs in the mallee and the Big and Little Deserts of western Vic., and the Eyre Peninsula and dry south-eastern region of S.A.

habit_description: Tussocks sparse
stem_description: stems short with leaves c. 40 cm long, or stems extended and decumbent with leaves c. 20 cm long
leaf_description: Leaves flat, rather thin, 2--4 mm wide, bluish-grey when dry | apex rounded-acute or rounded-truncate | sheath margins intact, whitish, or slightly lacerated in age and brownish
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence often nearly as long as leaves with well-spaced, separate flowers on fine axes | scape approximately equalling rachis | Male inflorescence with opposite or whorled branches | Female inflorescence similar, less well developed | Bracts as in Lomandra cylindrica | pedicel spreading to recurved, c. 2 mm long | pedicel 0.5 mm long
flower_description: Male flowers c. 2--2.5 mm long | Female flowers 4--6 mm long | Sepals and petals as in L. cylindrica but thin, creamy-white
habitat_description: Commonly found in marginal rainforest habitats, also in sandy soils over sandstone and in deep sands.
distribution_description: Occurs in eastern Australia, from coastal and subcoastal Qld to northern coastal N.S.W.
notes: The autumn to winter flowering, together with regularly whorled and very fine inflorescence axes, thin flat leaves, usually thinner texture of the perianth and short pedicels are features that distinguish Lomandra laxa , especially from some of the large northern forms of L. filiformis .

habit_description: Tussock small to robust
leaf_description: Leaves flat, rigid, coarsely veined, 20--60 cm long, c. 1--2.5 mm wide | apex acute to rounded | sheath margins white or orange-brown
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence shorter than leaves, entire or in segments | pedicels embedded among hairs of modified bracts, male 1--3 mm long, female 1 mm long
flower_description: Perianth to 7 mm long, cream-coloured | Stamens inserted at top of perianth tube
distribution_description: Occurs in all States except Tas., with two subspecies, one occupying a small north-eastern part of the range, and the other a larger south-western part.

habit_description: Plant slender, often less than 40 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves c. 1--2 mm wide | sheath margins long-decurrent, white, readily lacerating into abundant, loose, silky or woolly fragments
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence usually with 1 or 2 segments | female inflorescence usually not segmented, spherical | scape minutely hirsute
habitat_description: Grows in open eucalypt forest on rocky slopes and sandy soils.
distribution_description: Occurs in dry coastal areas and ranges in Qld from near Rockhampton southwards, and in northern and central N.S.W. chiefly on the inland slopes of the Great Divide.

habit_description: Plant generally robust, often 40--60 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves c. 1.5--5 mm wide | sheath margins short, yellowish to orange-brown, the fragments few, woolly or fibrous
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence usually with more than 3 segments | female inflorescence segmented or often entire, cylindrical | scape glabrous
habitat_description: Grows on upper slopes and crests of sand dunes, including red sands of central Australia; often under mallee.
distribution_description: Occurs in central Australia, and adjacent regions of W.A., N.T., Qld, N.S.W., Vic., S.A.

habit_description: Plant tufted
leaf_description: Leaves flat or slightly concavo-convex, occasionally rolled, usually 50--100 cm long and 4.5--7.5 mm wide, glabrous | apex 2- or 3-toothed | central tooth in pronounced sinus or longer than laterals | sheath margins intact or coarsely split, brown, orange-brown or reddish brown, occasionally white
inflorescence_description: scape distinct, much shorter to much longer than rachis, flattened | bract and inner bract shorter than flower, truncate, whitish
flower_description: flower clusters whorled | Flowers ellipsoidal or cylindrical, sessile | male flowers 3--3.5 mm long | females c. 4.5 mm long | Sepals shiny, scarious, purplish or yellow | Petals dull, fleshy, yellow or cream
habitat_description: Grows in a variety of habitats.
distribution_description: Occurs in eastern parts of eastern Australia, from Lizard Is. in N Qld to the Mt Gambier and Millicent area of S.A., and eastern and northern Tas.
notes: A very variable species which, in parts of N.S.W. and southern Qld, is not clearly distinct from Lomandra confertifolia subsp. pallida . Other taxa closely related and in some cases difficult to distinguish from L. longifolia include L. hystrix , L. fluviatilis , L. spicata and L. montana .

habit_description: Tussocks dense
leaf_description: Leaves flat or channelled, 30--60 cm long, 1--2 mm wide, glabrous, old leaves coiled and straw-coloured | apex obtuse | sheath margins lacerated, pale brown to purple
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence largely concealed among leaf bases, c. 4--5 cm long, branched | scape shorter than rachis, hidden | Female inflorescence similar, smaller, almost completely hidden | Bracts tapering, shorter to slightly longer than pedicel | inner bract present
flower_description: flowers separate or 2 or 3 together | Male flowers globular or ovoid, 3.5--6 mm long, pedicellate | sepals and petals incurved | sepals shorter, thinner than petals, purple | petals fleshy, yellow | Female flowers similar, ovoid, 5--8 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in sandy soils often over limestone.
distribution_description: Occurs close to the coast of south-western W.A. from N of Geraldton to Bunbury.
notes: Closely related to Lomandra hermaphrodita, from which it differs in the colour of old leaves, colour of leaf sheath margins, to some extent in the inflorescence branching and in the flowering period. Its distribution is adjacent but apparently not overlapping.

habit_description: Plant tufted
leaf_description: Leaves 20--70 cm long | apex broadly acute or obtuse | sheath margins dark or light brown
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence with scape hidden by leaf bases or exserted | Male inflorescence branched | Female inflorescence branched or unbranched | Bracts broadly acuminate, 1--3 mm long | inner bract evident or not
flower_description: flowers separate or 2 together | Flowers pedicellate, greenish yellow to dark red, usually with pale margins | males 1.5--3 mm long | females 3--5.5 mm long | Sepals and petals similar, spreading or reflexed at anthesis
distribution_description: Occurs in southern W.A., southern S.A., Vic. and south-eastern N.S.W.

leaf_description: Leaves usually flexuose, plano-convex, flat and inrolled, 0.4--2.5 mm wide, or almost terete and less than 0.6 mm wide | sheath margins usually lacerated but some remaining intact
inflorescence_description: Inflorescences 1/3--1/2 as long as leaves, male 7--25 cm long, female 3--12 cm long | scape usually hidden | axis smooth or scaberulous with fine blisters
distribution_description: Widespread in southern Australia, in south-western W.A. south of Geraldton, in much of southern S.A. and in Vic.

leaf_description: Leaves rigid although sinuate, terete, 0.9--3.5 mm diam. | sheath margins usually lacerated but some remaining intact
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 1/3--1/2 as long as leaves, male 6--15 cm long, female 5--10 cm long | scape usually hidden | axis scaberulous with fine dense blisters
habitat_description: Grows on sand in low heath and open mallee.
distribution_description: Occurs in south-western W.A., from Dalwallinu to Ongerup and Lake King eastward, and in western Vic.

leaf_description: Leaves flexuose, or stiff and erect, plano-convex or flat and inrolled or folded, 0.8--2.5 mm wide (flat and up to 5 mm wide in montane areas) | sheath margins usually intact, occasionally slightly lacerated
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence 1/3--1/2 as long as leaves | the scape hidden or, in the more easterly populations 1/2--3/4 as long as leaves and the scape exposed, male 10--27 cm long, female 7--18 cm long | axis strongly tuberculate
phenology_text: Flowers autumn and winter (spring in montane areas).
distribution_description: Occurs in coastal and tableland areas of N.S.W. south of Gosford, in Vic. mainly in the Victorian Highlands and Grampians, and in S.A. mainly in the south-east.

habit_description: Plant tufted
leaf_description: Leaves flat or rolled when dried, rather thin, usually 35--50 cm long, 2--4 mm wide | apex toothed | central one often much exceeding laterals | sheath margins lacerated, brown
inflorescence_description: scape much longer than rachis, flattened | bract and inner bract brown
flower_description: flower clusters whorled | Flowers as in Lomandra longifolia
habitat_description: Grows usually near creeks and waterfalls.
distribution_description: Occurs in a restricted area of N.S.W. in the Blue Mountains.
notes: The above nomenclatural combinations made by Bailey and by Fraser & Vickery, and the description by the latter authors, were intended to apply to Lomandra spicata , a species then undescribed but erroneously known as Lomandra (or Xerotes ) montana , fide A.T.Lee, Contr. New South Wales Natl Herb. 3: 159 (1962).

stem_diameter_description: stems forming dense mats up to 30 cm diam
habit_description: Plant with extending leafy stems forming dense mats up to 30 cm diam
leaf_description: Leaves concavo-convex to semiterete, not or scarcely twisted or recurved, usually 2.5--3.5 cm long, 1--2 mm wide, glaucous | apex acuminate | almost pungent | sheath margins abruptly narrowed at top, intact, white to golden brown, developing a reddish line along junction with leaf base
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence subsessile, equalling leaves, or rarely scape exposed above leaf bases for c. 5 mm | rachis branched or unbranched, 1--2.5 cm long, usually shorter than leaves | Female inflorescence 5--7 mm diam. | scape not exposed | Bracts and flowers as in Lomandra obliqua
habitat_description: Grows mostly in sandy or lateritic soils in low or tall shrubland or mallee.
distribution_description: Occurs in south-western W.A., from York to Cape Arid.

habit_description: Tuft slender to robust
leaf_description: Leaf apex entire | sheath margins entire or with little laceration, white, purplish or brown
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence usually 1/4--3/4 as long as leaves, branched or rarely unbranched | scape shorter than rachis, not flattened | Female inflorescence similar, unbranched | bract and inner bract brown or purplish | pedicel absent or up to 12 mm long
flower_description: flower clusters whorled | Male flowers campanulate, usually 2--3 mm long | Female flowers larger, sessile | Sepals and petals similar except petals thicker | sepals purplish | petals yellow
distribution_description: Occurs in tropical N.T. and Qld to south-eastern Australia; also in southern New Guinea.

leaf_description: Leaves flat or slightly concavo-convex, 25--65 cm long, 2--4.5 mm wide, smooth, usually greyish green
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence once-branched
flower_description: flowers sessile or on pedicels rarely up to 2 mm long, usually concealed by bracts
habitat_description: Grows in loamy or sandy soils in woodland or shrubland.
distribution_description: Occurs in the southern Flinders and Mt Lofty Ranges and the Yorke and Fleurieu Peninsulas, S.A.
notes: Recorded for N.S.W. by A.T. Lee, Contr. New South Wales Natl Herb., Fl. Ser. 34: 38 (1966), but N.S.W. specimens attributed to this taxon are now considered to be Lomandra multiflora subsp. multiflora.

pedicel_length_description: pedicels rarely up to 2 mm long

leaf_description: Leaves flat or slightly concavo-convex, occasionally plano-convex, rarely terete, 25--90 cm long, usually 1.5--3 mm wide, smooth, or scabrid underneath, green, greyish green or rarely glaucous
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence once- or twice-branched or rarely unbranched
flower_description: flowers on pedicels usually 3--8 mm long, always distinctly exceeding bracts at anthesis
habitat_description: Grows in a variety of soils, chiefly in woodland and forest.
distribution_description: Occurs in Arnhem Land, N.T., throughout eastern Qld, slopes, tablelands and coastal areas of N.S.W., and eastern and southern Vic. almost to the border of S.A. Earlier records from W.A. were erroneous. Not yet found in S.A. and perhaps not occurring there.

habit_description: Tussock 5--10 cm diam
leaf_description: Leaves usually flat, erect or often curved to one side, c. 5--15 cm long, 0.8--1.5 mm wide, blue-green, scarcely glaucous | apex obtuse or truncate | occasionally shortly acute or with a minute central point | sheath margins gradually narrowed at top, rather tardily and coarsely lacerated, white when young, often dark brown when old
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence usually shorter than leaves and unbranched | scape usually shortly exposed above leaf bases | Female inflorescence subsessile | Bracts and flowers as in Lomandra obliqua
habitat_description: Grows in sandy and rocky soils in eucalypt woodland.
distribution_description: Occurs in SE Australia, in Tas., western Vic. and south-eastern S.A.
notes: Sterile shoots, in which leaf sheath margins are most visible, are rarely seen in Lomandra nana ; the character as described is common in fertile shoots of this species complex.

habit_description: Tussocks narrow
leaf_description: Leaves channelled to semiterete, 25--70 cm long, 1--3 mm wide, glabrous | apex rounded | sheath margins at first intact and white or nearly transparent, later finely lacerated and dark brown to purplish black
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence branched or unbranched, at least half the leaf length | scape equalling or longer than rachis | Female inflorescence similar but often unbranched | Bracts broad, acute, shorter than pedicel | inner bract sometimes absent | pedicel 2--7.5 mm long | pedicel absent or up to 0.8 mm long
flower_description: flower clusters in distant whorls, the whorls of branches and flowers at least 2 cm apart | Male flowers c. 2.5--4 mm long | sepals and petals nearly equal, white with purple markings | petals slightly thicker | Female flowers similar
habitat_description: Grows in eucalypt forest on laterite, eucalypt or banksia woodland on sand and in shrubland on black peaty (sometimes swampy) or lateritic sands.
distribution_description: Occurs in south-western W.A., from Gingin south to Albany and east along the south coast to Israelite Bay.
notes: Until recently this species was confused with Lomandra odora and L. integra , the composite taxon being known by the illegitimate name L. endlicheri . All three species have strongly scented flowers.

habit_description: Tussocks compact
stem_description: branches predominantly opposite or whorled | axes smooth or papillose
leaf_description: Leaves semiterete or channelled, 9--30 cm long, 0.5--1 mm wide, somewhat discolorous and papillose-puberulent | apex acute or truncated | sheath margins lacerated, white
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence with partially to fully recurved scapes | the rachis and flowers thus more or less pendent | Male inflorescence 1/3--1/2 as long as leaves | Female inflorescence smaller | Bracts acuminate, shorter than or equalling pedicels | inner bract regularly present | pedicel rather stout, straight, manifestly articulate near flower | pedicel 1--2 mm long | pedicel 1 mm long
flower_description: flowers separate | Flowers greenish-cream and partly red, with a deep receptacle | Male flowers depressed-globular, 2--3 mm long | sepals and petals incurved | Female flowers ellipsoidal, 3--4 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in well-drained situations in various sandy or loamy soils, usually in open places between mallee trees and shrubs but also in eucalypt woodland in the north of the range.
distribution_description: Occurs in south-western W.A.; known from the plain S and E of the Stirling Range, from Narrogin and from W of York.
notes: Unique in having a recurved inflorescence.

habit_description: Plant decumbent to scrambling
leaf_description: Leaves nearly flat, spreading or recurved, commonly twisted, 2--4 cm long, rarely to 15 cm, 1--2 mm wide, green or glaucous | apex long-acute | almost pungent | sheath margins auriculate at top at least when young, intact, white
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence | scape short or hidden among leaf bases | rachis c. 2--10 cm long, shorter to longer than leaves, usually with a few branches | Female inflorescence c. 5--8 mm diam. | scape absent or up to c. 3 cm long
flower_description: Flowers yellow, flushed with purple
habitat_description: Grows in eucalypt woodland and forest on sandy soils, often shallow, or on rocky slopes.
distribution_description: Occurs in eastern Australia from the Blackdown Tableland, Qld, through the coast and tableland areas of N.S.W. as far south as Jervis Bay.

habit_description: Tussocks small
leaf_description: Leaves channelled to semiterete, 20--54 cm long, 0.5--1.2 mm wide, glabrous | apex rounded | sheath margins finely lacerated, white to pale grey
inflorescence_description: Male inflorescence usually unbranched, less than half the leaf length, clearly scapose | Female inflorescence similar, sometimes with a very short rachis on a long scape | Bracts as in Lomandra nigricans
flower_description: flowers in close whorled clusters, the whorls commonly less than 1 cm apart | Flowers yellowish-green, sometimes purple-flushed | males pedicellate | females sessile, otherwise as in L. nigricans
habitat_description: Grows in sandy soils of banksia and Tuart (Eucalyptus gomphocephala ) woodland, or marginal to swamps, on the coastal plain, and in Jarrah (Eucalyptus marginata ) forest on the Darling Range.
distribution_description: Occurs in south-western W.A., from Perth S to near Bridgetown.
notes: See note under Lomandra nigricans regarding past taxonomic confusion of this species.

habit_description: Large tufts or small trees
stem_description: stems up to 1.5 m long, erect or reclining | branches whorled
leaf_description: Leaves flat, 60--150 cm long, 10--20 mm wide, glabrous | apex rounded | sheath margins intact, reddish brown
inflorescence_description: scape shorter to longer than rachis, somewhat compressed | bract and inner bract white | pedicel up to 3.5 mm long in male, c. 0.5 mm long in female
flower_description: flower clusters whorled | Flowers campanulate, 4--6 mm long, shortly pedicellate | Sepals and petals similar, white or cream
habitat_description: Grows on river banks, often in sandy soil.
distribution_description: Occurs in south-western W.A., from Northcliffe to Walpole.

habit_description: Tuft robust
leaf_description: Leaves flat or inrolled, 40--100 cm long, 2.5--4.5 mm wide, smooth | apex rounded | sheath margins intact or slightly lacerated, white, grey or brown
inflorescence_description: scape shorter than rachis, flattened or somewhat compressed | bract and inner bract white
flower_description: flower clusters whorled | Flowers campanulate | Male flowers 4--6 mm long, sessile or on a pedicel with up to 1 mm visible above bracts | Female flowers sessile, mature length unknown | Sepals and petals similar except sepals thicker | sepals purple or yellowish purple | petals yellow
habitat_description: In Central Australia it grows in gorges, elsewhere on rocky hillsides.
distribution_description: Occurs in the Macdonnell and adjacent ranges of Central Australia, N.T., in scattered locations in inland N.S.W. and south-central Qld.
notes: Similar to Lomandra multiflora but differs in being a larger plant with larger inflorescences that are always well-branched in both sexes, and in having well-developed pistillodes c. 1.5 mm long in male flowers compared with minute ones in L. multiflora .

stem_description: Stems decumbent, spreading or in a dense cushion
leaf_description: Leaves flat or concave, fine, up to c. 30 cm long, 0.5--1 mm wide, glabrous | apex acute | readily eroding | sheath margins intact except in age, white

Lomandra sororia differs from L. brittanii in having longer, rigid, terete leaves and larger inflorescences, male and female scarcely distinct, not the short, flexible, flat leaves and small inflorescences, male and female markedly different, of L. brittanii . Some plants of L. sororia from Vic. (eg. from Mt Clay and Anglesea) show similarities to L. brittanii but the male and female inflorescences are similar and the scabridities on the leaves are horizontally elongated and confined to or project into the furrows, rather than being erect and papilla-like as in L. brittanii .

Recently, however, specimens resembling the latter subspecies have been collected in the Kimberley region; further distributional data should determine whether the subspecies can continue to be recognised.
