habitat_description: Found on coastal ranges and adjacent tablelands.
distribution_description: Endemic to New South Wales, where it occurs from Sassafras to Lake Bathurst and Braidwood, with an apparently isolated occurrence southwest of Eden.
notes: Morphologically intermediate between the other two subspecies, but with a more southern distribution.

habit_description: Shrub 2--5 m high
flower_description: Anther 0.5--0.7 mm long
fruit_description: Cone bracteoles obtuse to truncate
habitat_description: Occurs on tablelands and western slopes.
distribution_description: Endemic to New South Wales, where it occurs from the Pilliga Scrub south to Temora, and in the Capertee to Bathurst area.

habit_description: Shrub 1--2.5 m high
flower_description: Anther 0.5--0.7 mm long
fruit_description: Cone bracteoles obtuse to broadly acute
distribution_description: Endemic to New South Wales, where it occurs in the Sydney area from Kingsford to Little Bay and northwest of Heathcote and also in the Central Tablelands from Blackheath to Taralga and Bundanoon.

common_name: Black Sheoak, Scrub Oak, She Oak.
habit_description: Dioecious shrub 1--3 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes occasionally moniliform, 1.5--5 (rarely to 9) cm long, 4.5--6.5 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | peduncle 2--15 mm long, rarely to 32 mm long and 2--4 mm diam. | bracteoles obtuse to truncate, pyramidal protuberance shorter than bracteole body
flower_description: anther 0.8--1.3 mm long
fruit_description: Cones long-cylindrical, often with sterile apex to 12 mm long | cone body 13--35 (rarely to 50) mm long, 11--22 mm diam. | Samara 4--8 mm long, very dark brown to black
habitat_description: Grows in tall heath on sandstone ridge tops.
distribution_description: Occurs from the south side of Port Stephens and Gospers Mountain south to the ranges east of Cooma, New South Wales, and perhaps on the upper Genoa River, Victoria.
notes: Hybrids between this species and Allocasuarina littoralis are quite common in disturbed areas between Broken Bay and Port Hacking.

habit_description: Dioecious intricate shrub 0.5--3 m high, penultimate branchlets green
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 4--10 mm long, c. 20 whorls per cm | bracteoles thick, flat-topped and triangular, divided into 5--8 convex bodies
flower_description: anther c. 0.7 mm long
fruit_description: Cones ovoid to cylindrical, sessile on woody branches, cone body 8--15 mm long, 7--8 mm diam. | Samara 3.0--4.0 mm long, sparsely hairy
habitat_description: Grows in tall heath on lateritic ridges and on sandplain.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where restricted to Three Springs - Wongan Hills area.
notes: The samara of this species has a very short wing and sparse short (1--2 mm long) white hairs on the sides of the body.

habit_description: Dioecious, erect tree to 8 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 7.5--13 mm long, early deciduous, usually with 6--8 whorls | bracteoles obtuse, the protuberance equalling the bracteole body
flower_description: anthers c. 1 mm long
fruit_description: cone body 1.5--6 cm long, 12--25 mm in diam. | Samaras 6--10 mm long, dark brown to black
habitat_description: Chiefly on dolerite rock plates or shallow soils over dolerite, typically in association with either Eucalyptus delegatensis or Eucalyptus coccifera. Two small sites are on quartzitic sandstone; 230--1000 m alt., with most plants above 500 m.
distribution_description: Occurs in south-eastern Tas.

common_name: Emu Mountain Sheoak, Mt Emu She-oak.
habit_description: Dioecious spreading shrub 0.5--1.5 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 1--3 cm long, 8.5--9.5 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | peduncle 3--13 mm long, slender | bracteoles broadly acute to obtuse, pyramidal protuberance shorter than bracteole body and diverging from it low down
flower_description: anther 0.8--0.9 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical, occasionally irregular and with a sterile apex to c. 5 mm long | cone body 12--28 mm long, 6--15 mm diam. | Samara 4.5--7.5 mm long, dark brown to black
habitat_description: Grows in low heath in acid volcanic soil and in nearby wallum areas.
distribution_description: Occurs from northerly slopes of Mount Emu, N of Coolum, S to Caloundra, Queensland.
notes: The populations are slightly different.

habit_description: Dioecious or monoecious shrub, dense, erect, 1--3 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 1--3.5 cm long, 7--11 whorls per cm | peduncle 4--15 mm long | bracts often inconspicuous | bracteoles with obtuse to acute apex, protuberance completely fused to bracteole body except apex of protuberance which is marked by a curved or straight line or indentation (rarely a tiny mucro) across bracteole body
flower_description: anther 0.6--0.8 mm long
fruit_description: Cones long-cylindrical, shortly white-pubescent at least between bracts and bracteoles with some longer ferruginous hairs | cone body 20--45 mm long, 13--21 mm diam. | Samara 5--10.5 mm long, black
habitat_description: Usually found on or near rocky outcrops.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where it occurs from Comet Vale to Norseman, with an apparent outlier SSE of Zanthus.
notes: Related to Allocasuarina campestris, but differing morphologically in having pedunculate cones with more persistent indumentum, and phyllichnia without a small ridge; they differ also in habitat preferences. Allocasuarina eriochlamys subsp. eriochlamysCones with bract slightly thickened and bracteoles scarcely exceeding cone body; articles 0.5--0.9 mm diam.; cone body 13--18 mm diam. Allocasuarina eriochlamys subsp. grossaCones with bract strongly thickened and bracteoles protruding prominently beyond cone body; articles 0.8--1.1 mm diam.; cone body 14--21 mm diam.

inflorescence_description: Male spikes 10--34 mm long, c. 7 whorls per cm | bracteoles not protruding beyond cone body, with obtuse to truncate apex, indentation marking apex of protuberance close to body apex
fruit_description: Cones on peduncle 4--13 mm long, cone body 23--39 mm long, 13--18 mm diam.
habitat_description: Found in mallee woodland on stony and gravelly slopes, probably usually near subdued rocky outcrops.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where it occurs in the Comet Vale - Kalgoorlie area.

inflorescence_description: Male spikes 16--35 mm long, 10--11 whorls per cm | bracts thickened laterally, so base appears 2-lobed | bracteoles protruding prominently beyond cone body, with acute to broadly acute apex, indentation marking apex of protuberance below body apex
fruit_description: Cones on peduncle 4--15 mm long, cone body 20--38 mm long, 14--21 mm diam.
habitat_description: Grows around granite outcrops.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where it occurs in the Norseman district, with one record SSE of Zanthus.
notes: Cone bracts are more prominent and thicker than in Allocasuarina campestris; bracteole has indentation below apex (cf. subsp. eriochlamys and A. campestris) and is slightly less prominent than in A. campestris.

habit_description: Shrub 0.5--1.5 m high, penultimate branchlets woody
stem_description: Branchlets 2--5 cm long, elongate articles 2--4, terete, 8--16 mm long, glabrous | erect, with broad whitish translucent margins at least towards apex, 1.5--2.0 mm long
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 4--7 mm long | bracteoles thin, long-acuminate, often awn-like (c. 1 mm long) and hooked, with thick pyramidal protuberance separating from bracteole near base, with short curved awn 1--2 mm long
flower_description: anther 0.5--0.6 mm long
fruit_description: Cones subcylindrical to globose, with long coarse hairs, cone body 11--25 mm long, 9--11 mm diam. | Samara 6--7 mm long, glabrous, brown to black
habitat_description: Found in tall open-heath in sand over laterite on a low ridge.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where only one population known, near Tammin.
notes: This species has a cone with long (10--20 mm) tangled coarse hairs on the body, protruding from between the bracts and bracteoles.

habit_description: Dioecious shrub 1.5--3 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes elongate but too young to describe details | peduncle 2--9 mm long | bracteoles acute to broadly acute, often with small mucro, pyramidal protuberance as long as or exceeding bracteole body, with or without little mucro
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical to barrel-shaped, sparsely pubescent | cone body 14--30 mm long, 11--18 mm diam. | Samara 6.5--9 mm long, dark brown to black
habitat_description: Grows on summits and exposed upper slopes, in crevices of trachyte rocks with other shrubs.
distribution_description: Endemic to Queensland, where restricted to the Glass House Mountains.
notes: Differs from Allocasuarina littoralis in being a shrub and in having longer articles and longer teeth which are recurved to spreading and only 5 or 6 in number.

habit_description: Tree 5--15 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 3--8 cm long, 5 or 6 whorls per cm | bracteoles broadly acute to obtuse, protuberance slightly shorter than bracteole body and divided into 4--8 bodies, pungent or obtuse
flower_description: anther 0.7--1.2 mm long
fruit_description: Cones coarse, usually shortly cylindrical, warty, pubescent at least when young, sessile or on peduncle to 32 mm long, cone body 15--40 mm long, 15--22 mm diam. | Samara 9--10 mm long
habitat_description: On the Darling Range grows in lateritic soil in Jarrah (Eucalyptus marginata) forest; near the coast grows in sand in woodland and open forest.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where it occurs from Perth to Albany, with an isolated population between Moora and Jurien Bay.

habit_description: Dioecious or monoecious slender, erect shrub 1--2 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes moniliform, 0.2--2.5 cm long, c. 5 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | bracteoles broadly acute to obtuse with tiny mucro, pyramidal protuberance much shorter than bracteole body, with obtuse apex
flower_description: anther 0.7--0.8 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical, on peduncle 4--7 mm long, cone body 10--13 mm long, 7--8 mm diam. | Samara 3.0--3.5 mm long, mid-brown
habitat_description: Found in open forest in Tertiary alluvial gravels with clayey subsoil.
distribution_description: Endemic to New South Wales, where restricted to a few small populations in and beside Castlereagh State Forest northeast of Penrith on Cumberland Plain.
notes: Differs from Allocasuarina rigida in its shorter, more slender articles (which often have only slightly rounded phyllichnia), 5--7 teeth which are usually shorter, not marcescent and much less spreading and overlapping, and its smaller cones. Differs from A. defungens in its yellow-green articles, phyllichnia that are occasionally strongly rounded, and teeth that are straighter-sided and often somewhat spreading.

habit_description: Dioecious shrub c. 1.5 m high
inflorescence_description: bracts inconspicuous | bracteoles with obtuse apex, divided into 3 obtuse bodies surmounted by a tiny mucro
flower_description: Males unknown
fruit_description: Cones subglobose, tessellated, sessile, cone body 15--17 mm long, 13--15 mm diam. | Samara 6.0--6.5 mm long, mid-brown
habitat_description: Found in dense scrub with Allocasuarina campestris, at the foot of a steep slope (J.S. Beard, Proc. Linn. Soc. New South Wales 93: 264 (1969)).
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where known only from Mount Day at the northwest end of the Bremer Range, west of Norseman.
notes: This species differs from Allocasuarina scleroclada in the shorter teeth, slender articles, paler samara and divided bracteoles; from A. campestris and A. tessellata in the longer articles, inconspicuous cone bracts, shorter cone, paler samara and the form of the divided cone bracteoles.

habit_description: Dioecious shrub 1.5--4 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes moniliform, 1--4 cm long, 5 or 6 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | peduncle 2--6 mm long | bracteoles broadly acute to obtuse, pyramidal protuberance shorter than bracteole body
flower_description: anther 0.7--0.8 mm long
fruit_description: Cones long-cylindrical, with short sterile apex to 3 mm long | cone body 13--35 mm long, 7--9 mm diam. | Samara 4.5--5.5 mm long, black
habitat_description: Associated with sandstone outcrops.
distribution_description: Endemic to Victoria, where restricted to The Grampians.
notes: Close to Allocasuarina monilifera and A. zephyrea of Tasmania, but distinguished by a combination of the phyllichnia being generally more angular and the articles having a stronger waxy bloom.

habit_description: Spreading, lignotuberous shrub, 15--30 cm high, penultimate branchlets green
stem_description: Branchlets ascending, pungent, 1--3 cm long, elongate article(s) 1 or 2, terete to subquadrangular, 10--24 mm long, 0.5--0.8 mm diam., often pubescent when young, phyllichnia flat or with broad shallow median groove | erect to slightly spreading, overlapping, usually shortly fimbriate, 0.3--0.6 mm long, marcescent
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 2--5 mm long, dense | bracts with deciduous awn c. 1.5 mm long | bracteoles greatly thickened but relatively small, acute, protuberance much shorter than bracteole body, divided into 4--6 small pyramidal bodies
flower_description: anther 0.6--0.7 mm long
fruit_description: Cones inconspicuous, ovoid, irregular, sessile, densely and minutely pubescent, becoming glabrous, cone body 9--14 mm long, 6--9 mm diam. | Samara 5.5--7 mm long, very dark brown, with long ferruginous hairs
habitat_description: Grows in heath.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where restricted to the Jurien Bay - Mogumber area.
notes: This species has an unusual samara that is usually wingless and very plump, with a dense mass of long (5--7 mm) ferruginous septate hairs (readily deciduous).

habit_description: Dioecious or rarely monoecious shrub or tree, 2--5 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes moniliform, 2.5--6 cm long, 3--5 whorls per cm | bracteoles deciduous | peduncle 3--8 mm long | bracteoles obtuse or truncate, pyramidal protuberance slightly shorter than bracteole body, obtuse
flower_description: anther 0.8--1.4 mm long
fruit_description: Cones usually long-cylindrical, often with sterile apex to 3 mm long, often sparsely pubescent | cone body 14--40 mm long, 9--12 mm diam. | Samara 4.5--7 mm long, very dark brown to black
habitat_description: Grows in low open woodland in sandy soil on sandstone ridges.
distribution_description: Endemic to New South Wales, where it occurs from the southern Pilliga Scrub to the lower Goulburn River Valley (Ulan and Baerami) and to Glen Davis.
notes: Differs from most species in section Cylindropitys in its long, strongly moniliform male spikes with deciduous bracteoles. Differs from Allocasuarina striata in its shorter and more slender articles with usually pubescent furrows and 6--9 shortish teeth. Its geographical range overlaps that of A. diminuta.

habit_description: Dioecious shrub, 1--5 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 0.5--2.5 cm long, 9--12 whorls per cm | bracts inconspicuous | bracteoles thick, body and protuberance not distinguishable, the whole divided into 4--7 obtuse or truncate bodies
flower_description: anther 0.5--0.7 mm long
fruit_description: Cone usually long-cylindrical, of smoothish outline and tessellated surface, shortly white-pubescent, sometimes ferruginous-pubescent when young, sessile or on peduncle to 4 mm long, cone body 15--33 mm long, 8--13 mm diam. | Samara 4--5 mm long, mid-brown
habitat_description: Found in mallee woodland and tall heath, in a wide range of soils.
distribution_description: Occurs from Nungarin, Western Australia, to northwestern South Australia, with outliers on the northern Eyre Peninsula, South Australia, and Dirk Hartog Island, Western Australia.

habit_description: Tree 4--10 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 2--10 cm long, 4.5--7 whorls per cm | bracteoles obtuse to acute
flower_description: anther 0.8--1.2 mm long
fruit_description: Cones on peduncle 3--5 mm long, cone body 14--35 mm long, 10--14 mm diam. | Samara 5--7 mm long, dark brown to black
habitat_description: Associated with granite.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where it occurs from Murchison River and Mingenew south to the south coast and east to Newman Rock, west of Balladonia.
notes: Close to Allocasuarina verticillata, but A. huegeliana is more slender and has cones with more rounded bracteoles.

habit_description: Dioecious or monoecious shrub, erect to spreading, 0.2--2 m high, penultimate branchlets woody
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 6--18 mm long, 12--16 whorls per cm | bracteoles thick, flat-topped and triangular, divided into 6--8 obtuse or acute bodies
flower_description: anther 0.7--0.8 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical, slightly longer than broad, of smoothish outline and tessellated surface, sessile, cone body 12--22 (rarely to 33) mm long, 10--17 mm diam. | Samara 5--6 mm long, glabrous | wing truncate, shorter than body
habitat_description: Grows in heath in sand.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where widespread from the Murchison River south to the south coast and east to Israelite Bay.
notes: Exhibits considerable morphological variation.

flowering_time_description: Male flowers have been collected in February; female flowers in February, April, June and December
habit_description: Dioecious shrub to 3 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes sessile on the permanent branches, 0.4--1.5 cm long, 12--15 whorls per cm | bracts inconspicuous | bracteoles broadly ovate | apex with or without tiny mucro | dorsal protuberance divided into (2-) 3 (-5) spines | the spines deciduous | reddish brown, central awn pyramidal, separating near the base of bracteole body, 1.5--6 mm long, curved to straight, sometimes hooked at apex, minor lateral awns subulate, occasionally pyramidal, 0.5--3 mm long
flower_description: anthers 0.6--0.8 mm long
fruit_description: Cones sessile, oblong to elliptic, more rarely subglobose, truncate at apex, pubescent, becoming glabrous with age, cone body (10-) 13--30 mm long, (10-) 13--18 mm wide | Samara 4.5--9 mm long, glabrous, red-brown to brown-black
phenology_text: Male flowers have been collected in February; female flowers in February, April, June and December.
habitat_description: Occurs on plains, lower slopes and hilltops, in orange, red or brown loam with limestone or granite outcropping. Recorded from mallee shrubland or heathland, shrubland with Acacia ophiolithica and Hakea verrucosa, and heathland with Allocasuarina campestris. Also noted to form small dense stands, sometimes in association with Melaleuca pauperiflora and Gahnia lanigera.
distribution_description: Endemic to Esperance Plains IBRA region, south-western Western Australia, where known largely from the Ravensthorpe region.

habit_description: Open tree 3--10 m high
stem_description: Branchlets drooping or ascending, to 21 cm long
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 2--4 cm long, 7--14 whorls per cm | peduncle 3--8 mm long | bracteoles acute to obtuse, protuberance usually divided near apex into 2 or 3 bodies, acute to obtuse, rarely only 1 body
flower_description: anther 0.5--0.8 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical, densely pubescent | cone body 10--20 mm long, 9--12 mm diam. | Samara 5--6 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in woodland on sandstone or laterite ridges.
distribution_description: Occurs from the Herberton area, Queensland, south to Warialda, New South Wales.
notes: The ribbony-fibrous bark of this species is unique in the family.

habit_description: Dioecious or less commonly monoecious shrub 1.5--4 m high
stem_description: Branchlet articles 5--9 mm long, 0.7--1.2 mm diam., occasionally with a waxy bloom, phyllichnia rounded to angular | not overlapping, 0.4--0.8 mm long, not marcescent
inflorescence_description: Male spikes often moniliform, 1--3 (rarely to 6) cm long, 5--8 whorls per cm
flower_description: anther 0.6--0.9 mm long
fruit_description: Cones on peduncle 2--38 mm long, rarely sessile, cone body 12--35 mm long, 7--12 mm diam | Samara 4--5.5 mm long, black
habitat_description: Grows in woodland and tall scrub, often near the sea, in sandy-loam and sandy soils.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where it occurs from Jurien Bay south to near Albany and east to Ravensthorpe.
notes: Allocasuarina lehmanniana subsp. ecarinataPhyllichnia strongly rounded to angular, without median groove; teeth 7 or 8; cones on peduncle 4--38 (rarely 2) mm long. Allocasuarina lehmanniana subsp. lehmannianaPhyllichnia flat to slightly rounded, often with median groove; teeth 6 or 7; cones sessile or on peduncle to 4 mm long.

habit_description: Dioecious or monoecious shrub 0.5--1 m high
fruit_description: Cones sessile or on peduncle to 4 mm long, cone body 12--24 mm long, 7--11 mm diam
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where it occurs from near Ongerup to east of Esperance.

habit_description: Dioecious or rarely monoecious shrub 1--4 m high
fruit_description: Cones on peduncle 4--38 (rarely to 2) mm long, cone body 13--35 mm long, 9--12 mm diam
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where it occurs from Jurien Bay south to east of Albany.

common_name: Black Sheoak, Black Oak, Bull Oak, Stringybark Oak, Hairy Oak Flame Oak.
habit_description: Usually dioecious tree 5--15 m high or rarely shrub
stem_description: Branchlets ascending or drooping, to 20 (rarely to 35) cm long
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 0.5--5 cm long, 6--12.5 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | peduncle 4--23 mm long | bracteoles thin, broadly acute to obtuse, thick pyramidal protuberance shorter than bracteole body, occasionally with 2 lateral bodies
flower_description: anther 0.4--0.8 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical, rarely broader than long, pubescent at least when young | cone body 10--30 (rarely to 45) mm long, 8--21 mm diam. | Samara 4--10 mm long, dark brown to black
habitat_description: Grows in woodland and occasionally tall heath, in sandy and other poor soils (cf. Allocasuarina torulosa).
distribution_description: Occurs from Cape York, Queensland, south along coast and adjoining tablelands to the Otway Range, Victoria, and down the east coast of Tasmania to south of Hobart.
notes: Very variable in size of articles and cones. Occurs as a coarse shrub in maritime exposed situations. Variation is not simply linked to chromosome number or distribution, and there appears to be complete intergradation between forms.

habit_description: Tree 5--15 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 1.5--4.5 cm long, 5--8 whorls per cm | bracteoles acute to obtuse, protuberance pyramidal or flattened, obtuse, much shorter than bracteole body and diverging from it near its base
flower_description: anther 1--1.3 mm long
fruit_description: Cones very shortly cylindrical (broader than long), pubescent at least when young, sessile or on peduncle to 5 mm long, cone body 5--12 mm long, 8--14 mm diam. | Samara 4.5--5.0 mm long
habitat_description: Scattered in woodland in non-calcareous soils.
distribution_description: Occurs from Mareeba, Queensland, south through central Queensland and New South Wales to northwestern Victoria and adjoining areas of South Australia to south of Bordertown; rarely towards the coast, as in the Hunter Valley, New South Wales, and near Rockhampton, Queensland; also in the Australian Capital Territory.

habit_description: Dioecious or rarely monoecious shrub 0.5--3 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes very dense and thick, 1--4 cm long, 4.5--10 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | bracteoles obtuse to broadly acute, pyramidal protuberance slightly shorter than bracteole body
flower_description: anther 0.8--1.5 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical, occasionally broader than long, sessile or on peduncle to 3 mm long, cone body 12--22 (rarely to 30) mm long, 8--14 mm diam. | Samara 5--7.5 mm long, dark red-brown to black
distribution_description: Occurs from the Southern Lofty Ranges, South Australia, east to western Victoria.
notes: Closely related to Allocasuarina paradoxa. Allocasuarina mackliniana subsp. hirtilineaBranchlets with furrows pubescent, often strongly so; phyllichnia slightly rounded. Allocasuarina mackliniana subsp. macklinianaBranchlets with phyllichnia rounded and furrows glabrous Allocasuarina mackliniana subsp. xerophilaBranchlets with furrows pubescent usually only when young; phyllichnia nearly flat to slightly rounded.

inflorescence_description: Male spikes with c. 7 whorls per cm
flower_description: anther 1.1--1.5 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in woodland in sandy soils.
distribution_description: Endemic to Victoria, where found in the western parts of The Grampians.

inflorescence_description: Male spikes with 6--9 whorls per cm
flower_description: anther 0.9--1.1 mm long
habitat_description: Found in heath in sandy soils.
distribution_description: Occurs from the southern Lofty Ranges, South Australia, to near Portland, Victoria.

inflorescence_description: Male spikes with 4.5--5 whorls per cm
flower_description: anther 0.8--1.5 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in heath in sandy soils.
distribution_description: Occurs from near Pinnaroo and Keith, South Australia, to Wyperfeld National Park and the Little Desert, Victoria.
notes: Some forms from the Little Desert may approach Allocasuarina mackliniana subsp. hirtilinea; there is also intergradation to subsp. mackliniana generally in the southern part of the range.

habit_description: Dioecious or rarely monoecious shrub 1--3 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes occasionally moniliform, 1--4.5 cm long, 5--7 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | bracteoles obtuse to broadly acute, pyramidal protuberance slightly shorter than bracteole body
flower_description: anther 0.6--1 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical, sessile or on peduncle to 12 mm long, cone body 14--27 (rarely to 45) mm long, 8--15 mm diam. | Samara 5--8 mm long, very dark red-brown to black
habitat_description: Found in low woodland in sand.
distribution_description: Endemic to Victoria, where it occurs only at the northern end of Wilsons Promontory.
notes: Probably a taxon of recent hybrid origin from Allocasuarina littoralis and A. paradoxa (which are in the region but not in the particular localities), but fairly well stabilised and self-reproducing. Differs from A. littoralis in being a smooth-barked shrub, with branchlets usually with glabrous furrows, with male spikes mostly moniliform, and with cones on generally shorter peduncles. Differs from A. paradoxa in the often more slender branchlets with erect to only slightly spreading teeth, which are more slender and often shorter than in A. paradoxa and are not marcescent.

habit_description: Dioecious intricate shrub 0.1--1 m high, penultimate branchlets green
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 1.5--3 mm long | bracteoles thick, divided into 6--9 tubercles, rounded or flat-topped with deciduous mucro 0.5--3 mm long
flower_description: anther 0.5--0.6 mm long
fruit_description: Cones shortly cylindrical to ovoid, irregular, sessile, cone body 8--12 mm long, 5--10 mm diam. | Samara 2.5--5 mm long, hairy
habitat_description: Grows in heath in gravelly sand over laterite.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where it occurs from Strawberry, near Geraldton, southeast to Albany and the Munglinup River, east of Ravensthorpe.
notes: Variable in size characters. The samara is most striking, being wingless and having a mass of spreading, long, septate, usually ferruginous hairs c. 3--5 mm long.

habit_description: Dioecious or monoecious shrub 0.5--2 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes rarely moniliform, 0.5--1.5 cm long, 9--11 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | bracteoles obtuse to acute, pyramidal protuberance usually slightly shorter than bracteole body
flower_description: anther 0.5--0.8 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical, sessile or on peduncle to 5 mm long, cone body 9--16 mm long, 7--13 mm diam. | Samara 4--6 mm long, very dark red-brown to black
habitat_description: Grows in heath or open woodland in sandy soil.
distribution_description: Endemic to Victoria, where it occurs from The Grampians to near Bairnsdale.
notes: Occurs as isolated populations, showing some variation; in particular, some specimens from eastern Victoria have coarser branchlets (though still short-toothed). Allocasuarina misera is generally more slender and has more erect teeth than the related species A. mackliniana and A. paradoxa . It further differs from A. mackliniana in its slender male spikes. It differs from A. pusilla in lacking a waxy bloom and median groove on the phyllichnia and in often having longer teeth (0.3--0.8 mm long), which are brown rather than pale yellow.

habit_description: Usually monoecious shrub 1.5--4 m high
stem_description: Branchlet articles 6--11 mm long, 0.6--1.2 mm diam., at least slightly waxy, phyllichnia strongly to slightly rounded | erect and appressed to slightly spreading, often overlapping, eventually the apex marcescent, 0.5--1 mm long
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 1--3.5 cm long, with 3.5--7 whorls per cm | bracteoles truncate to broadly acute | bracteole protuberance shorter than or occasionally equalling body
flower_description: anther 0.7--1.2 mm long
fruit_description: Cones on peduncle 2--10 mm long, cone body 15--30 mm long, 8--14 mm diam. | Samara 5--6 mm long, very dark brown to black
habitat_description: Grows in lowland heath and open woodland in sandy soil.
distribution_description: Endemic in northern and eastern Tasmania, also Flinders Island and Kent Group in Bass Strait.
notes: Similar to Allocasuarina grampiana. Also close to A. zephyrea, but differing in being tetraploid and mostly monoecious and in having slightly broader teeth that are mostly erect and appressed (occasionally teeth spreading) and in typically having articles more waxy. Articles vary in coarseness, while phyllichnium shape varies from strongly and narrowly rounded with a prominent rounded ridge to nearly flat, and teeth vary from appressed to spreading. However, there is no clear pattern to this variation and hence no formal subspecific taxa are here recognised.

habit_description: Dioecious or rarely monoecious shrub 0.5--3 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes often moniliform, 1--4 cm long, 6--8 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | bracteoles not protruding far from cone body, obtuse to truncate, thick pyramidal protuberance shorter than bracteole body
flower_description: anther 0.5--1.0 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical, often with short sterile apex to 5 mm long, sessile or on peduncle to 16 mm long, cone body 14--30 (rarely to 35) mm long, 9--18 mm diam. | Samara 6--9 (rarely 5) mm long, black
habitat_description: Grows in scrub and heath, in rocky siliceous soils.
distribution_description: Occurs from Ceduna and the Flinders Ranges, South Australia, east to Bendigo, Victoria; also on Kangaroo Island, South Australia.
notes: Allocasuarina muelleriana subsp. alticolaArticles 0.7--1.1 mm diam.; phyllichnium margins flat; cone body 12--18 mm diam. Cones sessile or on peduncle to 3 mm long, 2.5 mm diam. Allocasuarina muelleriana subsp. muellerianaArticles 0.6--0.8 mm diam.; phyllichnium margins (when dry) often raised along furrows; cone body usually 9--12 mm diam.; peduncle usually 1--8 mm long. Allocasuarina muelleriana subsp. notocolpicaArticles 0.7--1.1 mm diam.; phyllichnium margins flat; cone body 12--18 mm diam. Cones on stout peduncle 8--17 mm long, 3--4.5 mm diam.

habit_description: Shrub 1.5--3 m high
fruit_description: Cones sessile or on short peduncle to 3 mm long, cone body 18--30 mm long, 12--17 mm diam
distribution_description: Endemic to South Australia, where it occurs in the northern Flinders Range from Freeling Heights south to Wilpena Pound and Bibliando.

habit_description: Shrub 0.5--3 m high
fruit_description: Cones on peduncle 1--8 (rarely to 16) mm long, cone body 14--28 (rarely to 35) mm long, 9--12 (rarely to 15) mm diam
distribution_description: Occurs throughout range of species, except the Northern Flinders Range and Kangaroo Island.

habit_description: Shrub 2--3 m high
fruit_description: Cones on stout peduncle 8--17 mm long, 3--4.5 mm diam., cone body 18--30 mm long, 12--18 mm diam
distribution_description: Restricted to Kangaroo Island, South Australia.
notes: In eastern and northern parts of the island there may be some gradation towards Allocasuarina muelleriana subsp. muelleriana.

habit_description: Spreading shrub, 0.2--2 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes dense, 5--10 mm long, 16--20 whorls per cm | bracteoles thick, body and protuberance not distinguishable, acute to broadly acute, divided into 2 larger and 3 (rarely to 5) smaller bodies
flower_description: anther 0.5--0.6 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical to barrel-shaped, sessile or on peduncle to 3 mm long, cone body 14--24 mm long, 10--15 mm diam. | Samara 4--6 mm long
habitat_description: Grows on the coast and tablelands in heath on sandstone, in exposed situations such as ridges on the ranges of the eastern highlands.
distribution_description: Occurs from Cowan and Glen Davis, New South Wales, south to the upper Genoa River, Victoria.
notes: This is the only eastern Australian species with cones that are of smoothish outline with a tessellated surface because of the thick, divided bracteoles and protuberances. There are considerable disjunctions in its distribution.

habit_description: Shrub 1--3 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes not moniliform, 1--2.5 cm long, c. 6 whorls per cm | bracteoles obtuse to very broadly acute
flower_description: anther 0.8--1.2 mm long
fruit_description: Cones on peduncle 3--15 mm long, cone body 9--20 mm long, 7--12 mm diam. | Samara 3.5--6 mm long, mid-brown
habitat_description: Grows on serpentinite outcrops in tall heath and low open woodland.
distribution_description: Endemic to New South Wales, where restricted to the southern end of the New England region and adjoining coastal ranges, from Bralga Tops to Curricabark and Glenrock.
notes: Similar to Allocasuarina rigida, differing in its generally shorter and more slender articles with more rounded phyllichnia and more erect teeth (which are not overlapping or marcescent), its cone bracteoles (which are often more acute) and its paler samara. Plants small in more exposed situations, tree-like in more sheltered situations.

habit_description: Monoecious or dioecious shrub, spreading, 0.3--3 m high
stem_description: Branchlets ascending or curved, to 20 cm long
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 1--2.5 cm long, 7--9 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | bracteoles truncate to obtuse, pyramidal protuberance shorter than bracteole body, truncate, often with minute deciduous mucro
flower_description: anther 0.7--1.1 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical to ovoid, sessile or on peduncle to 2 mm long, cone body 10--18 mm long, 7--13 mm diam. | Samara 3.5--5 mm long, dark brown to black
habitat_description: Grows in heath and in poorly drained soils above swamps at edge of woodland.
distribution_description: Occurs from Broken Bay, New South Wales, south along coast and adjoining tablelands to northeastern Tasmania (including Flinders Island) and west to Lucindale and Mount Burr, South Australia.
notes: Individuals in a population may appear green or grey depending on hairiness of articles. Variable in size.

habit_description: Dioecious or less often monoecious shrub 0.5--2 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes rarely moniliform, 1--3 cm long, 3.5--7 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | bracteoles obtuse to broadly acute, pyramidal protuberance slightly shorter than bracteole body
flower_description: anther 0.7--1.2 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical, sessile or on peduncle to 3 mm long, cone body 13--25 mm long, 7--13 mm diam. | Samara 4--8 mm long, very dark red-brown to black
habitat_description: Often grows in tall heath in sandy soil.
distribution_description: Endemic to Victoria, where it occurs in The Grampians and from the Melbourne area to Wilsons Promontory.
notes: Allocasuarina paradoxa and A. mackliniana are closely related. They are more or less sympatric in The Grampians, but have separate ranges elsewhere. A. mackliniana is typically coarser than A. paradoxa (although the Wilsons Promontory form of A. paradoxa may be coarse), with phyllichnia less strongly rounded and typically with teeth strongly marcescent, more overlapping and recurved especially on the very dense, thick male spikes. The two species are closely related to A. misera and A. pusilla .

habit_description: Shrub 1--3 m high
stem_description: Branchlets 2--6 cm long with 1 elongate article
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 5--10 mm long, 8--10 whorls per cm | bracteole apex with small deciduous mucro, protuberance separating from bracteole body near base, extending into yellowish awn 3--7 mm long and about as long as or exceeding bracteole apex
flower_description: anther 1--1.4 mm long
fruit_description: Cones sessile or on peduncle to 5 mm long, cone body 14--25 mm long, 12--16 mm diam. | Samara 10--11 mm long, dark brown to black
habitat_description: Grows in tall shrubland and heathland in lateritic soils.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where restricted to the Hyden-Dumbleyung area.
notes: Similar to Allocasuarina acuaria, but generally larger. Female plants have a distinct main stem and a number of main branches aligned parallel to it, the whole axis thus formed being inclined at 30--40° from the vertical and in a consistent southerly direction; male plants are smaller and are more spreading with no main stem and branchlets less clustered (J.S. Beard, W. Austral. Nat. 11: 73--75, 1969).

habit_description: Slender dioecious shrub, 3--5 m high
stem_description: Branchlets drooping to spreading, to 27 cm long
inflorescence_description: Male spikes moniliform, 5--10 cm long, 3.5--4.5 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | peduncle 2--15 mm long | bracteoles obtuse, pyramidal, protuberance shorter than bracteole body
flower_description: anther 0.8--1 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical | cone body 12--15 mm long, 8--10 mm diam. | Samara 4--5 mm long, dark brown
habitat_description: Found in tall shrubland on slope of sandstone headland.
distribution_description: Endemic to New South Wales, where known only from 10 individuals in Sydney Harbour National Park, c. 6 km ENE of Sydney.
notes: Differs from typical Allocasuarina rigida and A. diminuta in the strongly moniliform male spikes. From A. rigida subsp. exsul it differs in its generally longer articles and often longer, broader teeth. It further differs from A. rigida in its more rounded phyllichnia and generally more slender articles; from A. diminuta in its spreading and mostly slightly overlapping teeth, its longer articles and its longer, less dense male spikes.

habit_description: Dioecious spreading shrub 0.2--2 m high
stem_description: Branchlets ascending or spreading, to 12 cm long
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 0.3--2 cm long, 8--11 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | bracteoles broadly acute to obtuse, pyramidal protuberance shorter than bracteole body
flower_description: anther 0.6--1 mm long
fruit_description: Cones subglobose or shortly cylindrical, occasionally as broad as long, sessile, cone body 10--15 mm long, 8--11 (rarely to 13) mm diam. | Samara 4.5--5.0 mm long, very dark brown to black
habitat_description: Grows in heath in sandy soil.
distribution_description: Occurs from Yorke Peninsula, South Australia, east to Big and Little Deserts, Victoria.
notes: Differs from Allocasuarina mackliniana and A. paradoxa in its slender glabrous articles, usually with a waxy bloom, and flat to rounded phyllichnia (with median line or groove) and short, erect teeth, and its slender male spikes.

habit_description: Somewhat divaricate shrub c. 1 m high, penultimate branchlets green
stem_description: Branchlets ascending, verticillate, 1--6 cm long, elongate articles 1--5, terete to subangular, 6--20 mm long, 0.6--1 mm diam., glabrous or pubescent especially in furrows, phyllichnia rounded, lacking median groove | ascending to spreading, markedly overlapping, 0.6--1.3 mm long, marcescent, dark brown with broad white erose margins
inflorescence_description: Male spikes head-like, 1.5--2.0 mm long, with prominent bracts | bracts densely pubescent when young, with deciduous dark brown broadly acute apex with broad erose margins | bracteoles inconspicuous, truncate, with small protuberance
flower_description: anther 0.6--0.7 mm long
fruit_description: Cones ovoid to cylindrical, sessile, with short coarse hairs 1--2 mm long around bracts and bracteoles, cone body 9--13 mm long, 7--9 mm diam. | Samara 4.5--5.0 mm long, dark brown (including short wing), shortly pubescent on sides of body at least towards base
habitat_description: Found in heath in sand.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where restricted to Badgingarra-Dandaragan area.
notes: Cone features are obscured by the very prominent cone bracts and ferruginous hairs and deciduous coarse grey hairs or hair-like appendages.

habit_description: Dioecious shrub 0.5--4 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes occasionally moniliform, 1--7 cm long, rarely to 9 cm, 4--6.5 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | peduncle 2--9 mm long | bracteoles truncate to obtuse, pyramidal protuberance shorter than bracteole body
flower_description: anther 0.7--1.2 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical to ovoid, pubescent | cone body 8--27 mm long, 7--14 mm diam. | Samara 3--7.5 mm long, mid to dark brown
habitat_description: Grows in poor sandy soils on acid granite, rhyolite or trachyte, in exposed situations.
distribution_description: Occurs from the McPherson Range, Queensland, south to the Ebor area, New South Wales, with isolated occurrences on Mount Cooroora, Queensland, and, in New South Wales, on the Koonyum Range and Big Nellie north of Taree.
notes: Allocasuarina rigida subsp. exsulArticles 0.7--0.9 mm diam., 10--14 mm long; teeth erect to slightly spreading, overlapping slightly only when young. Allocasuarina rigida subsp. rigidaArticles 0.8--1.5 mm diam., 10--25 mm long; teeth recurved to spreading, overlapping.

inflorescence_description: Male spikes strongly moniliform
fruit_description: Cone body 9--19 mm long, 6--11 mm diam | Samara 3.5--4.5 mm long
habitat_description: Grows on rocky (trachyte) hillside.
distribution_description: Endemic to Queensland, where restricted to Mount Cooroora near Pomona.
notes: Differs from Allocasuarina rigida subsp. rigida (from which it is geographically isolated) in the less overlapping and spreading and slightly narrower teeth and in the strongly moniliform male spikes. From A. emuina and A. thalassoscopica it is distinguished by its longer articles with glabrous furrows, 7--9 teeth and usually smaller cones.

inflorescence_description: Male spikes not or shortly moniliform
fruit_description: Cone body 8--27 mm long, 7--14 mm diam | Samara 3--7.3 mm long
distribution_description: Occurs from the McPherson Range, Queensland, south to the Ebor area, New South Wales, and, in New South Wales, on the Koonyum Range and Big Nellie north of Taree.

habit_description: Monoecious or more rarely dioecious shrub 0.2--3 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes rarely moniliform, 0.5--4.5 cm long, 5--9 whorls per cm | bracteoles persistent | bracteoles broadly acute to obtuse, pyramidal protuberance shorter than bracteole body, acute or obtuse with mucro
flower_description: anther 0.8--1.2 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical, often irregular, sparsely pubescent, sessile or on peduncle to 3 mm long, cone body 12--20 mm long, 7--12 mm diam. | Samara 5.5--6.0 mm long, black
habitat_description: Grows in upland heath and open woodland with heathy understorey.
distribution_description: Endemic to South Australia, where it occurs in the South Mount Lofty Ranges.
notes: Differs from Allocasuarina paradoxa in its always glabrous articles with more rounded phyllichnia and less spreading, mostly non-overlapping teeth, and in being usually monoecious. Differs from A. striata in its often shorter articles and usually shorter and more slender teeth, its persistent male bracteoles, and its shorter cone peduncles. It is uncommon and could be considered endangered.

habit_description: Shrub 1--3 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes moniliform, 1--2.5 cm long, 7.5--8 whorls per cm | peduncle 2--14 mm long
flower_description: anther 0.7--0.8 mm long
fruit_description: Cones shortly cylindrical | cone body 6--19 mm long, 6--10 mm diam | Samara 2.8--5 mm long
habitat_description: In clefts in granite on mountain slopes and along rocky creeks.
distribution_description: Restricted to the area between Wyberba, Queensland, and Boonoo Boonoo Falls, New South Wales.
notes: Close to Allocasuarina rigida, but differs in teeth not spreading when fresh, and forming quite distinct populations.

habit_description: Straggling dioecious shrub, 1--3 m high
stem_description: Branchlets spreading or drooping, to 23 cm long
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 6--16 mm long, dense | bracts inconspicuous | bracteole and protuberance fused, greatly thickened, broadly acute when young, becoming thickly obtuse, with or without a tiny deciduous mucro
flower_description: anther 0.5--0.8 mm long
fruit_description: Cones subcylindrical, sessile, glabrous except scattered hairs between bracteoles, cone body 18--25 mm long, 13--19 mm diam. | Samara 5--8 mm long, black
habitat_description: Found in scrub and low woodland, in lateritic soils on rocky hillsides and on limestone pavements near the sea.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where it occurs sporadically along the southwestern coast from Borden to the western part of the Great Australian Bight.
notes: This species has a very straggling and open habit, often with a single main stem with arching drooping branches, especially in the female.

inflorescence_description: Male spikes 1.5--4.5 cm long, c. 4 whorls per cm | peduncle 3--14 mm long and c. 2 mm diam. | bracteoles broadly acute to obtuse
flower_description: anther c. 1.3 mm long
fruit_description: Cones often irregular with sterile apex to 12 mm long | cone body 14--33 mm long, 9--12 mm diam. | Samara 4.5--6 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in heath in sand.
distribution_description: Endemic to New South Wales, where known only from Myall Lakes area between Booti Booti and Nabiac.
notes: Similar to Allocasuarina distyla, but generally more slender and with the phyllichnia less angular when dry. The cones have smaller parts.

habit_description: Monoecious shrub 2--4 m high
stem_description: Branchlets with articles 8--13 mm long, 1--1.8 mm diam., verruculose | erect, slightly overlapping at bases, 0.5--1.0 mm long
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 1.5--3 cm long, 7 or 8 whorls per cm
flower_description: anther 0.8--1.3 mm long
fruit_description: Cones ovoid to cylindrical, sessile or on peduncle to 6 mm long, cone body 10--23 mm long, 8--12 mm diam., protuberance usually extending into a stout, often deciduous awn 4--11 mm long | Samara 5.5--7 mm long, very dark purple-brown to black
habitat_description: Found in tall heath on sandplain.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where widespread from Southern Cross to Norseman and Queen Victoria Spring.
notes: Previously regarded as a large-coned form of Allocasuarina corniculata, which it resembles in habit and overlaps in range, but differing in the larger cones; larger black samara; verruculose and somewhat stouter articles; teeth 9--11, slightly overlapping and broader; and in being monoecious.

habit_description: Dioecious or monoecious shrub or small tree 1--4 m high
bark_description: Bark smooth or somewhat fissured in older plants
inflorescence_description: Male spikes rarely moniliform, 1--3 cm long, 5--7 whorls per cm | bracteoles deciduous | peduncle 3--12 mm long | bracteoles obtuse, pyramidal protuberance shorter than bracteole body, rarely superficially divided into 2 or 3 parts
flower_description: anther 0.7--1.3 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical | cone body 16--33 mm long, 10--13 mm diam. | Samara 6--7 mm long, very dark brown to black
habitat_description: Grows in heath in lateritic or sandy soils.
distribution_description: Endemic to South Australia, where it occurs in the Southern Mount Lofty Range and on Kangaroo Island.
notes: Of variable habit, which may be correlated with ploidy level.

habit_description: Dioecious shrub or tree, 3--5 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 2--4 cm long, 7 or 8 whorls per cm | peduncle 7--13 mm long | bracts thickened | bracteoles obtuse, body and protuberance not distinguishable, the whole divided into 3--5 tightly packed, thickened bodies
flower_description: anther c. 0.8 mm long, much broader than long
fruit_description: Cones occasionally with sterile apex to 5 mm long | cone body 26--55 mm long, 14--18 mm diam. | Samara 5--7.5 mm long
habitat_description: Grows on rocky hillsides.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where it occurs on Mount Singleton.
notes: More tree-like than Allocasuarina campestris.

habit_description: Shrub c. 1 m high, rarely to 2.5 m
stem_description: Branchlet articles 7--12 mm long, 0.7--0.8 mm diam., phyllichnia angular | 0.3--0.6 mm long, occasionally marcescent
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 0.5--4.5 cm long | bracteoles obtuse
flower_description: anther 0.6--0.8 mm long
fruit_description: Cones on peduncle 8--14 mm long, cone body 10--26 mm long, 9--15 mm diam. | Samara dark brown
habitat_description: Forms a dense low closed heath.
distribution_description: Endemic to Queensland, where known only from the windswept south-facing upper slopes of Mount Coolum.

habit_description: Intricate shrub 0.3--2 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes of 1--4 whorls at apex of branchlet, 1--5 mm long | peduncle slender, 2--7 mm long | bracteoles thin, acuminate, occasionally with hooked tip, protuberance diverging low on bracteole body, with pyramidal portion nearly as long as bracteole body and with 2--8 mm long coarse yellowish awn with a deciduous hooked tip
flower_description: anther 0.4--0.6 mm long
fruit_description: Cones shortly cylindrical to globose, as long as broad, spiny | cone body 8--20 mm long, 8--15 mm diam. | Samara 5.0--6.0 (rarely to 10) mm long
habitat_description: Found in heath on lateritic foothills and sandplain.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where widespread from the Murchison River south to near Albany and E to Esperance.

habit_description: Dioecious shrub c. 1.7 m high
stem_description: Branchlets spreading, twisted, to 10 cm long
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 5--9 mm long, dense | bracts inconspicuous | bracteoles obtuse, protuberance obtuse, shorter than bracteole body
flower_description: anther 1.1--1.2 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical, sessile, cone body 10--15 mm long, c. 10 mm diam. | Samara 5.5--6 mm long, mid-brown
habitat_description: Found in dense tall heath in loam soil on granite.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where known only from two populations in and near a Nature Reserve W of Lake King.
notes: Similar to Allocasuarina globosa, but readily distinguished by the shorter articles with median furrow down the phyllichnia and the fewer, broader, thicker-textured teeth. It further differs from that species in the undivided bracteole protuberance on the cone.

common_name: Forest Oak, Rose Sheoak, Forest Sheoak, Baker's Oak.
habit_description: Usually dioecious tree 5--20 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 0.5--3 cm long, 7--12 whorls per cm | peduncle 8--30 mm long | bracts inconspicuous | bracteoles acute, protuberance divided into 8--12 small tubercles slightly shorter than or as long as bracteole body
flower_description: anther 0.5--0.6 mm long
fruit_description: Cones shortly cylindrical or barrel-shaped, warty, occasionally densely pubescent, pendent or spreading | cone body 15--33 mm long, 12--25 mm diam. | Samara 7--10 mm long, mid to dark brown
habitat_description: Grows on coastal hills and ranges as understorey in open forest to tall open forest, in a wide range of soils.
distribution_description: Occurs from the McIlwraith Range, Queensland, south to Macquarie Pass and Jenolan Caves, New South Wales.
notes: In north Queensland material, phyllichnia are often more angular. Generally grows in higher-nutrient soils and in moister forest than Allocasuarina littoralis.

habit_description: Erect to spreading shrub, 0.5--3 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 3--8 cm long, 8 whorls per cm | bracteoles slender, acute or acuminate with small mucro, usually pungent, protuberance nearly as long as bracteole body and very similar in size and shape
flower_description: anther 1--1.2 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical to barrel-shaped, pubescent, sessile, cone body 15--50 mm long, 14--20 mm diam. | Samara 8--10 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in tall heathland, often in skeletal soils.
distribution_description: Endemic to Western Australia, where it occurs from Albany east to beyond Esperance and in the Stirling Range.
notes: The long spreading leaf teeth are distinctive amongst Western Australian species.

common_name: Drooping Sheoak, Coast Sheoak, Sheoak, Hill Oak.
habit_description: Tree 4--10 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 3--12 cm long, 2.5--4 whorls per cm | bracts with long slender mucro | bracteoles broadly acute to acute, often pungent, protuberance fused with body or inconspicuous and only about as long as bracts
flower_description: anther 1.2--2.5 mm long
fruit_description: Cones cylindrical to barrel-shaped, sessile or on peduncle to 10 mm long, cone body 20--50 mm long, 17--30 mm diam. | Samara 7--12 mm long, very dark brown
habitat_description: Grows in usually grassy woodland, forming pure stands or amongst eucalypts; also on rocky sea-coasts and dry rocky hills and ridges inland.
distribution_description: Occurs from near Cobar, New South Wales, southwards and extending to the coast on shale patches near Sydney and on the south coast, widespread through Victoria, except in the northwest, west to the Flinders and Gawler Ranges, western Eyre Peninsula and Kangaroo Island, South Australia, and in Tasmania from Launceston down the east coast to Kingston and the Tasman Peninsula.

habit_description: Shrub 0.5--2 m high
inflorescence_description: Male spikes often moniliform, 1--3.5 cm long, 5--7 whorls per cm
flower_description: anther 0.7--0.9 mm long
fruit_description: Cones on peduncle 2--15 mm long, cone body 10--25 mm long, 6--11 mm diam | Samara 4.0--5.5 mm long, black
habitat_description: Grows in heath and on rocky outcrops.
distribution_description: Endemic to Tasmania, where it occurs from the western lowlands to central and southeastern highlands, and also on King Island.
notes: There is variation between populations in length of articles and in shape and amount of overlapping of teeth, and this may prove worthy of taxonomic recognition. Forms close to the sea are coarser and there is a fairly well-defined form with short slender articles on the highlands from Cradle Mountain to Lake St Clair and Lake Margaret.

habit_description: Tree 10--20 m high, frequently producing suckers
bark_description: Bark finely fissured or scaly, grey-brown
stem_description: Branchlets drooping in vigorous specimens, spreading in depauperate specimens, to 25 cm long
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 1.3--5 cm long, 6--10 whorls per cm | peduncle 1--14 mm long | bracteoles acute
flower_description: anther 0.8--1.1 mm long
fruit_description: Cones ferruginous-pubescent when young, nearly glabrous at maturity | cone body 13--18 mm, occasionally to 25 mm long, 10--16 mm diam. | Samara 6--10.5 mm long
vegetative_reproduction_description: May form pure woodland stands; clonal stands occur
habitat_description: Usually found in clayey grey or brown soils with calcareous nodules near the surface.
distribution_description: Occurs from Clermont, Queensland, south to Temora, New South Wales. Some intergradation with Casuarina pauper occurs in the area from Bourke to west of Condobolin, New South Wales.
notes: May form pure woodland stands; clonal stands occur.

common_name: River Oak, River Sheoak, Creek Oak, Fire Oak.
habit_description: Tree 15--35 m high
bark_description: Bark finely fissured and scaly, grey-brown
stem_description: Branchlets drooping in vigorous specimens, erect in depauperate specimens
inflorescence_description: Male spikes 0.4--4 cm long, 11--13 whorls per cm | peduncle 2--9 mm long | bracteoles broadly acute to acute

habit_description: Shrub or tree to 15 m high, glabrous

distribution_description: Occurs from Cape York to near Mareeba, Qld.

habit_description: Slender erect glabrous annual to 19 cm

inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a dense cylindrical spike

habit_description: Dense, broom-like perennial to 45 cm, glabrous or puberulent at base

habit_description: Sedge-like glabrous perennial to 55 cm

habit_description: Erect annual to 80 cm high, glabrous, rarely sparsely puberulent

notes: A polymorphic species. Typical specimens are slender. In the arid zone there is a robust variant distinguished by sometimes pubescent cocci and relatively short sepals. Two other variants occur in the tropics, one distinguished by reduced leaves, another by small globular cocci.

habit_description: Spreading, glabrous to puberulent perennial to 50 cm high, sometimes higher
leaf_description: Leaves linear to narrowly obovate, to 45 mm long

habit_description: Glabrous or pubescent perennial to 70 cm

notes: A polymorphic species which as treated here includes Stackhousia aspericocca Schuch., S. huegelii Endl. and S. pubescens A.Rich.

habit_description: Glabrous perennial or annual, to 55 cm high
stem_description: Stems erect to ascending, often branched above

notes: The species has two races, one perennial (including the type of Stackhousia muricata ) and spread across southern semi-arid Australia and in eastern N.S.W., the other annual (equivalent to Stackhousia occidentalis Domin) confined to arid S.A. and W.A.

habit_description: Glabrous broom-like perennial to 95 cm
stem_description: Stems erect or ascending, branched above
leaf_description: Leaves reduced to scales

habitat_description: Grows in moist sand, often peaty, and on sandstone, in low heath on swamp margins and on coastal flats, rarely on hillsides.
distribution_description: Occurs along the E coast from south-eastern Qld to eastern Vic.

habitat_description: Grows in alpine herbfields and subalpine grasslands, often in small depressions or associated with margins of bogs and swamps.
distribution_description: Occurs in the Australian Alps in N.S.W. and Vic., and in Tasmania.

habit_description: Glabrous broom-like perennial to 60 cm
leaf_description: Leaves reduced to scales
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a lax one-sided spike | bracts 3--6 at each node, ovate, entire or serrulate

fruit_description: Cocci 1--3, obloid-ellipsoidal, 2.5--4 mm long, deeply rugose to densely tuberculate, with two lips of bony endocarp at base
habitat_description: Grows in sand, gravelly loam or sandy clay, in mallee heath.
distribution_description: In the S wheatbelt and S coastal regions of south-western W.A.
notes: This species, treated here in its traditional broad sense, encompasses three taxa. Typical Stackhousia scoparia has tribracteate flowers arranged singly, hyalescent serrulate bracts and deeply rugose-tuberculate cocci; it occurs throughout the drier wheatbelt. An unnamed taxon with clustered flowers, entire opaque bracts and densely tuberculate cocci occurs E of Ravensthorpe. Another unnamed taxon near the Stirling Range has flowers arranged singly and entire caudate bracts, sepals and corolla lobes; its cocci are unknown.

habit_description: Glabrous perennial to over 45 cm high

habit_description: Glabrous perennial to 70 cm high

habit_description: Glabrous perennial to 80 cm
stem_description: Stems erect or ascending, branched above
leaf_description: Leaves narrowly linear to broadly ovate, sometimes scale-like, to 20 mm long

seed_description: Seed c. 0.8 mm long

leaf_description: Leaves 1--2.6 cm long, 1-veined, glabrous | lamina linear, flattened, c. 0.2 mm wide

seed_description: Seed c. 0.9 mm long

leaf_description: Leaves 1--2.3 cm long, 1-veined, glabrous | lamina linear-subulate, keeled, c. 0.5 mm wide
inflorescence_description: Scape straight, 0.7--2.5 cm long | Spike erect, symmetric, broadly ovate, 3--6 mm long, 3--4 mm wide, remaining compact
flower_description: Anthers 0.6--0.7 mm long
seed_description: Seed 0.7--0.9 mm long

inflorescence_type_description: glomerules; terminal; solitary; in leaf axils

leaf_description: Leaves shortly petiolate, narrowly elliptic to narrowly obovate, 5--20 mm long, entire to remotely denticulate, scurfy lepidote below, sparsely scurfy above
flower_description: Male flowers in small glomerules in terminal axils | Female flowers solitary or paired in leaf axils
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles scurfy, shortly stipitate (c. 1 mm), free to base, flat, deltoid, 3--6 mm long, acute, toothed, several short spine-like appendages present on each face (these sometimes united at their base to form a spiny semicircular rim)
seed_description: Seed semicircular | radicle lateral, erect
distribution_description: Found in central and eastern N.S.W., south-eastern Qld and northern Vic.

habit_description: Erect rounded annual herb, c. 20 cm high, monoecious
leaf_description: Leaves thin with a scaly sheen on both surfaces, broadly elliptic to rhombic | lamina 10--15 mm long, obtuse | margin sinuate dentate | base cuneate and passing into a petiole | c. 5 mm long
flower_description: Male flowers in glomerules arranged in continuous spikes, c. 20 mm long, 5 mm diam., with scattered female flowers | Female flowers congested in distal axils
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles sessile to very shortly stipitate, rhomboid, c. 2.5 mm long and wide, lower half fused, campanulate, biconvex with prominent reticulate veins from which arise on either surface 5--12 slender spines, 0.5--1.5 mm long, distal half flat with central triangular lobe c. 1 mm long and, at its base, 2--4 small acicular lateral lobes
seed_description: Seed circular | radicle lateral, erect
distribution_description: Known from the type locality area in the Pilbara region of north-western W.A. and near Carnarvon and Geraldton.

habit_description: Rounded annual or short-lived perennial to 30 cm high, monoecious
leaf_description: Leaves elliptic, broadly elliptic or ovate, 1--2 cm long, acute to obtuse, entire to sinuate dentate (or rarely deeply serrate), narrowed at base into a short petiole or sessile, scurfy on both surfaces

fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles sessile, fused, broadly ellipsoidal, to globular 4--6 mm long, rarely to 8 mm, shortly apiculate, inflated, epidermal covering thin, loosely scurfy, supported on a network of fibrous veins | utricle in centre of bracteoles, cavity compressed elliptic, with a thin woody wall
seed_description: Seed erect, broadly elliptic | radicle lateral, erect
habitat_description: Occurs on margins of salt lakes and in dry, somewhat saline areas.
distribution_description: Found from southern N.T. south-east to western N.S.W.

habit_description: Erect shrub to 1 m high, predominantly dioecious
leaf_description: Leaves narrowly elliptic to orbicular, entire obtuse or rounded at apex, sometimes conduplicate and recurved when dry, with scaly sheen on both surfaces | lamina 7--25 mm long | petiole 2--3 mm long
flower_description: Male flowers in small disjunct glomerules forming spikes or panicles | Female flowers in well-spaced clusters forming slender spikes
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles on a slender stipe to 10 mm long | valves reniform, cordate, to 5 mm long and 10 mm wide, thin, appressed, joined at base to form a compressed turbinate tube | appendages absent
seed_description: Seed with lateral, erect radicle
distribution_description: Found in semi-arid areas of southern Australia and southern N.T.

habit_description: Spreading annual or short-lived perennial to 30 cm high, monoecious
leaf_description: Leaves thin, obovate, sinuate-dentate, scaly on both surfaces | apex rounded | base cuneate | lamina 10--20 mm long | petiole slender
flower_description: Male flowers in distal axils | perianth glabrescent | Female flowers numerous in scattered glomerules
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles, when immature oblong and shortly stipitate | the stipe eventually becoming spongy | when mature narrowly cylindrical, 3--5 mm long, of two distinct portions, lower third to half a cylindrical firm spongy straw-coloured stipe, upper portion a somewhat compressed green to straw-coloured thin walled, longitudinally nerved tube, obtuse
seed_description: Seed obovate | radicle lateral and slightly exserted
habitat_description: Occurs principally in white sand.
distribution_description: Found in central Australia from south-eastern N.T. to far north-western N.S.W.

habit_description: Sprawling herb branching from base, to 60 cm high, monoecious
leaf_description: Leaves thin, narrow to broadly rhomboid, 15--30 mm long, coarsely serrate, shortly petiolate | upper surface glabrescent | lower surface somewhat scurfy
inflorescence_description: bracteoles rhomboid, acute, c. 2--5 mm long, flat or convex, connate in lower half, thin or somewhat thickened with age, scurfy pubescent | margin entire in lower half | 2--4-toothed in upper half
flower_description: Male flowers in subterminal clusters | Female flowers in axillary clusters
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles shortly stipitate the stipe sometimes thickening with age
seed_description: Seed circular | radicle lateral, erect
habitat_description: Occurs around lakes or dams, also coastal.
distribution_description: Found in southern Australia; considered naturalised in S Africa.

habit_description: Rounded annual or short-lived perennial to 30 cm high, monoecious
leaf_description: Leaves thin scurfy on both surfaces, sessile, elliptic to obovate, 10 mm long, rarely to 30 mm, obtuse, entire or weakly sinuate-dentate, cuneate at base
flower_description: Male flowers in glomerules in terminal axils | Female flowers in axillary clusters
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles stipitate, turbinate to narrowly turbinate, lower two-thirds united into a flattened narrowly deltoid tube 2--3 mm long, upper one-third of free appressed semicircular herbaceous reticulate lobes shortly 3-toothed | stipe slender or thickened, equal in length to tube
seed_description: Seed circular | radicle erect, prominently projecting
habitat_description: Grows in heavy soil on plains and along creeks.
distribution_description: Found in south-eastern N.T., central and north-eastern S.A., north-western N.S.W. and in Victoria on the Murray River floodplain near Winlaton.

habit_description: Erect short-lived perennial to 1 m high, monoecious, thinly lepidote to scaly tomentose all over
leaf_description: Leaves sessile, thin, broadly elliptic to broadly ovate, 1--3 cm long, sinuate to bluntly toothed or sinuate-lobed, acute to obtuse | base cuneate to rounded
flower_description: Flowers in mixed clusters, axillary or forming interrupted spikes
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles sessile or shortly stipitate, appressed, free except at the short, broadly cuneate base, narrowly to broadly triangular, 4--8 mm long, entire or toothed at base, almost glabrous to tomentose, smooth or with 1 or 2 tubercles on either side near base
seed_description: Seed circular | radicle erect
distribution_description: Found from central S.A. to south-eastern N.T., south-western Qld and north-western N.S.W., usually around dams, creeks or bores in saline soil.

inflorescence_type_description: glomerules; terminal; spike; panicle; in upper axils
habit_description: Erect or decumbent shrub to 1 m high, predominantly dioecious
leaf_description: Leaves elliptic to oblong or obovate, acute, obtuse, or rounded, usually entire, attenuate at base, sparsely to densely scaly, somewhat green | lamina 5--25 mm long, 3--15 mm wide
flower_description: Male flowers in disjunct or contiguous glomerules arranged in a terminal spike or panicle 2--4 cm long | Female flowers 2 to many in upper axils
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles sessile with stipe 1--3 mm long | valves free or fused to above seed, orbicular to oval-triangular or rhomboid, obtuse, acute, or mucronate, 4--13 mm long and wide, entire or dentate towards apex, cuneate to cordate at base | appendages thin-walled and bladder-like attached to base of valves, or fused to one another below bracteoles, or to the bracteole margin, sometimes absent
distribution_description: A highly variable species found in a variety of habitats in southern arid and semi-arid Australia in all mainland states.
notes: There are 8 subspecies.

habit_description: Erect shrub to 60 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves narrowly elliptic to orbicular or obovate, obtuse to rounded, 5--15 mm long 3--8 mm wide, entire
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles sessile or very shortly stipitate | valves fused for 1 mm above base, orbicular to rhomboid or triangular, obtuse to acute, to 5 mm long and wide, entire or slightly denticulate, truncate or slightly cordate at base | bladder-appendages small or absent
seed_description: Seed medium brown
habitat_description: Grows in mixed scrub and woodland over limestone or loam.
distribution_description: Found from the western Nullarbor Plain in S.A. to Norseman and Kellerberrin in W.A.

inflorescence_description: Bracteoles attenuate, entire
habitat_description: Grows in calcareous soils.
distribution_description: Found in far western N.S.W., central to eastern S.A., and southern N.T.

habit_description: Erect shrub to 80 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves elliptic to obovate, rounded at apex, 8--15 mm long, 2--8 mm wide, entire
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles sessile or on stipe 1 mm long | valves cordate-triangular to orbicular, rounded or obtuse, truncate to cordate at base, entire | bladder appendages absent
seed_description: Seed dark brown
habitat_description: Grows on sandy plains and margins of salt pans.
distribution_description: Found near the west coast of W.A. from south of Geraldton to Shark Bay.

habit_description: Rounded shrub to 80 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves obovate, rounded to obtuse, 10--30 mm long, 4--8 mm wide, entire
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles sessile or on stipe 1 mm long | valves broadly orbicular, obtuse or slightly mucronate, to 9 mm long, 12 mm wide, fused up to 2 mm above base, entire or with a few teeth above widest point, truncate at base | bladder appendages almost equal to valves, attached near base and often fused to each other below valves and around stipe
seed_description: Seed light brown
habitat_description: Grows on arid plains and silty or clay-loam soils.
distribution_description: Found in central and western N.S.W., north-western Vic., south-western Qld west to southern N.T. and central S.A.

habit_description: Rounded shrub 30--50 cm high and wide
stem_description: branches finer than those of other subspecies
leaf_description: Leaves sessile, narrowly elliptic, acute, 10--15 mm long, 2--3 mm wide, entire, attenuate at base
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles orbicular, 3--8 mm long and wide | valves soft and somewhat membranous, entire, rounded to truncate at base | bladder appendages smaller than valves or absent
