habitat_description: Grows in heavy red and grey clay soil.
distribution_description: Found on the southern Riverine Plain of N.S.W. and northern Vic.

habit_description: Decumbent shrub 30--50 cm high and wide
leaf_description: Leaves narrowly elliptic to ovate, obtuse or slightly retuse, usually entire | lamina 8--15 mm long, 5--8 mm wide | petiole 2 mm long
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles with stipe 2--3 mm long but appearing subsessile due to bladder appendages | valves fused to above seed, broadly orbicular to rhomboid (appearing spherical), acute to mucronate, to 10 mm long and wide, entire or sparsely dentate, attenuate at base | bladder appendages exceeding valves and obscuring them, fused to near upper margin of valves and to each other below
seed_description: Seed light brown
habitat_description: Grows on stony slopes and ridges of hills and occasionally on plains.
distribution_description: Found in southern N.T., central S.A. and western N.S.W.

habit_description: Erect shrub to 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves narrowly elliptic, acute or obtuse, 10--15 mm long, 4--6 mm wide, entire
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles sessile | valves free to base, orbicular, obtuse to rounded, 7--11 mm long, 6--10 mm wide, entire or with 2 large teeth above widest point, truncate to slightly cordate at base | bladder appendages smaller than bracteoles or absent from one or both valves
seed_description: Seed brown
habitat_description: Grows in sands or silty loams.
distribution_description: Found in north-western Vic., southern N.T. and central W.A.

habit_description: Rounded shrub to 50 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves narrowly elliptic, 20--30 mm long, 3--5 mm wide
fruit_description: Fruiting bracteoles 5--10 mm long and wide
seed_description: Seeds not dimorphic, all dark brown
habitat_description: Grows in heavy red and grey clay soil.
distribution_description: Found in the northern Riverine plain near the Lachlan River, N.S.W.

profile_author: K.A. Shepherd, K.R. Thiele, J. Sampson, D. Coates, M. Byrne
habit_description: Subdioecious perennial shrub forming rounded mounds 0.4--1 m high, with divaricate, smooth or sometimes shallowly striate woody branches
leaf_description: leaves and flowers with an indumentum of collapsed, vesicular hairs that fuse to form a thin, pale sheen | Leaves alternate, scattered along branches and in small, dense clusters | petiole absent or to 0.3 mm long | lamina elliptic or rhombic to trullate, rarely hastate, 0.8--6.5 mm long, 0.9--3.2 (-5.3) mm wide, flat or gently undulating, with a rounded to obtuse apex | margins entire or sinuate to shallowly dentate | concolorous
inflorescence_description: terminal glomerules or short panicles 3--10 mm long, 2.9--4 mm wide (often with scattered female flowers further down the flowering branch) | bracteoles absent | bracteoles 2, sessile or with a short stipe 0.8--0.9 mm long
flower_description: Male flowers in dense | perianth 5-lobed | the lobes elliptic, 1.5--1.9 mm long, 0.6--0.9 mm wide, fused in the lower half, with a rounded apex | stamens 5 | the filaments 1--1.8 mm long, 0.2--0.3 mm wide | the anthers oblong, c. 0.4 mm long, c. 0.45 mm wide, yellow, becoming reddish with age | pollen yellow | Female flowers solitary, axillary (often present in small numbers on plants with mostly male flowers) | perianth absent | stigmas 2, filiform, 0.6--1.5 mm long, minutely plumose
fruit_description: the valves obovate, 1.5--4.4 mm long, 0.9--3.7 mm wide, equal in length, fused for lower 1/2--2/3, sinuate to dentate at apex, with outer surface smooth or later developing finger-like appendages | Fruiting bracteoles 0.7--1.8 mm long with a thickened peg-like base or sessile | valves broadly obovate to fan-shaped, 4.5--7 mm long, 4.0--7.4 mm wide, becoming indurated with a swollen, spongy outer layer | outer surface smooth or with finger-like appendages on both sides | apex broadly dentate
seed_description: Seeds rounded to broadly ovate in outline, brown, smooth, 0.9--1.4 mm long, 1.0--1.4 mm wide
habitat_description: Populations are restricted to a palaeodrainage channel associated with near-surface uranium mineralisation (Clarke et al. 2012), with one situated directly above the subsurface Yeelirrie uranium orebody. The species constitutes the dominant component of a vegetation community described by Western Botanical (2011) as ‘Atriplex sp. Yeelirrie Station shrubland on calcrete (CApS)’, which primarily occurs on self-mulching, cracking clay in depressions confined to clay flats over a calcrete hardpan. Plants form a low shrubland to 0.6 m high, sometimes with scattered, emergent shrubs of Lycium australe to 1.5 m high, and Melaleuca xerophila to 4 m high.
distribution_description: Yeelirrie Station in the Murchison IBRA region in Western Australia’s Eremaean Botanical Province (Department of the Environment 2013).

common_name: Fivehorn Smotherweed, Five-horn Smotherweed, Five-hook Bassia, Thorn Orache.
habit_description: Erect annual to 1 m high, usually much-branched
stem_description: Branches slender with thin cottony indumentum when young
leaf_description: Leaves sessile, usually linear to narrowly oblanceolate, 5--20 mm long, 1--3 mm wide, flat or concave above/convex below, sparsely cottony or glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in axillary clusters of 2 or 3
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth depressed-spherical, pilose, 5-lobed, with 5 uncinately incurved spines arising from base of lobes (the tepals being hemispherical, c. 1 mm long, each with a hooked spine c. 1.5 mm long arising from near centre)
seed_description: Seed elliptic, c. 1.5 mm long, horizontal, remaining enclosed by fruiting perianth when shed
habitat_description: Weed of drainage areas.
distribution_description: Native to eastern Europe and Asia. Occurs in a small area of north-western Victoria (Mildura-Red Cliffs area).

common_name: Kochia, Belvedere, Summer Cypress, Burning Bush, Tumbleweed, and many more.
habit_description: Erect herb to 1.5 (-2) m high
distribution_description: Native from eastern Europe to temperate Asia. Naturalised in Western Australia and South Australia. Doubtfully naturalised in Tasmania (see Baker et al. 2019).
notes: Can become a serious weed. It competes with pasture grasses and crops and is toxic to livestock (Kochia (Bassia scoparia) in NSW WeedWise, accessed 28 October 2025); see also Bassia scoparia Weeds of Australia Fact Sheet (2016; accessed 28 October 2025).

flowers_per_inflorescence_description: Flowers solitary or in clusters of up to 8
habit_description: Biennial herb with stem decumbent to erect and up to 2 m high, sometimes purplish
leaf_description: Basal leaves rosetted | lamina ovate to rhombic or spathulate, 5--20 cm long, 3--6 cm wide | petiole slender, half to about as long as lamina | cauline leaves smaller and becoming almost sessile toward inflorescence
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in clusters of up to 8 | Perianth lobes oblong, 1--2.5 mm long, incurved
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth with segments corky at least toward base, adjacent fruits fused and falling as a unit
distribution_description: Naturalised mainly in near-coastal areas in South Australia, New South Wales, Victoria and Tasmania. Native from Azores and western Europe to the Mediterranean and India (Plants of the World Online, accessed 17 February 2025).

common_name: Wild Beet, Sea Beet, Wild Spinach.
flowers_per_inflorescence_description: Flowers solitary or in clusters of up to 4
habit_description: Biennial herb with slender taproot
stem_description: Stems decumbent to erect, to 75 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves rosetted (basal) and cauline, glossy, often tinged with red | lamina ovate to rhombic or spathulate, to c. 5 (-10) cm long, 3--6 mm wide, glabrous | petiole slender, half to equal length of lamina | The cauline leaves smaller and becoming almost sessile toward inflorescence
flower_description: Flowers solitary or in clusters of up to 4 (often 3 or 4) within the inflorescence, green | Perianth lobes narrowly oblong
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth indurated, united in clusters and falling as a whole | pericarp hard
habitat_description: Near-coastal saltmarsh communities, sandy beach areas, disturbed weedy areas, near brackish streams and lakes on heavier soils further inland, usually near settlement.
distribution_description: Recorded from coastal South Australia and Victoria, central coastal New South Wales and south-eastern Tasmania, but probably more widespread. Native to Europe.

common_name: Beet, Common Beet, includes cultivars e.g. Beetroot, Silverbeet, Sugarbeet.
flowers_per_inflorescence_description: Flowers in clusters of up to 8
flower_description: Flowers in clusters of up to 8 within the inflorescence
distribution_description: Recorded as naturalised in Victoria where it is occasionally found along riverbanks near settlements. Native from western Europe to the Mediterranean and India (Plants of the World Online, accessed 17 February 2025).

common_name: Fat Hen, White Goosefoot, Lamb's Quarters, Common Lambsquarters, Blue Weed, Pigweed, Wild Spinach, Baconweed, Mealweed.
profile_author: Paul G. Wilson, P.G. Kodela, P.S. Green
habit_description: Erect annual to c. 1 m high, grey-farinose throughout

flower_description: Perianth lobes 5, 0.5--2.5 mm long, dorsally keeled, green, farinose

habitat_description: A weed of agriculture (e.g. crops) favouring richly nitrogenous soil; also other disturbed sites, including roadsides, cleared areas, wasteland and bushland. On Norfolk Is., a weed of disturbed soils (Green 1994: 83).
distribution_description: Found in all mainland Australian States and Territories as well as Tas. and Norfolk Is., but rare in the tropics; cosmopolitan. (W.A., N.T., S.A., Qld, N.S.W., N.Is., A.C.T., Vic., Tas.).

habit_description: Erect annual to 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves with slender petiole | the lamina thin, narrowly ovate to ovate or rarely hastate, 2--10 cm long, entire or coarsely toothed, glabrescent above, mealy below when young
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a terminal panicle with slender densely flowered branches | axis villous with tubular hairs
flower_description: Flowers bisexual, sessile, spherical, c. 1 mm diam | Perianth almost glabrous, 5-lobed | the lobes imbricate, broadly elliptic to circular, yellow-green, ciliate | Stamens 5 | disc absent
fruit_description: Pericarp membranous, papillate, adherent
seed_description: Seed horizontal, lenticular, c. 1 mm diam., rounded on margin | testa brown to black, minutely puncticulate
habitat_description: Grows on seasonally waterlogged black-soil plains.
distribution_description: Found in south-eastern Qld and north-eastern N.S.W.
notes: First described from Switzerland where it had been introduced in wool; it is a native of Australia.

common_name: Queensland Bluebush, Golden Goosefoot, Swamp Bluebush, Bluebush, Northern Bluebush.
habit_description: Soft-wooded bluish grey shrub to 2 m high
leaf_description: Leaves with slender petiole c. 1 cm long | the lamina oblong-elliptic to hastate, mostly 2--4 (-6) cm long, the basal lobes and apex rounded | upper surface glabrescent | lower surface with a thin, mealy, grey to very pale yellow indumentum
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a broad panicle c. 10 cm long with ovoid to cylindrical branches | axis villous with tubular hairs

habit_description: Weak intricately branched shrub to 1 m high

seed_description: Seed lenticular with rounded margin, c. 1.5 mm diam. | testa black, prominently reticulate with a honeycomb matrix
habitat_description: Usually growing in light often calcareous soil.
distribution_description: Found from south-western N.S.W. and north-western Vic. westwards to south-eastern W.A.

habit_description: Annual or perennial herb, prostrate to erect, branching from base, mealy
leaf_description: Leaves opposite or alternate, subsessile or prominently petiolate | the lamina elliptic, 5--20 mm long, deltate, hastate or orbicular

habit_description: Erect perennial c. 20 cm high with slender branches

seed_description: Seed c. 1.5 mm diam

habit_description: Erect, rounded, much-branched herb to 20 cm high

seed_description: Seed c. 1.5 mm diam

habit_description: Intricately branched prostrate to decumbent perennial, not noticeably fetid

inflorescence_description: Inflorescence short, scarcely exceeding leaves
flower_description: Flowers c. 1 mm diam | Perianth covered with white vesicular hairs
seed_description: Seed c. 1 mm diam

habit_description: Erect perennial to 40 cm high

fruit_description: Pericarp membranous or slightly succulent

habit_description: Erect annual to 1.5 m high

leaf_description: Leaves elliptic, undulate or obtusely lobed | lamina 10--20 mm long | petiole somewhat shorter
flower_description: Flowers in compact clusters of 3--7 in paniculately-arranged spikes, bisexual and female | Tepals 4, erect, c. 1 mm long, united below, sometimes horizontally keeled, glabrous to hirsute, inflated in fruit | stamen 1 or absent | styles 2 | Tepals and seed shed as unit
fruit_description: Pericarp dull, somewhat adherent
seed_description: Seed subglobular, horizontal to erect, 0.5 mm diam. | embryo semicircular | radicle superior
notes: There are two subspecies.

inflorescence_description: Inflorescence of long slender spikes often with disjunct glomerules | bracts inconspicuous
flower_description: Tepals glabrous or almost so, ciliate, rounded on back
fruit_description: Pericarp dull, rarely glossy
seed_description: Seed horizontal or slightly oblique
habitat_description: Usually grows in skeletal soil.
distribution_description: Found in north-western W.A., southern N.T., central Qld, and northern N.S.W.

inflorescence_description: Inflorescence much-branched | bracts smaller than or exceeding flower clusters
flower_description: Tepals hirsute, rounded or slightly keeled
fruit_description: Pericarp dull
seed_description: Seed oblique to erect
habitat_description: Usually grows in skeletal soil on rocky slopes
distribution_description: Found in western Qld, northern S.A., NW and central W.A. and southern N.T.

habit_description: Erect annual to 30 cm high, aromatic, moderately pilose all over with weak gland-tipped and stiffer simple hairs
leaf_description: Leaves thin, ovate to elliptic, entire to sinuate or obtusely lobed | lamina 10--20 mm long | petiole slender, c. ½ length of lamina
flower_description: Flowers sessile in small clusters forming a paniculate inflorescence with flexuose branches | Perianth spherical, c. 1 mm high | Tepals 4, erect, shortly pilose | Stamens 0--2 | tepals navicular, c. 1.5 mm long, free
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth herbaceous | Pericarp transparent, adherent
seed_description: Seed erect, lenticular, c. 0.6 mm diam., minutely puncticulate
habitat_description: Grows on rocky outcrops and at the base of breakaways.
distribution_description: Found in central W.A.

habit_description: Annual 10--30 cm high with decumbent to ascending branches, pubescent
leaf_description: Leaves soon falling | lamina elliptic, 1--2 cm long, obtuse to acuminate, with 2--4 pairs of prominent lobes | petiole shorter than lamina
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence an erect spike of crowded 7-flowered cymes, 5--25 cm long, 4 mm diam., sessile in branch axils
flower_description: Terminal flower of cyme bisexual | tepals 3, hooded, c. 1 mm long, united in lower half into an indurated papillose tube | stamen 1 | styles 2 | Lateral flowers female, otherwise similar to but smaller than terminal flower | tepal limbs with horizontal hyaline wings | Tepals and seed shed as unit
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth cartilaginous, firmly attached
seed_description: Seed erect, broadly pear-shaped, c. 0.6 mm long | embryo vertical | radicle superior
habitat_description: Occurring in saline or calcareous soil, often around salt lakes.
distribution_description: Found in central Australia.

habit_description: Prostrate to ascending annual with several stems, pilosulose with simple and glandular hairs
leaf_description: Leaves elliptic, obtuse, entire, often undulate | lamina 0.5--1.5 cm long | petiole short
flower_description: Flower clusters in a narrow cylindrical spike to 15 cm long, subsessile or on thick pedicels c. 0.1 mm long | Terminal flower of cluster bisexual or female | tepals 3, glabrous, c. 1 mm long in fruit, free but persistent | the limb rounded, inflated | claw broad | stamen 1 | style 1 | Lateral flowers similar to terminal but female | Tepals and seed shed as unit
fruit_description: Pericarp minutely granulate-papillose
seed_description: Seed compressed-globular, c. 0.5 mm high | embryo semicircular, oblique or erect | radicle inferior
habitat_description: Usually associated with gypseous or calcareous soils, frequently around salt lakes.
distribution_description: Found from north-western Qld. through southern N.T. and westwards to Shark Bay area of W.A.

habit_description: Prostrate to ascending annual branching from base, aromatic
stem_description: Stems pilosulose with slender and sessile to shortly stipitate gland-tipped hairs
leaf_description: Leaves elliptic, obtuse, entire to slightly undulate, glandular-puberulous all over and pilosulose below along veins | lamina c. 10 mm long | petiole slender c. 5 mm long
flower_description: Flowers in compact axillary clusters | Tepals 5, erect, united to near apex | Stamen 0 or 1 | tepals firmly united to apex, toothed or lacerate on margin, not rostrate
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth cartilaginous, white or black, very broadly obtriangular in side view, flat above or the lobes ascending, c. 2 mm wide | Pericarp transparent, adherent
seed_description: Seed erect, lenticular, c. 0.7 mm diam
habitat_description: Usually in deep red sand.
distribution_description: Found in south-western Qld, western N.S.W., northern S.A. and southern N.T.

habit_description: Short-lived prostrate perennial to 60 cm diam., almost glabrous to sparsely pilose with simple and gland-tipped hairs
leaf_description: Leaves with lamina narrowly oblong to narrowly elliptic, 10--15 mm long, obtuse, entire | petiole c. half length of lamina
flower_description: Flowers in axillary glomerules 3--5 mm diam | Terminal flower of glomerule male | tepals 3, shortly united | stamens 2, pistillode minute | Lateral flowers of glomerule female | tepals 2, in fruit c. 1.3 mm long, with an inflated limb, the short broad claws united | styles 2, short | Tepals and seed shed as unit
fruit_description: Pericarp adherent, smooth
seed_description: Seed erect, lenticular, c. 0.6 mm long | embryo semicircular around lower two-thirds of seed | radicle and cotyledons erect
distribution_description: Found in southern Qld.

habit_description: Spreading perennial to 1.5 m high, branching at base
leaf_description: Leaves opposite or subopposite, triangular to broadly hastate, entire, somewhat leathery and resinous when dry, glabrous or with scattered vitreous vesicular hairs when young | lamina 10--25 mm long | apex rounded and often apiculate | lateral lobes short and obtuse | petiole slender
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a slender racemose panicle with scattered glomerules
flower_description: flowers sessile or subsessile | Tepals oblong-obovate, thickened and hooded at apex, red and somewhat succulent in fruit | Stamens 1 or 2
fruit_description: Fruit a berry, depressed-globular, clasped by persistent tepals, c. 3 mm diam
seed_description: Seed 1.5 mm diam., radially rugulose
distribution_description: Found in Vic., A.C.T. eastern Qld and N.S.W., in gullies, on rocky slopes and plains.

habit_description: Scrambling perennial with woody base
leaf_description: Leaves opposite or alternate | lamina linear to broadly triangular, entire, rounded to truncate or hastate at base, usually 10--20 mm long, moderately mealy when young, abruptly petiolate
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a narrow panicle 2--4 cm long
flower_description: Perianth depressed-globular, 0.7--1.5 cm diam., mealy to glabrescent | tepals oblong, enlarging and becoming red and fleshy in fruit | Stamens 0--2, rarely 3
fruit_description: Pericarp succulent, c. 4 mm diam
seed_description: Seed 1--1.5 mm diam. | testa rugulose to areolate-reticulate, black
distribution_description: Central and eastern Australia, including Tas.

habit_description: Scrambling perennial to 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves narrowly triangular, sagittate, grey | lamina somewhat leathery, 15--40 mm long
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence paniculate
flower_description: Flowers and fruits sessile
fruit_description: Berry depressed-globular
seed_description: Seed c. 1.5 mm diam. | testa strongly alveolate
habitat_description: Usually growing in sand.
distribution_description: Found in central and western Qld, north-western N.S.W., northern S.A., east-central W.A. and N.T.

habit_description: Prostrate or scrambling perennial
leaf_description: Leaves thin, linear to narrowly oblong
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence slender
flower_description: Tepals enlarged and reflexed or spreading in fruit
fruit_description: Fruits often on slender pedicels | Berry depressed-globular
seed_description: Seed 1 mm diam. | testa finely reticulate
habitat_description: Grows usually in heavy soil.
distribution_description: Found in eastern Qld and N.S.W. and in northern Vic.

leaf_description: Leaves thin, hastate to triangular and shortly lobed at base
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence slender or branched at base
fruit_description: Fruits sessile or pedicellate | Berry depressed-globular
seed_description: Seed variably reticulate, c. 1 mm diam
habitat_description: Grows in loam or heavy soil.
distribution_description: Found in central and SE Australia including Tas.

habit_description: Scrambling subshrub to 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves somewhat leathery, narrowly hastate, acute, c. 15 mm long, basal lobes narrow, acute
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence branched
flower_description: flowers and fruits sessile
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth fleshy and reflexed, red | Berry ovoid, c. 4 mm long
seed_description: Seed horizontal to erect, c. 1 mm diam. | testa moderately reticulate
distribution_description: Found in N.S.W. and S.A.

biostatus: Native to Qld and N.S.W. but introduced in S.A.
habit_description: Spreading weak grey-green perennial with numerous stems arising from taproot
leaf_description: Leaves opposite or alternate, narrowly oblong-elliptic to narrowly hastate | lamina 0.5--1.5 cm long, acute, thin, glabrescent above, mealy below when young | petiole short and slender
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a terminal racemose panicle elongating in fruit to 15 cm with disjunct glomerules | axis at first with globular hairs | short tubular hairs, and small gland tipped hairs
flower_description: flowers sessile, 0.5--1 mm diam | Tepals broadly obovate | Stamens 1 or 2
fruit_description: pericarp thin, prominently papillose
seed_description: Seed c. 1 mm diam. | testa finely radially rugulose
habitat_description: Occurs in heavy soil.
distribution_description: Found in central-eastern Qld, central-eastern N.S.W. and as an introduction on Eyre Peninsula and around Adelaide, S.A.

habit_description: Weak prostrate or straggling perennial
leaf_description: Leaves thin, broadly ovate to triangular or hastate with short spreading lobes | lamina 8--15 mm long, glabrescent above, sparsely mealy below
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a congested to slender panicle
flower_description: flowers sessile | Perianth depressed-globular, 0.5--1 mm diam. | tepals linear to ovate or obovate, sparsely mealy or glabrous | Stamen 1 or absent | tepals oblong to obovate, herbaceous or indurated, smooth
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth | pericarp thin, often black and prominently papillose
seed_description: Seed c. 1 mm diam. | testa slightly granular or striate
distribution_description: Occurs in Qld, N.S.W. and Vic.; naturalised on Norfolk Is.

habit_description: Erect perennial herb branching from base
leaf_description: Leaves hastate to narrowly hastate, acute, mealy below | lamina c. 15 mm long | petiole slender, c. ½ length of lamina
flower_description: Tepals broadly elliptic to obovate
fruit_description: Pericarp smooth, translucent, not blackened
seed_description: Seed c. 1.2 mm diam. | testa glossy, radially striate
distribution_description: Found in north-eastern N.S.W.

habit_description: Prostrate to spreading herb with stout taproot
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a slender racemose panicle with disjunct glomerules
flower_description: Tepals spathulate to linear, frequently indurated in fruit
fruit_description: Pericarp strongly papillose, frequently black
habitat_description: Usually grows in moist situations in partial shade; a ready coloniser of disturbed areas.
distribution_description: Found in south-eastern Qld and eastern N.S.W.; on Norfolk Island.

habit_description: Plant prostrate to decumbent
leaf_description: Leaves broadly hastate or deltoid with rounded apex
flower_description: Tepals ovate to obovate, herbaceous in fruit
fruit_description: Pericarp almost smooth
distribution_description: Found in southern Vic. and south-eastern N.S.W.

habit_description: Rounded shrub to 60 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves slender, fusiform but flattened above, c. 10 mm long, villous
flower_description: Perianth densely pubescent
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth globular to cup-shaped, c. 5 mm diam., pubescent, extending upwards as short (c. 1 mm high) corona (wing)
habitat_description: Occurring principally on heavy slightly saline soils.
distribution_description: Found in inland south-western Australia.

common_name: Ruby Saltbush, Barrier Saltbush, Plum Puddings, Berry Cottonbush.
fruiting_time_description: Generally fruits from late summer to early winter
habit_description: Lax shrub c. 1 m high, densely woolly with short curled hairs to shortly villous or glabrous, sometimes glaucous
leaf_description: Leaves slender, terete or fusiform, 7--20 mm long
flower_description: Perianth tube glabrous | lobes glabrous or pubescent, woolly-ciliate
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth depressed-globular, c. 5 mm diam., green, yellow, or red, drying black | apex flat or deeply sunken in centre, glabrous or woolly | wing absent or represented by an incurved undulate corona up to 1 mm high
phenology_text: Generally fruits from late summer to early winter.
habitat_description: Occurs principally in slightly saline soil.
distribution_description: Widespread in mainland Australia where it is endemic; naturalised in New Caledonia.

stem_description: Branches and leaves very sparsely and minutely appressed villous to glabrous, glaucous
fruit_description: Fruit flat or slightly sunken in centre | lobes glabrous apart from ciliate margins
distribution_description: Widespread from the Kimberley, W.A. to the E coast of Qld and N.S.W. Wilson (1984: 215) includes distribution to north-western Vic., however, according to the Flora of Victoria (accessed 6 January 2026) var. glabra occurs near (but apparently not beyond) the Victorian border in south-western N.S.W.

stem_description: Branches decumbent to erect with a thin woolly indumentum
leaf_description: Leaves villous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth depressed-globular, flat to deeply sunken in centre | wing absent or coronate and incurved | lobes glabrous (but minutely ciliate) to pubescent
distribution_description: Widely distributed in all mainland States.

habit_description: Small shrub, densely tomentose all over with dendritic and stellate hairs
leaf_description: Leaves slender, semiterete, 10--20 mm long, spreading
flower_description: Flowers in 3-flowered axillary cymes congested into globular inflorescences due to the closely aggregated floral leaves | Perianth densely tomentose
fruit_description: Fruiting perianths closely aggregated in groups of 18--30 and partly sunken into swollen branch to form globular infructescences c. 12 mm diam. | perianth woody, cylindrical, c. 4 mm high | lobes erect | spines 5, erect, arising from base of each lobe
distribution_description: Known only from the type area in W.A., between Geraldton and Carnarvon.

habit_description: Rounded shrub c. 30 cm high
stem_description: Branches brittle, tomentose with dendritic and stellate hairs
leaf_description: Leaves narrowly obovate to obovate, 10--15 mm long, obtuse, fleshy, tomentose, the floral ones often clustered
flower_description: Flowers solitary, slightly sunken into branch | perianth cup-shaped, densely tomentose outside
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth urceolate, c. 4 mm long, woody, tomentose, becoming embedded in woody branch axis | lobes membranous, erect | spines arising from beneath perianth lobes but usually coalescing to form a stout adaxial 3-pronged spine 3--6 mm long and a shorter abaxial 2-pronged spine, the fused bases of which become flattened | Fruits irregularly clustered and persistent
habitat_description: Occurs in Mulga (Acacia aneura) scrub, also on calcareous hills and in sandy soil on eroded flats (Chippendale, 1960).
distribution_description: Found in north-western S.A. and southern N.T. westwards to the North West Cape area in W.A.
notes: The irregularly-shaped woody masses containing several fruits appear to be the natural form taken by this plant when the floral leaves are clustered (as is usual). They appear not to be galls as stated by Chippendale (1960.) and Ising (1964).

habit_description: Rounded shrub c. 20 cm high with woolly branches
leaf_description: Leaves linear, 5--10 mm long, silky-woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth densely silky-woolly, c. 1 mm high and 2 mm wide with the inner appendages c. 3 mm long | Pericarp and base of style villous
habitat_description: Grows on loamy sands in semi-arid areas.
distribution_description: Occurs in temperate W.A. eastwards to western N.S.W. and north-western Victoria.

habit_description: Small brittle shrub to 40 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves fleshy, globular to ovoid or terete, 5--15 mm long, glabrous to sericeous
flower_description: Flowers paired, bisexual
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrescent, woolly or pilose | base angular, truncate | tube short, hemispherical, woody, rarely spongy | wings 5, horizontal, oblong to fan-shaped, usually 1.5--3 mm long, rarely smaller, papery to coriaceous or spongy, rarely almost absent | upper perianth coriaceous to spongy, usually with 5 radial ridges
habitat_description: Usually found on sandy rises around salt lakes.
distribution_description: Widespread in W.A. from the latitude of Carnarvon S to Norseman.

habit_description: Divaricately-branched shrub to 2 m high, often spinescent, predominantly dioecious
leaf_description: Leaves small, alternate, slender and subterete, mostly 1--4 mm long, sparsely to densely woolly, very shortly spurred at base, frequently caducous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, occasionally with 2 minute bracteoles
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth straw-coloured when dry, glabrous except sparsely woolly upper perianth | base small, sometimes tumid or produced into a very short hollow stipe | tube hemispherical to turbinate, 1--2 mm high | wing simple, horizontal, c. 8 mm diam., papery, faintly to prominently veined, with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth thick forming a circular convex disc open in centre, sparsely woolly
habitat_description: Usually occurs in seasonally waterlogged clay soil.
distribution_description: Found west of the Great Dividing Range in N.S.W. and southern Qld, also in north-western Vic., eastern S.A., southern N.T., and in the Carnarvon-Wiluna area of W.A.
notes: This species sometimes has woolly galls caused by insect attack; hence the common name.

habit_description: Intricately-branched shrub 10--60 cm high, loosely white-woolly all over
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, suberect (if small) to spreading, narrowly deltoid to narrowly oblong, mostly 2--5 mm long
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, glabrous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous or rarely the upper perianth pubescent, straw-coloured when dry | attachment excentric on a hollow stipe to 1 mm long produced from base of tube | tube turbinate, 1--2 mm high, thin-walled and readily crushed | wing simple, c. 10 mm diam., papery, faintly nerved, with a radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth usually sunken, covering ovary, with 5 ridges extending radially between lobes
habitat_description: Usually grows on sandy saline or gypseous soils.
distribution_description: Widespread in the drier areas of the southern half of Australia in all mainland States.

habit_description: Rounded divaricately branched shrub to 1 m high, closely covered on branches and leaves with a dendritic tomentum
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, fleshy, narrowly to broadly obovoid with attenuate base, 5--10 mm long
flower_description: Flowers solitary, polygamo-dioecious, the male hemispherical and the female globose, densely tomentose, minutely bibracteolate
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth tomentose except the glabrous wing | tube turbinate, c. 3 mm high, thick-walled and smooth | wing simple, papery, horizontal, c. 15--20 mm diam., pale to dark brown when dry, with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth convex, thick
distribution_description: Found in western N.S.W., central S.A., south-western Qld and the southern portion of N.T., usually in well-drained gravelly soil in open situations.
notes: Maireana astrotricha is readily distinguished from M. sedifolia, with which it has been confused, by its dendritic hairs.

habit_description: Rigid, brittle, intricately-branched shrub to 60 cm high, dioecious
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, well-spaced or clustered on dwarf shoots, narrowly to broadly obovoid, 5--10 mm long, fleshy, sparsely appressed-pubescent
flower_description: Flowers in pairs, closely woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth thin-walled, pink to red when mature | tube convex, 10-ribbed, glabrous | wing simple, horizontal, thin, slightly crenulate, without a radial slit, to 18 mm diam. glabrous | upper perianth convex, sparsely woolly, deeply 5-lobed, 2 of the lobes with a pair of erect narrowly oblong processes, c. 6 mm high, 1 lobe with a single process, the other 2 lobes without processes
habitat_description: Usually occurs near salt lakes.
distribution_description: Found in W.A. from Shark Bay south to Watheroo and east to Laverton.

common_name: Small-leaf Bluebush, Eastern Cotton Bush, Short-leaf Bluebush.
habit_description: Shrub to 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, obovoid to narrowly fusiform, 2--5 mm long, fleshy, narrowed into a short petiole, glabrous
flower_description: Flowers bisexual, solitary, ebracteolate, glabrous except woolly-ciliate lobes | perianth lobes thick and fleshy, sharply demarcated from wings
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous | tube shallowly hemispherical, thin-walled, c. 2 mm diam. | wings 5, horizontal, thin, fan-shaped, 2--3 mm long, with delicate brown venation when dry
habitat_description: Grows in light to heavy sometimes somewhat saline soil. An early coloniser of disturbed lands.
distribution_description: Found in all mainland States, mostly S of 26°S lat.

habit_description: Small shrub to 60 mm high
stem_description: Branchlets with a thin tomentum of pale fawn curled shortly branched hairs
leaf_description: Leaves terete, slender, acute, 8--15 mm long, fleshy, glaucous, glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, glabrous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous | tube cup-shaped, c. 6 mm high and wide, spongy | wing thin, horizontal, entire, very narrow, c. 10 mm diam., with no radial slit
habitat_description: Grows principally on rocky slopes and in other well-drained situations.
distribution_description: Found in central Australia from southern half of N.T., to northern S.A. and south-western Qld.
notes: This species may be distinguished from M. spongiocarpa by the glaucous and more slender leaves, the very thin pale brown stem indumentum of dendritic hairs and the smaller fruit which lacks a vertical wing on the tube.

habit_description: Small much-branched shrub
leaf_description: Leaves opposite, sessile, semiterete, 5--6 mm long, with short silky indumentum | base shortly spurred | apex recurved
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, densely pubescent above, glabrous below | attachment broad and flat | tube shortly hemispherical, c. 2.5 mm diam., crustaceous | wing simple, circular, horizontal, thin, c. 6 mm diam., with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth slightly convex | Style hard, exserted
distribution_description: Found between Port Pirie and Leigh Creek, S.A.

habit_description: Erect perennial to 30 cm high, woody at base
leaf_description: Leaves fleshy, alternate, rarely opposite, narrowly to broadly oblong, acute, to 10 mm long | the floral leaves often broader than stem leaves, silky to woolly or almost glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, spirally arranged in dense leafy spikes, densely covered in long floccose wool
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth sessile, enveloped in a thick mass of wool to 8 mm diam. | tube shallowly hemispherical, 2--3 mm diam., crustaceous | wing circular, horizontal, 0.5 mm wide, with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth flat or slightly inflexed in centre, crustaceous
habitat_description: Usually grows in heavy soil, often around salt lakes.
distribution_description: Found in south-eastern Qld, northern S.A. and temperate and subtropical regions of the arid areas of W.A. Also in arid N.T.

habit_description: Small erect caespitose perennial with woody stock and swollen tap-root
stem_description: Branches slender, closely woolly when young
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, fleshy, slender, semiterete, c. 6 mm long, glabrous, very shortly spurred at base
flower_description: Flowers solitary or paired, bisexual
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth wheel-shaped, cartilaginous to woody, somewhat woolly above, 5--6 mm diam. | tube convex but depressed in centre, 2 mm diam., strongly 10-ribbed, with a solid boss-like base | wings 5, fan-shaped, cartilaginous, horizontally radiating | upper perianth flat | radicular slit continuing down tube as a more prominent rib
habitat_description: Grows in heavy soil.
distribution_description: Occurs in south-western Qld and near the N.S.W.-Vic. border between Bendigo and Hay.

common_name: Fissure Weed, Hairy Bluebush, Hairy Fissure-weed.
habit_description: Decumbent to erect perennial with woody base and slender taproot, to 10 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, narrowly oblong, c. 10 mm long, silky
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, densely villous, often congested into leafy spikes
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth lenticular, pentagonal in outline, c. 3 mm diam., horny, silky-villous all over | lower surface convex in centre, otherwise flat and wing-like with 5 prominent radiating intertepaline ribs extending to angles of wing
distribution_description: Found in central and north-eastern S.A. and far western N.S.W. Also in N.T. and Qld.

habit_description: Open, divaricately branched shrub 1--2 m high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, semiterete, 10--20 mm long, c. 1.5 mm wide, fleshy, somewhat silky
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual | Style massive, hard and conical, included within perianth
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth | tube broadly turbinate, c. 3 mm high and 5 mm wide at apex, smooth | the base rounded, wall thick and hard | wing horizontal, papery, c. 15 mm diam., faintly veined, with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth convex hard, closely woolly
habitat_description: Usually grows in non-saline soils in mulga (Acacia aneura) communities.
distribution_description: Found in Western Australia between latitudes 25° and 30°.

habit_description: Decumbent to erect perennial with woody base and slender taproot, c. 15 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, linear, 7--20 mm long, appressed-villous or silky
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, densely silky-villous, often in congested leafy spikes
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth like an inverted academic hat (‘mortar-board’), horny, silky-villous | base flat and continuous with a narrow circular wing, c. 4 mm diam. | upper surface with a cup-shaped outgrowth (corona) to 2.5 mm high | radicular slit extending through corona to notched margin of wing
habitat_description: Usually grows in heavy soil.
distribution_description: Found in central and eastern Australia from the vicinity of Alice Springs E to the Great Dividing Range and as far south as Dubbo, N.S.W.
notes: Very similar in appearance to M. ciliata (F. Muell.) Paul G. Wilson and M. pentagona (R. Anderson) Paul G. Wilson but readily distinguished by the ‘mortar-board’ fruit.

habit_description: Tufted to bushy shrub to 50 cm high
stem_description: Branches slender, striate, sparsely woolly or glabrous, often woolly in leaf axils
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, slender and terete to narrowly fusiform, 5--8 mm long, fleshy, glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, glabrous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous | tube shallowly hemispherical, c. 3 mm diam., thin-walled | wing thin, horizontal, simple, c. 8 mm diam., with fine pale brown anastomosing veins when dry, entire except a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth flat with somewhat fleshy lobes
habitat_description: Usually grows in heavy seasonally waterlogged soil; sometimes an early invader of cleared land.
distribution_description: Found from southern Qld to north-western Vic. and south-eastern S.A.

habit_description: Erect perennial to 20 cm high with woody base
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, linear, 7--25 mm long, appressed-villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary or paired, bisexual, shortly tomentose
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth thin-walled, sparsely pilosulose, straw-coloured when dry, with 6 delicate radially-positioned vertical wings on top of a horizontal wing | tube flat, 2.5 mm diam., 6-veined | horizontal wing simple, circular, c. 7 mm diam., continuous with tube, vertical wings 4+2 on upper side of perianth, intertepaline (the contiguous pair placed either side of the radicular slit) attached to horizontal wing and to arched upper perianth, c. 3.5 mm high | upper perianth forming a convex crustaceous ring with short inflexed membranous lobes
distribution_description: Found in central and southern Qld, also N.T.

habit_description: Erect shrub to 1 m
stem_description: Branches slender, striate, sparsely woolly when young
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, obovoid and c. 3 mm long on short lateral branches, narrowly fusiform and up to 15 mm long on the erect branches, sparsely pubescent to glabrous, narrowed into a short flattened petiole
flower_description: Flowers bisexual, solitary, glabrous, subtended by a pair of bracteoles c. 0.7 mm long | perianth lobes thickened but not fleshy, continuous with wings
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous | tube convex, thin-walled, c. 2 mm diam. | wings 5, horizontal, thin, fan-shaped, c. 2 mm long, with delicate brown venation when dry
habitat_description: Grows in saline soil.
distribution_description: Found in south-western W.A. between Dalwallinu and Merredin.

habit_description: Perennial herb to 20 cm high
stem_description: Branches decumbent to erect, slender, sparsely puberulous to villous, arising from a woody rootstock
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, narrowly oblong-elliptic, mostly 4--10 mm long, sparsely pubescent to villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, sometimes subtended by a pair of small triangular bracteoles
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth sparsely puberulous, drying black | tube slightly convex, thin-walled, c. 3 mm diam. | wings 5, only slightly exceeding tube, c. 4 mm diam., coriaceous, each broadly lunate and unevenly imbricate | the margins sometimes incurved and somewhat inflated
habitat_description: Generally occurs in woodland in loamy soil.
distribution_description: Found in southern Qld, N.S.W., Vic., south-eastern S.A. and south-western W.A.

habit_description: Shrub to 0.5 m high, predominantly dioecious
stem_description: Branchlets tomentose, the older ones scarred with persistent leaf-bases
leaf_description: Leaves alternate or opposite, fleshy, very narrowly oblong, acute, obtusely trigonous in transverse section, 10--30 mm long, 1.5--3 mm wide, densely silky
flower_description: Flowers solitary or paired, in leafy spikes
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth silky-woolly forming a soft ball c. 10 mm diam. | tube broadly turbinate to cup-shaped, c. 3 mm high, with thin weak walls | wing leathery, horizontal, deeply and irregularly divided into 5 lobes | upper perianth deeply lobed, covering ovary
habitat_description: Grows principally on rocky plains and hills.
distribution_description: Occurs in eastern S.A. north of Port Augusta and in adjacent areas in Qld, N.T. and N.S.W.

habit_description: Shrub to 60 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, fleshy, narrowly obovoid to clavate, to 10 mm long, glabrous | apex rounded
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, glabrous except woolly-ciliate lobes
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous | tube narrowly funnel-shaped, solid in lower half, c. 5 mm high, with 5 vertical semicircular wings that are attached to horizontal wing and to the tube throughout its length | horizontal wing at apex of tube, simple, c. 12 mm diam., radially sulcate at attachment to vertical wings and with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth convex, glabrous apart from ciliate margin to lobes
habitat_description: A frequent invader of disturbed areas alongside roads.
distribution_description: Found from southern W.A. eastwards to western N.S.W. and Vic.

habit_description: Erect loosely branched perennial to 30 cm high, woody towards base
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, linear to narrowly oblong, acute, to 10 mm long, silky
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, densely silky-villous, in vertical rows in dense terminal spikes 2--10 cm long
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth on a slender pedicel 0.5--1 mm long, densely covered with long silky wool forming a soft ball c. 10 mm diam. | tube thin, hemispherical to turbinate, 1.5--2.5 mm high | margin of tube thickened and undulate or of 5 short rounded erect divisions (wing lobes), continuous with tube or sometimes these forming a very narrow horizontal wing | upper perianth of 5 acuminate lobes c. 1 mm long, inflexed or eventually raised by dense indumentum arising from pericarp and overflowing tube
habitat_description: Grows in clay, at the base of breakaways and near margins of salt lakes.
distribution_description: Found in arid areas of W.A. from the Rudall River S to Norseman.
notes: Very similar to M. carnosa in which the flowers are spirally arranged in the spike.

habit_description: Decumbent perennial with stout taproot
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, narrowly oblong-elliptic to elliptic, 7--12 mm long, tawny appressed-villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, with or without a pair of narrowly-oblong bracteoles c. 1.5 mm long
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth fleshy when fresh, depressed barrel-shaped, constricted in middle, c. 3 mm high, flat above, glabrous | tube when dry with upper half very broadly turbinate to convex, 10-ribbed, thin-walled, the lower half expanded into a spongy hollow base enclosing the cushion-shaped receptacle | wing thin, horizontal, circular, entire, c. 10 mm diam., faintly nerved and with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth flat, glabrous except woolly-ciliate margin to perianth lobes
habitat_description: Grows in heavy soil.
distribution_description: Found in south-eastern S.A., southern N.S.W. near Wagga Wagga, and western Vic.
notes: This species is similar in habit to M. humillima and the two are often found growing together. Maireana humillima may be recognised by its cup-shaped perianth tube and woolly upper surface of the fruit.

habit_description: Compact rounded shrub to 50 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, slender, semiterete, 8--15 mm long, rarely longer, fleshy, sparsely to densely silky or almost glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual | style massive, hemispherical, hard, included within perianth
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous except woolly margin to lobes | tube turbinate, somewhat laterally compressed, very thick-walled, upper half fleshy on outside when fresh and becoming wrinkled on drying | the base solid and rounded, c. 6 mm high and wide (at apex) | wing horizontal, 15--20 mm diam., thin, faintly veined, with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth flat
distribution_description: Widespread in Australia but absent from the wetter southern and northern regions and east of the Great Dividing Range.
notes: A very variable species which hybridises with Enchylaena tomentosa R. Br. It may be readily distinguished from M. turbinata (with which it has been confused) by the wrinkled tube of the fruit (not smooth all over) and the radial split in the wing (not entire); it may be distinguished from M. convexa by the flat, glabrous, upper perianth.

habit_description: Rigid, open, divaricately-branched shrub to 60 cm high
stem_description: Branches brittle, woolly, covered with compact glomerules of leaves
leaf_description: Leaves sessile, fleshy and woolly, those towards apex of elongating branches alternate appressed and deltoid, c. 1.5 mm long, elsewhere minute and in dense glomerules
flower_description: Flowers solitary but arranged in short terminal spikes, polygamodioecious, woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth thin-walled, pink to red when mature | tube convex, glabrous | wing simple, rarely divided into 5 lobes, horizontal, thin, slightly crenulate, to 15 mm diam., with a single radial (radicular) slit, woolly above | upper perianth convex, deeply 5-lobed, 2 of the lobes with a pair of erect narrowly oblong processes 3--4 mm long, one lobe with a single process, the other two lobes without processes
habitat_description: Usually occurs in saline or subsaline areas.
distribution_description: Found in the dry inland areas of W.A. S of 26°S lat.
notes: This species is readily recognised by the compact woolly glomerules of leaves along the branches. The wing of the fruiting perianth is usually simple but in one specimen from Yelma Station (H.R. Toelken 6130, AD) it consists of five separate lobes.

habit_description: Decumbent perennial with a woody base
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, narrowly elliptic to obovate, acute, 7--12 mm long, rarely longer, tawny appressed-villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, subtended by a pair of narrowly ovate bracteoles c. 1.5 mm long
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth woolly on upper side of wing, otherwise glabrous, dark brown when dry | tube cup-shaped, 1.5--2 mm high, hard, faintly ribbed or smooth with a rounded base | wing simple, circular, rigid but thin, horizontal, c. 12 mm diam. | faintly veined with a radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth flat, woolly
habitat_description: Usually grows in heavy soil.
distribution_description: Found from central southern Qld and central N.S.W. to southern Vic.

habit_description: Shrub to 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, semiterete, 5--14 mm long, 1 mm wide, obtuse, woolly
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth pale to dark brown when dry | tube hemispherical, 1 mm high, 2.5 mm wide at apex, faintly costate, crustaceous, glabrous | wing simple, without a radial slit, horizontal, c. 10 mm diam., glabrous | upper perianth flat, pubescent
distribution_description: Found from western N.S.W. westwards through S.A. and southern N.T. into south-central W.A.
notes: In western N.S.W. and south-western Qld there are plants intermediate in morphology between M. integra and M. villosa; it is possible that these are hybrids between the two species.

habit_description: Small divaricately-branched shrub to 50 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, elliptic to narrowly obovate, c. 4 mm long in upper (fruiting) branches, 10--20 mm long in lower branches, silky pubescent
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, densely woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth sparsely woolly, leathery to crustaceous | tube slightly convex | wing simple, horizontal, 7--12 mm diam. with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth with 4+2 erect processes alternating with the perianth lobes | the contiguous pair placed either side of the radicular slit, the processes linear to subulate, 3--4 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in sandy and loamy soils.
distribution_description: Found from north-western W.A. to south-western Qld and central N.S.W.
notes: This species appears to intergrade with M. lobiflora in north-western W.A.

habit_description: Decumbent perennial herb with woody rootstock, or small shrub to 50 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, linear to very narrowly elliptic, mostly 7--15 mm long
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth leathery to crustaceous, woolly | tube slightly convex | wing horizontal, of 5 spathulate to fan-shaped lobes (sometimes contiguous), in all to 10 mm diam. | upper perianth with 4+2 erect processes alternating with the perianth lobes | the contiguous pair placed either side of radicular slit | processes narrowly spathulate to clavate, to 4 mm long, frequently expanded or lacerated at apex or deeply bilobed
distribution_description: Found from the southern half of W.A. eastwards to western N.S.W. and Vic.

habit_description: Woody divaricately branched perennial to 40 cm
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, fleshy, obovoid, c. 5 mm long, shortly sericeous, narrowed to a petiole-like base
flower_description: Flowers paired, bisexual
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth flattened, appressed to axis | attachment broad and flat | tube short, convex, 10-ribbed | wings 5, woody, 2--3 mm long, often irregularly curved, each divided into 2 or more spiny lobes | upper perianth flat
habitat_description: Grows around salt lakes.
distribution_description: Occurs in east-central W.A., southern N.T., northern S.A. and western Qld.

habit_description: Prostrate to decumbent perennial with a woody stock
stem_description: Branches slender, somewhat woolly when young
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, linear to narrowly oblong, 5--10 mm long, fleshy, villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, subtended by a pair of deltoid bracteoles c. 1 mm long
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth when fresh depressed barrel-shaped, constricted in middle, c. 3 mm high, 4--5 mm diam. at apex, fleshy, flat above and below, papillose on sides and puberulous above | tube bulging in lower half, smooth in upper half with 10 rounded ribs (when dry the lower half forms an expanded slightly spongy base, the upper half becomes broadly turbinate and thin-walled) | wing a very narrow horizontal extension to the flat upper perianth
habitat_description: Grows in heavy loam of eucalypt woodlands.
distribution_description: Found in south-western W.A. from Morawa SE to Ravensthorpe.

habit_description: Much-branched shrub c. 50 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, spreading, semiterete, 3--5 mm long, c. 1 mm wide, woolly, rounded at apex
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, glabrous except woolly-ciliate margin to lobes
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth dark brown to black when dry, glabrous | tube shortly hemispherical, 1 mm high, 2 mm diam., faintly costate, firmly crustaceous | wing simple, horizontal, to 6 mm diam., with prominent dark brown venation and a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth thickened and convex around margin, thin and sunken in centre
habitat_description: Grows on sandy rises around salt lakes.
distribution_description: Occurs between Beltana and Lake Watherstone near Leigh Creek W of the north Flinders Range, S.A.

habit_description: Weak diffuse shrub to 50 cm high, glabrous except woolly in leaf axils
leaf_description: Leaves subterete to narrowly fusiform, 10--20 mm long, acute
flower_description: Flowers solitary but clustered in terminal spike-like groups, bisexual, glabrous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous, pale green to gold or pale red when fresh, black when dry | tube convex, smooth, thick-walled with a thick hard base | wing horizontal, simple, 12--16 mm diam., without a radial slit | upper perianth prominently convex, hard, covered with numerous erect hair-like processes up to 6 mm long
habitat_description: Usually grows on rocky hillsides.
distribution_description: Found in the drier NW of W.A.
notes: This species may be readily recognised when in fruit by the hair-like processes which arise from the upper perianth.

habit_description: Weak shrub c. 40 cm high
stem_description: Branches slender, loosely white-woolly when young
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, sub-terete to obovoid, mostly 3--5 mm long, fleshy, glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, glabrous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous, dark brown on wing, rarely pale | tube shortly cup-shaped, 1.5 mm high, 2 mm diam., costate, crustaceous | wing simple, horizontal, firm, 5--6 mm diam., rarely wider, with a single radial (radicular) slit | the margin usually recurved | upper perianth flat or concave, obscuring ovary
habitat_description: Usually grows on claypans.
distribution_description: Found in western N.S.W., northern S.A., southern N.T., and south-western Qld.

common_name: Cotton Bush, Small-leaf Bluebush, Eastern Cottonbush.
habit_description: Divaricately branched shrub to 1 m high
stem_description: Branches slender, attenuate, sparsely strigose or appressed-pubescent to glabrous
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, subterete, mostly 2--4 mm long, glabrous to sparsely strigose or villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary forming dense leafy spikes, bisexual
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous or sparsely villous above, dark brown when dry | tube shallowly hemispherical, 1.5--2 mm diam. | wing (when present) horizontal, simple (sometimes shortly lobed opposite tepals), c. 7 mm diam., thin, crenulate on margin, with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth slightly convex
distribution_description: Found in southeastern Qld and eastern N.S.W., also northern Vic.
notes: A rather variable species which requires further study. The wing of the perianth does not always develop and the plant then resembles a species of Enchylaena.

habit_description: Shrub c. 0.3 m high, closely woolly on branches and leaves
stem_description: Branches stout, bearing protuberances left by fallen leaves
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, thick and fleshy, narrowly oblong to obcuneate, c. 20 mm long, 4 mm wide, convex below, rounded at apex
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, globose and densely woolly | Style base hard and turbinate, included, the upper portion slender, exserted and deciduous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth large | attachment broad, c. 2 mm diam. | tube turbinate, 3--4 mm high, smooth, glabrous, with thick woody walls | wing simple, horizontal, thin, c. 20 mm diam., sparsely woolly above, with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth slightly convex, thick, densely woolly
habitat_description: Grows on dissected sandstone.
distribution_description: Known from only a few collections made in W.A. between the Upper Gascoyne and Murchison Rivers.

habit_description: Compact shrub to 1 m high, usually dioecious
leaf_description: Leaves opposite (alternate and in compact glomerules in inland variant), sessile, spurred, narrowly ovate, to 4 mm long (deltoid and c. 1 mm long when clustered), obtusely trigonous in T.S., shortly sericeous to almost glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous except lobes | tube broadly obconical to convex, 1.5--2 mm diam., thin-walled | wings 5, thin, fan-shaped, prominently veined, spreading unevenly (the smaller two sub-erect), c. 7 mm diam
habitat_description: Along the southcoast of W.A. and S.A. on mud flats; in western Vic. and southern W.A. around inland salt lakes.
distribution_description: Found in W.A., S.A. and Vic.
notes: The variant found in inland area of W.A. has divaricate branches with small alternate leaves clustered into compact glomerules. In fruit characters it is identical with the coastal variant with erect branches and opposite leaves.

habit_description: Small densely branched shrub to 30 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves small, alternate, sessile, erect or appressed, narrowly ovate to broadly triangular, 2--5 mm long, loosely woolly
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth small, pale gold when dry, glabrous except woolly upper perianth | tube hemispherical, 1 mm high, 1.5 mm diam., woody, smooth except radicular ridge | wing simple, entire, with no radicular slit, horizontal, usually 4--6 mm diam., translucent | upper perianth woody, shortly woolly
habitat_description: Grows on sandy rises and eroded slopes of stony hills.
distribution_description: Found in central Australia from southern N.T. to north-eastern S.A. and north-western N.S.W.

habit_description: Prostrate to decumbent perennial with a small woody base and a long fleshy taproot, c. 10 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, linear, mostly 7--12 mm long, appressed-villous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth woolly-villous, discoid, pentagonal in outline, 2.5--4 mm diam
habitat_description: Generally grows in heavy soil.
distribution_description: Found in southern N.S.W., western Vic. and south-eastern S.A., also N of Carnarvon in W.A.

habit_description: Shrub to 60 cm high
stem_description: Branches ascending, closely white-woolly and pilose in leaf axils
leaf_description: Leaves subterete, c. 10 mm long, fleshy, glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual | perianth lobes densely woolly-villous towards margin
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous except densely woolly margin to lobes | tube turbinate, c. 4 mm high, solid in lower half, crustaceous, with 3--5 fan-shaped vertical wings usually restricted to lower half of tube | horizontal wing circular, flat, to 12 mm diam., with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth convex or arched
habitat_description: Frequently in calcareous soil.
distribution_description: Found in central and south-eastern W.A., southern N.T., S.A. and western N.S.W. and Vic.
notes: This species may be distinguished from M. erioclada (Benth.) Paul G. Wilson by the raised woolly upper perianth of the fruit and by the short vertical wings which do not reach the horizontal wing. The axillary tufts of long hairs are also distinctive.

habit_description: Openly-branched shrub to 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, flattened, narrowly obovate to obovate, obtuse, mostly 8--15 mm long, sparsely to densely appressed-pubescent
flower_description: Flowers solitary or paired (normally only one maturing), bisexual
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth straw-coloured to pale brown when dry | tube broadly turbinate, smooth or faintly ribbed, thin-walled, glabrous | wing horizontal (never infolded when young), simple with a single radial (radicular) slit, 10--14 mm diam., translucent | upper perianth flat, shortly woolly all over
habitat_description: Occurs on the rocky slopes of hills, in sand, and in mulga scrub.
distribution_description: Found in W.A. between 22° and 31°S lat., in southern N.T. and northern S.A.

habit_description: Brittle, much-branched shrub to 60 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves usually opposite, linear to semi-terete or boat-shaped, obtuse to acute, 7--12 mm long, sessile, silky
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, densely woolly | Style terete, hard, prominently exserted
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth very depressed, pale gold when dry | tube flat or slightly convex, 4--6 mm diam., crustaceous or cartilaginous, glabrous | wing continuous with tube, simple, flat or somewhat recurved around stem usually 15--23 mm diam., thin, entire, with a single radial (radicular) slit, sparsely woolly above | upper perianth convex, woolly
habitat_description: Usually occurs in saline areas but also recorded from rocky hillsides.
distribution_description: Found in W.A. from Carnarvon south-east to Norseman.
notes: The variant of M. platycarpa found towards the south-eastern area of its distribution is more slender and has much smaller fruits (c. 10 mm diam.) than the typical variant.

habit_description: Shrub c. 70 cm high, usually dioecious
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, semiterete to spathulate, rounded below, 8--15 mm long, appressed-pubescent
flower_description: Flowers solitary, glabrous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous | tube cup-shaped, 2.5--4 mm high, weakly crustaceous (somewhat fleshy when fresh), with a horizontal wing at base and apex and several imperfectly developed vertical wings, all wings papery and faintly veined | apical horizontal wing circular, 7--17 mm diam., usually with a single radial (radicular) slit, basal horizontal wing slightly smaller than apical, vertical wings up to 4+2 | the contiguous pair decurrent from the radicular slit
distribution_description: Found in north-western W.A. between Exmouth Gulf and Shark Bay.

habit_description: Open densely-leaved shrub to 60 cm high, glabrous
stem_description: Branches erect, somewhat fleshy, the older portions with prominent persistent leaf-bases
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, fleshy, semiterete, to 40 mm long, 2--3 mm wide, acute, erect (reflexed with age), bright green
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, minutely bibracteolate, glabrous, crowded towards branch apices
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth dark brown when dry, glabrous | attachment broad and flat, 2--3 mm diam. | tube turbinate, c. 5 mm high and 4 mm wide (at apex), crustaceous except thick base | wing simple, horizontal, c. 15 mm diam., the radicular split reaching only part way to tube | upper perianth flat, 5-lobed, with 4 erect linear processes at base of and alternate to lobes (no process opposite radicle)
distribution_description: Found in north-western W.A. from Cue north to the Gascoyne River.

common_name: Shrubby Bluebush, Sago Bush, Black Bluebush.
habit_description: Divaricately-branched shrub c. 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, spreading, subterete, acute, 2--6 mm long, shortly appressed-pubescent (consisting of dendritic woolly and scattered coarse smooth hairs)
flower_description: Flowers mostly unisexual, shortly woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth pale brown to black when dry | tube flat to shortly turbinate, thin-walled and readily crushed, sparsely puberulous | wing papery, horizontal, simple, 12 mm diam., rarely larger, entire or with a single radial slit | upper perianth erect, pyramidal, 2--4 mm high, puberulous
habitat_description: Grows in somewhat saline soil.
distribution_description: Found in inland W.A. and eastwards through S.A. to Qld, western N.S.W. and north-western Vic.

habit_description: Densely-branched shrub c. 0.3 m high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, erect, fleshy, narrowly ovate to semiterete, 2--4 mm long, somewhat woolly
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, glabrous below and woolly above
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous except the densely woolly upper perianth | tube hemispherical, to 1 mm high and 1.5 mm diam., brittle or almost woody, faintly ribbed | wing simple, horizontal, papery, 4--6 mm diam., when dry translucent between the fine dark-brown radial veins, with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth slightly convex, densely woolly
habitat_description: Generally grows in sandy loam, slightly saline or alkaline.
distribution_description: Found in southern Australia from Ravensthorpe in W.A. east to north-western Vic. and south-western N.S.W.

habit_description: Intricately branched shrub to 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, obovoid to narrowly fusiform, 3--8 mm long, fleshy, glabrous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, glabrous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous, pale brown when dry | tube broadly turbinate to hemispherical, to 2 mm high and 3 mm diam. at apex, thin-walled and readily crushed | wing simple, horizontal or undulate, thin, 12--16 mm diam., radially veined, with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth flat, thin
habitat_description: Usually growing in loamy soils.
distribution_description: Found from northern Eyre Peninsula, S.A., E to western Vic.

habit_description: Divaricately-branched shrub to 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves terete, slender, acute, fleshy, 5--12 mm long, sparsely appressed-villous with simple hairs
flower_description: Flowers solitary, rarely paired, bisexual, densely tomentose
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth soft and easily crushed, sparsely pilose except wing, straw-coloured when dry | tube broadly turbinate, c. 2 mm high with a vertical slit opposite radicle extending halfway down | wing horizontal, simple, papery, 12--15 mm diam., very faintly veined, with a single radial (radicular) slit from whose margins the wing passes down the tube as two membranes one either side of slit
distribution_description: Found in central Australia in south-western Qld, north-western N.S.W., south-eastern N.T. and north-eastern S.A.

habit_description: Prostrate to erect perennial to 30 cm high with a woody base
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, narrowly oblong to narrrowly obovate, usually 5--10 mm long, silky to almost glabrous
flower_description: Flowers bisexual, paired, densely woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth cartilaginous to woody, woolly all over | tube convex, 10-ribbed, c. 2 mm diam. | wings 5, horizontal, cartilaginous, broadly oblong, flat, crenulate on margin, 1--2 mm long | upper perianth open in centre, thick and hard, forming a discoid rim
habitat_description: Usually grows in sandy loam.
distribution_description: Found in central Australia.

common_name: Pearl Bluebush, Dense Bluebush, Hoary Bluebush.
habit_description: Compact divaricately branched shrub c. 1 m high covered with a close bluish-grey woolly tomentum, dioecious
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, fleshy, narrowly obovoid, 4--8 mm long, rounded at apex, slightly narrowed at base
flower_description: Flowers in pairs but usually only one maturing, closely woolly, the male hemispherical, the female globular | Style short, thick, woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth straw-coloured or pale brown when dry | tube hemispherical to turbinate, c. 2 mm high and 2--3 mm wide at apex, firm but thin-walled except thick base, sparsely woolly | wing simple, horizontal, papery, c. 10 mm diam., glabrous with fine radial venation and a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth flat, closely woolly
habitat_description: Often grows in calcareous soil.
distribution_description: Found in south-western N.S.W. and north-western Vic., S.A., southern N.T. and south-eastern W.A.

habit_description: Small shrub to 30 cm high
stem_description: Branches thin, densely woolly with smooth curled hairs
leaf_description: Leaves well-spaced, alternate, fleshy, narrowly-terete or fusiform, acute, 8--15 mm long, glabrous, dark green
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, glabrous except woolly margin of perianth lobes
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous, dark brown when dry | tube spongy, swollen and subglobular, c. 8 mm high and wide, easily crushed | wing simple, horizontal, entire, 12--15 mm diam., thin, shortly decurrent opposite radicle as a fused double vertical membrane on tube | upper perianth flat
habitat_description: Usually grows on open plains and denuded areas.
distribution_description: Found in central Australia from the southern half of N.T. south and east to western N.S.W. Also western Qld and S.A.

habit_description: Divaricately-branched shrub to 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, fleshy, semiterete, 6--10 mm long, obtuse, sparsely tomentose with shortly dendritic hairs
flower_description: Flowers solitary, unisexual or bisexual, dorsiventrally compressed
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth somewhat dorsiventrally compressed, pale brown | tube very short, broadly turbinate 0.5--1 mm high, thin-walled, densely papillose, produced at base into a prominent terete very thick-walled stipe, 1.5--3 mm long | wing simple, papery, undulate, 10--14 mm diam., finely nerved, glabrous, with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth obscuring ovary, pubescent in centre or all over, bordered by a ring of raised papillose tissue
habitat_description: Grows in sub-saline areas.
distribution_description: Occurs in the Shark Bay region and the Dampier Archipelago, W.A.

habit_description: Weak spreading dark bluish green shrub c. 0.5 m high, glabrous except axillary tufts of wool
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, well-spaced, fleshy, narrowed at base, those of fruiting branchlets fusiform and c. 5 mm long, on main branches slender-terete and up to 25 mm long
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, glabrous, minutely bibracteolate at base
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous, pink when fresh | tube shortly hemispherical, c. 3 mm diam., faintly costate, thin-walled | wing thin, horizontal, simple with a single radial (radicular) slit, 8--12 mm diam. | upper perianth flat
habitat_description: Grows on sand dunes around salt lakes and on alluvial plains.
distribution_description: Found in the southern areas of W.A. and S.A.

habit_description: Weak straggly shrub c. 1 m high, glabrous except axillary tufts of wool
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, narrowly fusiform, fleshy, 5--15 mm long, narrowed at base with a distinct petiole
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, glabrous except woolly margin to lobes
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous | tube turbinate, c. 3 mm high, crustaceous | wing thin, simple, horizontal, 10--15 mm diam., with a single radial (radicular) slit | upper perianth convex
distribution_description: Found in central W.A. from Koorda north to the Hamersley Range and east to Menzies. Also in S.A.

habit_description: Open shrub to 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, semiterete, mostly 5--8 mm long, 1 mm wide, fleshy, woolly-villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous | tube hemispherical or cup-shaped, 1--1.5 mm high, 1.5--2.5 mm diam. at apex, smooth, crustaceous or woody | wing simple, horizontal, mostly 8--11 mm diam., without a radial slit, brown to straw-coloured when dry, with indistinct nervation | upper perianth flat or raised to form a hard annular disc, woolly-ciliate but otherwise glabrous
distribution_description: Widespread in W.A. south of 20°S lat., in southern N.T., northern S.A. and north-western N.S.W.
notes: There are two subspecies.

leaf_description: Leaves obtuse to acuminate, moderately woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth | tube hemispherical, 1 mm high, crustaceous
distribution_description: Found in W.A. and southern N.T.

leaf_description: Leaves rounded at apex, loosely woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth | tube cup-shaped, often constricted at apex, 1.5 mm high, woody, glossy
distribution_description: Found in north-western N.S.W. and north-eastern S.A.

habit_description: Erect perennial to 50 cm high, woody at base
leaf_description: Leaves fleshy, semiterete, 5--10 mm long, 1.5--2 mm wide, appressed-pubescent
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual, often spicate
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth pubescent all over or only on upper surface, often red when fresh | tube (when fresh) c. 4 mm high, medially constricted, the lower half expanded into an excentric fleshy hollow stipe enclosing the receptacle, upper half shortly turbinate (when dry the lower half shrivels and becomes firm or spongy, the upper half becomes shallowly convex and papery) | wing simple horizontal, thin, reticulately veined, c. 10 mm diam. with a single radial slit | upper perianth flat, pubescent
distribution_description: Widespread in western N.S.W., western Vic., S.A., temperate W.A. and southern portion of N.T.
notes: The type of Chenolea dallachyana is without fruits and cannot be identified with certainty; it is certainly not conspecific with Eriochiton sclerolaenoides as has been suggested by R.H. Anderson, Proceedings of the Linnean Society of New South Wales 48: 327 (1923) and E.H. Ising, Transactions of the Royal Society of South Australia 88: 72 (1964).

habit_description: Compact bluish green shrub to 50 cm high, glabrous except pubescence in leaf axils
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, dense, slender and subterete, acute, c. 10 mm long
flower_description: Flowers solitary, usually bisexual
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous, glossy, dark brown to black when dry, often crowded along branches | tube turbinate, crustaceous, hard and solid in lower half | wings papery, in two series | vertical wings 5 (or with 1 or 2 undeveloped), alternate to perianth lobes, running length of tube and fusing with horizontal wing, horizontal wing at apex of tube, flat, entire, c. 8 mm diam., without a radial slit but sulcate opposite radicle | upper perianth flat
habitat_description: Found in heavy slightly saline soil.
distribution_description: Widespread in the drier areas of W.A. south of 20°S lat. and eastwards to western districts of Qld, N.S.W. and Vic.

habit_description: Divaricately branched shrub 30--60 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, subterete, 5--7 mm long, appressed-villous, fleshy
flower_description: Flowers solitary, bisexual | Style massive, solid and conical, sparsely woolly, included within perianth
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous, golden brown when mature | tube turbinate, attenuate at the solid base, crustaceous, smooth and glossy | wing papery, horizontal, 14--20 mm diam., with no radial slit, very faintly veined | upper perianth flat
distribution_description: Found in central Qld, southern N.T., western N.S.W., north-western Vic. and W to south-eastern W.A

habit_description: Open shrub to 0.5 m high
stem_description: Branches slender, minutely to loosely woolly
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, flattened, linear to very narrowly oblong or narrowly obovate, acute, 5--12 mm long, appressed-villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary or paired, bisexual, glabrous except ciliate lobes
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth brown when dry | tube broadly turbinate, faintly costate, c. 1 mm high, thin-walled and readily crushed | wing simple, horizontal (infolded when young), papery, with a single radial (radicular) slit, 7--10 mm diam., with dark brown anastomosing veins when dry | upper perianth flat, glabrous or sparsely pilose
distribution_description: Widespread in the arid areas of all mainland States except Victoria.
notes: This species is variable, particularly in the amount and texture of the indumentum. Plants intermediate in character between M. villosa and M. planifolia are found over much of the range of the former species, and may represent a distinct taxon.

habit_description: Shrub to 40 cm high
