leaf_description: Leaves spreading, narrowly linear or semiterete, 6--18 mm long, densely villous when young, glabrous with age
flower_description: Flowers paired in leaf axils, densely woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianths depressed, processes slender, terete, 2.5--4.5 mm long, 3 major and 2 minor or all of same length, with a Y- or star-shaped configuration, densely white-woolly
habitat_description: Grows in depressions and clay pans.
distribution_description: Occurs in north-eastern S.A., south-western Qld and western N.S.W.
notes: The illustration attributed to Bassia albolanata in Ising, Transactions of the Royal Society of South Australia 88: 69, fig. 9 (1964) was evidently published in error; it is an unrelated species of Sclerolaena.

habit_description: Small shrub to 25 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves slender, semiterete, acuminate, usually 5--12 mm long, white to brown villous
flower_description: Flowers in pairs in leaf axils, densely woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth very depressed, processes flat, narrowly triangular, densely woolly, 3 major c. 1.5 mm long forming a Y configuration, 1 or 2 minor ones sometimes also present
distribution_description: Occurs in the Lake Eyre Basin region of S.A. and southern N.T.

habit_description: Erect annual or perennial herb to 25 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves linear, acuminate, white-villous, 2.5--5 mm long, appressed or eventually spreading
flower_description: Flowers solitary, densely woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth depressed, appressed to branch, processes 3--5, the 3 major narrowly oblong and 2--3 mm long forming an inverted Y configuration, 2 minor ones irregularly shaped and fused with major ones to form a plate-like expansion
habitat_description: Grows on saline clay soils or gypseous mounds.
distribution_description: Recorded from eastern S.A. at Lake Callabonna and north-eastern Eyre Peninsula region.

common_name: Soft Horns, Goat Head, Woolly Saltbush.
habit_description: Erect shrub to 80 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves slender, semiterete, acute, 5--15 mm long, spreading, with recurved tips, densely white or pale brown villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary, woolly
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth densely woolly, processes 3 (rarely 4) subcylindrical, 3.5--6 mm long, forming a Y configuration
distribution_description: Occurs in inland southern W.A., southern N.T., central and eastern S.A., southern Qld, western N.S.W and far north-western Vic.

biostatus: Naturalised in S.A. Formerly naturalised in Qld.
habit_description: Annual with several decumbent stems to 15 cm long
leaf_description: Leaves narrowly obovate, obtuse, c. 10 mm long, sparsely mealy
flower_description: Flowers in compact axillary clusters | Tepals spathulate, c. 0.5 mm long
fruit_description: Utricle orbicular, c. 0.5 mm high
dispersal_description: According to Kew Plants of the World Online, the current name is Neomonolepis spathulata
habitat_description: Flora of Australia vol. 4 reports it grows "presumably near salt lakes".
distribution_description: Found in northern S.A.; native to North America.
notes: This species shows strong resemblances in its ovary and fruit to the genus Scleroblitum. According to Kew Plants of the World Online, the current name is Neomonolepis spathulata.

habit_description: Small shrub with short silky pubescence
leaf_description: Leaves semiterete, 5--15 mm long, c. 1.5 mm diam., often recurved at apex or sigmoid
flower_description: Perianth shortly silky-pubescent outside, shortly lobed | Ovary glabrous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth cylindrical, c. 3 mm long, 1 mm diam., crustaceous to thinly woody, truncate or slightly sunken at base, often somewhat expanded at apex | spines slender, half to three-quarters length of tube (if shorter then erect), spreading, shortly united at base by a saucer-shaped rim
habitat_description: Grows in saline soil.
distribution_description: Occurs from the W coast of W.A. (Shark Bay to Broome) eastwards to western N.T.
notes: Ising, Transactions of the Royal Society of South Australia 88: 95 (1964) noted that occasionally there are two flowers in the same leaf axil; in these cases the flowers are positioned one above the other, not laterally as in Dissocarpus. Probably closely related to D. biflorus.

habit_description: Small glabrous or sparsely villous shrub
leaf_description: Leaves slender, 10--20 mm long, 1 mm diam
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth tubular to bluntly ellipsoidal, c. 8 mm long, 2.5 mm diam., glabrous to villous, wall thick, initially succulent outside, later spongy, woody within | base oblique, firmly attached to branch | apex produced into a thin, very shortly 5-spined cup-shaped structure obscuring the small lobes
habitat_description: Grows in heavy soil.
distribution_description: Southern N.T. and northern S.A. to eastern N.S.W., north-western Vic. and Qld.

habit_description: Rounded perennial, branching from base, c. 15 cm high, glabrous or sparsely pilose when young
leaf_description: Leaves semiterete, 3--5 mm long, fleshy
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth | tube subglobular, c. 0.6 mm high, smooth or multiribbed, stipitate on a hollow cylindrical base equal in length to tube | apex usually produced into two opposite erect tubercles which bear vertical obovate wings, c. 3 mm long, or only the radicular tubercle present and winged, or this tubercle prominent and radially flattened but unwinged
distribution_description: W.A., N.T., S.A., Qld, N.S.W., Vic.

fruit_description: Fruiting perianth with 1 or 2 vertical wings, when 2 the longer borne on the radicular tubercle
distribution_description: Occurs from north-western W.A. through southern N.T. and north-western S.A. to south-western Qld and western N.S.W.

fruit_description: Fruiting perianth without wings | radicular tubercle prominent, erect, narrowly oblong, c. 2 mm high, sometimes pale red
habitat_description: Usually grows in heavy periodically waterlogged soil.
distribution_description: Occurs in eastern S.A. and western N.S.W. and Vic.

habit_description: Rounded perennial, branching from base, c. 15 cm high, glabrous
leaf_description: Leaves clavate, c. 5 mm long, fleshy
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth | tube cup-shaped with rounded inflexed apex, c. 0.7 mm high, ribbed, stipitate on a swollen hollow base c. twice length of tube | apex bearing 2 or 3 vertical wings c. 5 mm high which extend downwards to semicircular base of fruit
habitat_description: Grows on margin of salt lakes or on clay pans.
distribution_description: Found from southern N.T. to south-western Qld and western N.S.W.

habit_description: Rounded perennial branched from base c. 20 cm high, pilose in leaf axils otherwise glabrous
leaf_description: Leaves congested, clavate, c. 5 mm long, fleshy
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth | tube depressed-globular, sessile, ribbed, c. 1 mm high and 1.5 mm wide | wings 5, erect, fan-shaped, c. 2 mm high, arising from side of tube, in all c. 6 mm diam
seed_description: Seed horizontal | radicle centrifugal to slightly ascending
habitat_description: Grows in heavy soil subject to flooding.
distribution_description: Occurs in southern N.T., northern and north-eastern S.A. and south-western Qld.

habit_description: Glabrous, rounded perennial, branching from base, to 20 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves fleshy, semiterete or clavate, flattened above, congested towards apex of branches
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth sessile or with a short, hollow base | tube subglobular, c. 1 mm high, smooth or faintly ribbed, keeled and gibbous on the side with the radicular protuberance which is sometimes produced into a rounded tubercle
habitat_description: Generally found in clay soil subject to periodic flooding or on outer margin of salt lakes.
distribution_description: Found from inland southern W.A. eastwards through S.A. and southern N.T. to central and western N.S.W. and western Vic.

habit_description: Rounded perennial, branching from base, c. 15 cm high, glabrous
leaf_description: Leaves clavate, 3--5 mm long, fleshy
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth | tube very shortly cylindrical, c. 0.5 mm high, 1.5 mm diam., striate, expanded below into a broad smooth swollen base c. 2 mm diam. | apex bearing either 2--5 erect obovate wings up to 2 mm long or an erect narrowly oblong radicular tubercle (which is sometimes produced into a short wing) and four smaller intertepaline tubercles with or without short erect wings
distribution_description: Found in north-western N.S.W. and south-western Qld.
notes: The only collection in which 2--5 wings are present is the type; the others bear only a very short wing and 1--4 tubercles. Recorded for S.A. by J.M. Black, Flora of South Australia 2nd edn, 309 (1948), but the collection on which this was based is probably O. pentapterum. Black’s figure appears to have been copied from F. Mueller, Iconography of Australian Salsolaceous Plants t. 38, fig. 5, third fruit (1890).

habit_description: Compact intricately branched shrub c. 0.5 m high, closely mealy with minute vesicular hairs
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, narrowly elliptic, fleshy, 2--5 mm long, glabrescent above, mealy below
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence spicate with a spinescent axis c. 10 mm long
flower_description: flowers few | Male flowers broadly turbinate, c. 1 mm long | perianth mealy | filaments woolly near base, united into a thick cup-shaped disc, pistillode minute | staminodes absent | stigmas slender
fruit_description: Berry clasped around margin by perianth
seed_description: Seed c. 1.5 mm diam., radially verruculose
habitat_description: Grows in eucalypt woodland on lateritic slopes.
distribution_description: Found in the Wongan Hills, W.A.

habit_description: Spreading shrub to 2 m high
leaf_description: Leaves opposite or alternate, narrowly oblong-elliptic to elliptic, rounded to obtuse, shortly petiolate | lamina 1--4 cm long, 3--8 mm wide | margin often recurved | upper surface glabrous or sparsely mealy | lower surface sparsely to densely mealy with collapsed, saucer-shaped vesicular hairs, minutely mealy in subsp. dioica
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence an open panicle
flower_description: Perianth mealy | Male flowers with glabrous filaments and disc | terminal flowers with lanceolate staminodes and woolly disc | lateral flowers glabrous within, lacking staminodes and disc | ovary globular, glabrous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth spreading to reflexed, pale fawn | Berry depressed-globular, red
seed_description: Seed c. 1.8 mm diam. | testa glossy, minutely and irregularly tuberculate
distribution_description: Endemic in south-western W.A.

leaf_description: Leaves narrowly oblong-elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 2--4 cm long, 4--8 mm wide, thin | margins recurved | lower surface sparsely to densely mealy with saucer-shaped hairs, rarely glabrous
distribution_description: Found around the coast of southwestern W.A. from c. 80 km north of Perth to Cape Arid.

leaf_description: Leaves elliptic, obtuse, fleshy, 10--20 mm long, 3--7 mm wide | margins not recurved | upper surface glabrescent | lower surface densely white-mealy with minute hairs
distribution_description: Found in coastal southwestern W.A. from Geographe Bay north to Fremantle.

habit_description: Weak shrub, spreading or erect, to 5 m high
leaf_description: Leaves opposite to alternate, shortly petiolate | lamina thin to leathery, narrowly to broadly elliptic, broadly ovate or hastate, acute to obtuse, mostly 10--25 mm long, sparsely scaly to glabrous above, scaly below and developing a grey to silvery sheen, or glabrescent
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a pyramidal panicle to 15 cm long
flower_description: Perianth densely mealy outside | tepals ovate with thickened midrib | Male flowers | disc saucer-shaped, puberulous within, pistillode minute or similar to ovary but with erect stigmas | Female flower | staminodes with ovate membranous filaments | disc thick, woolly | stigmas spreading
fruit_description: Berry clasped at base by fleshy red perianth
seed_description: Seed depressed-globose, 1.5--2.5 mm diam. | testa almost smooth to rugulose
distribution_description: W.A., S.A., N.S.W., Vic. and Tas.

habit_description: Shrub covered with a silvery sheen
leaf_description: Leaves somewhat hastate, acute, 10--25 mm long
distribution_description: Found on the north-western plains of S.A.

leaf_description: Leaves narrowly to broadly elliptic, broadly ovate, or obtusely hastate, obtuse | lower surface covered with a grey sheen or glabrescent
habitat_description: Found in coastal situations.
distribution_description: Occurs in southern N.S.W., Vic., Tas., S.A. and in the Recherche Archipelago, W.A.

habit_description: Shrub to 1.5 m high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, fleshy, fusiform to semiterete, often channelled above or falcate, 1--2 cm long, mealy when young, the vesicles later fusing to form a metallic sheen
inflorescence_description: Panicle to 5 cm long or reduced to a short spike
flower_description: Flowers and fruit as in R. candolleana Moq
habitat_description: Usually grows in calcareous soil.
distribution_description: Principally a coastal species of S.A. and southern W.A.; an inland variant occurs from south-eastern W.A. to north-western Vic.

habit_description: Open, often scrambling shrub to 1.5 m high
leaf_description: Leaves opposite or alternate, narrowly elliptic to elliptic, somewhat fleshy, shortly petiolate | lamina usually 7--10 mm long and 2--3 mm wide, acute, glabrescent above, densely mealy below with grey saucer-shaped vesicular hairs
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence spicate or paniculate, to 2.5 cm long
flower_description: Perianth densely mealy | Male flowers | staminal filaments united into a fleshy disc which is woolly within | terminal flowers with minute staminodes and disc, slightly woolly | lateral flowers glabrous within, lacking staminodes and disc
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth eventually spreading, pale fawn or red within
seed_description: Seed c. 1.8 mm diam., faintly radially rugulose
habitat_description: Grows in somewhat saline soil.
distribution_description: Found in southern inland W.A. and in the extreme west of S.A.

habit_description: Rounded shrub to 2 m high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, ovate to elliptic | lamina 0.5--1.5 cm long, glabrescent above, mealy below with minute irregularly-shaped hairs | petiole c. ½ length of lamina
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence spicate to paniculate with the flowers uninterrupted or (in N areas) a slender spike with disjunct glomerules
flower_description: Perianth densely mealy | Male flowers caducous | perianth globular, c. 1.5 mm diam. | filaments united into a thick saucer-shaped disc, pubescent within | Female flower | perianth eventually hard and spreading beneath fruit, red above | staminodes present in terminal flower, absent in the others
seed_description: Seed c. 1.3 mm diam. | testa reticulate
distribution_description: Found from north-western W.A. eastwards into central Australia.

habit_description: Shrub to 1.5 m high
leaf_description: Leaves opposite or alternate, linear to orbicular, densely mealy all over with vesicular hairs, leathery or fleshy | lamina c. 1 cm long | petiole c. 5 mm long
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence pyramidal or spike-like
flower_description: Perianth c. 1.5 mm diam., densely mealy | Male flower | disc cup-shaped, woolly within | Female flowers, if terminal with short membranous staminodes and woolly disc, if lateral without staminodes and with glabrous disc
fruit_description: Berry c. 3.5 mm diam., exceeding perianth which is red within
seed_description: Seed c. 1.3 mm diam. with faint radial markings
distribution_description: Occurs in W.A. along the central western coast.

habit_description: Divaricately-branched shrub
leaf_description: Leaves elliptic to orbicular, often conduplicate, leathery, densely mealy with spherical vesicular hairs
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence pyramidal
distribution_description: Found in coastal W.A. from Shark Bay to the Murchison River, on sand dunes, often over limestone.

leaf_description: Leaves semiterete, fleshy, c. 10 mm long, 1 mm wide, flat and glabrous above, densely mealy below with minute irregularly-shaped vesicular hairs
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a spike-like panicle
habitat_description: Grows on sand dunes.
distribution_description: Found in coastal W.A. from near Geraldton north to the Murchison River.

common_name: Fragrant Saltbush, Mealy Saltbush, Oldman Saltbush.
habit_description: Rounded shrub to 2 m high
leaf_description: Leaves mostly opposite | lamina thin, very broadly elliptic to broadly or very broadly ovate, rarely obtusely hastate, acute to rounded at apex, apiculate, lamina 1.5--4 cm long, truncate to cuneate at base and passing into slender petiole half to as long as lamina, minutely mealy, becoming reddish brown with age
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a broad pyramidal panicle 5--8 cm long
flower_description: Perianth mealy, c. 1 mm diam | Male flowers | filaments united into a cupular disc densely woolly on margin | Female flower | staminodes in terminal flowers united into a cupular disc densely woolly within, in lateral flowers reduced or absent
seed_description: Seed c. 1.8 mm diam. | testa with faint radial ribbing
habitat_description: Growing principally on rocky hillsides and creek banks.
distribution_description: Found in south-eastern Qld, north-eastern N.S.W., southern Vic., southern S.A. and central Australia.

habit_description: Shrub to 2 m high
leaf_description: Leaves linear to spathulate or broadly obovate, thin to leathery | lamina 3--4 cm long, tapering into a slender petiole, sparsely and minutely mealy beneath when young
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a pyramidal panicle c. 5 cm long
flower_description: Flowers spherical, c. 1 mm diam | Tepals glabrous | Male flowers | filaments somewhat pilose at base, united into a saucer-shaped disc | Female flowers | terminal flowers usually sterile with densely pilose linear staminodes | lateral flowers fertile, without staminodes
fruit_description: Berry depressed-spherical, c. 3 mm diam
seed_description: Seed c. 1.5 mm diam. | testa with faint radial ribbing
distribution_description: W.A., S.A.

leaf_description: Leaves broadly obovate, rounded to truncate, apiculate, narrowed into a slender petiole, in all 1.5--3 cm long, leathery, glabrescent to sparsely mealy
flower_description: Perianth glabrous to sparsely mealy
distribution_description: Found from Shark Bay to Geraldton, W.A.

leaf_description: Leaves linear to narrowly obovate or spathulate, usually thin, flat or cymbiform
flower_description: Perianth glabrous
habitat_description: Grows in deep sand.
distribution_description: Found in W coastal and south-western W.A. and southern S.A.

common_name: Spiny Saltbush, Berry Saltbush, Hedge Salt-bush, Creeping Saltbush.
habit_description: Shrub to 1.5 m high
leaf_description: Leaves opposite or subopposite, ovate to deltoid or hastiform, mealy all over with discrete saucer-shaped or spherical vesicular hairs | lamina 5--20 mm long, obtuse to rounded | petiole c. ½ length of lamina
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a panicle or reduced to a spike
flower_description: Perianth densely mealy outside | Male flowers globular, 0.5--1 mm diam. | filaments united into a glabrous saucer-shaped disc | Female flowers globular to turbinate, c. 1 mm high, eventually spreading beneath fruit and 2.5--3 mm diam., becoming hard and pale red | staminodes c. 0.3 mm long, united into a glabrous or sparsely hairy disc
fruit_description: Berry depressed-globular, pink or red
seed_description: Seed c. 1 mm diam. | testa prominently reticulate
distribution_description: Found from south-eastern W.A. through central Australia and in north-western Vic.

habit_description: Dense, intricately branched spinescent shrub to 1 m high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, often clustered, elliptic, fleshy, 2--5 mm long, closely mealy with vesicular hairs
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a narrow condensed cyme (sometimes spinescent) with 1--4 lateral and a large terminal flower
flower_description: Perianth globose, 1.5 mm diam., mealy | Male flower | disc inconspicuous, glabrous, pistillode minute | Female flower | staminodes minute | style minute | stigmas spreading, slender, subulate
fruit_description: Berry at first enveloped by perianth
seed_description: Seed c. 1.5 mm diam. | testa smooth to minutely granular
habitat_description: Usually grows in rocky situations or on limestone.
distribution_description: Found from south-eastern W.A. to western N.S.W. and north-western Vic.

habit_description: Rigid divaricately-branched spinescent shrub to 60 cm high
stem_description: Branches pubescent when young, soon becoming glabrous and black
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, mostly in small dense globular fascicles on the closely spaced short dwarf branches, leaves on main branches narrowly triangular, c. 2 mm long, appressed, carinate, fleshy, shortly spurred at base, sparsely pubescent when young but eventually glabrous, leaves in fascicles broadly ovate, 0.5--1 mm long
flower_description: Flowers located in the leafy fascicles, subglobular, bisexual | Tepals free, broadly ovate, slightly fleshy with membranous margin c. 1.5 mm long, sparsely pubescent | Staminal filaments sparsely pubescent towards base | Ovary narrowly ovoid, silky-pubescent c. 1 mm long | styles 2 or 3, 0.5--1 mm long
fruit_description: Fruit depressed-spherical c. 3 mm high | mericarp crustaceous
vegetative_reproduction_description: Vegetatively similar to the inland variant of Maireana oppositifolia but differs in perianth structure and in the flowers being bisexual; in fruit readily distinguishable
habitat_description: Grows in heavy saline soil.
distribution_description: Found in southern central W.A. from Yuna east to Laverton and south to Koorda and Southern Cross.
notes: Vegetatively similar to the inland variant of Maireana oppositifolia but differs in perianth structure and in the flowers being bisexual; in fruit readily distinguishable.

habit_description: Perennial herb forming densely branched, silvery, mat-like growths to 1 m diam., dioecious
stem_description: Branchlets closely woolly, obscured by the leaves

habit_description: Erect perennial to 20 cm high

habit_description: Plant caespitose or with a dense cluster of slender stems arising from short horizontal stolons

seed_description: Seed covered with short acute trichomes
habitat_description: Occurs on rocky coasts where subject to periodic inundation by the sea.
distribution_description: Found in Tas. and S coast of Vic.

common_name: Prickly Saltwort, Soft Buckbush, Roly-poly, Soft Roly-poly.

habit_description: Erect perennial c. 20 cm high

seed_description: Seed horizontal, thick
habitat_description: Occurs on outer margin of salt lakes.
distribution_description: Found in central W.A. between 24° and 29°S lat.

habit_description: Glabrous rounded perennial to 15 cm high, branching from base
leaf_description: Leaves slender, terete, 5--10 mm long, fleshy

habitat_description: Grows in heavy soil.
distribution_description: Found in north-western and central N.S.W. and Qld.

habit_description: Small rounded shrub to 40 cm high, glabrous except woolly-pilose leaf axils
leaf_description: Leaves slender, semiterete, acute, 5--15 mm long
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth glabrous except woolly-ciliate tepals | Stamens 5

seed_description: Seed and radicle erect
habitat_description: Grows in heavy slightly saline soil.
distribution_description: Found in central W.A., north-eastern S.A., western N.S.W., and far north-western Vic. In Victoria, specimens are now treated as Sclerolaena intricata. (see VicFlora).
notes: Differs from S. intricata only in having 3, not 5, spines; possibly conspecific with that species. The fruits are sometimes congested along short portions of a branch which, when dead, may fall to the ground intact. Hybridisation with S. cuneata appears to take place, e.g. a collection from Mt Mulyah, N.S.W., C.E.W. Moore 6812 (CANB), with putative parents in same locality.

habit_description: Intricately branched shrub to c. 50 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves well-spaced, slender and semiterete, c. 20 mm long, erect and spreading at tips when young, sparsely silky-pilose with scabridulous hairs to glabrous

seed_description: Seed horizontal | radicle erect

fruit_description: Fruiting perianth c. 6 mm diam., with a thick white woolly indumentum | spines 10--20 mm long, erect to spreading, slender
habitat_description: Grows in heavy soil.
distribution_description: Found from north-western W.A. eastwards through southern N.T. and S.A. to Qld and central and western N.S.W.; also known in Vic. from a 2015 collection from a small stand of apparently naturalised plants in mallee woodland just west of Lake Buloke near Donald (Sclerolaena bicornis Lindl. var. bicornis in VICFLORA, accessed 8 October 2025).

fruit_description: Fruiting perianth c. 4 mm diam., with a close woolly indumentum | spines two, 3--4 mm long, erect, often with a small additional radicular spine or tubercle
habitat_description: Usually grows in red-brown soil.
distribution_description: Found in northern N.S.W. and in central and southern Qld.

habit_description: Small shrub c. 15 cm high

seed_description: Seed horizontal
distribution_description: Known from the Flinders Range area, S.A., and one locality in the Carnarvon district, W.A. Check this.

biostatus: Native but doubtfully so in Victoria.

distribution_description: Found in southeastern Qld, central N.S.W., northern Vic. and occasionally in southern N.T. and southeastern S.A.

habit_description: Rounded herb to 30 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves slender, semiterete, 5--20 mm long, silky-villous or eventually glabrous

distribution_description: Found in northern S.A., south-western Qld and western N.S.W.

habit_description: Rounded annual or short-lived perennial c. 15 cm high, glabrous except slight axillary pubescence

habitat_description: Grows in depressions and channels on gravelly downs.
distribution_description: Known only from the type locality in south-western Qld.

habit_description: Decumbent shrub, villous on leaves and branches
leaf_description: Leaves linear, c. 10 mm long

habitat_description: Usually in heavy somewhat saline soils.
distribution_description: Found in south-western Qld, central and western N.S.W., western Vic., S.A., southern N.T., and north-central W.A.

habit_description: Small erect shrub c. 30 cm high, hirtellous all over or eventually almost glabrous

habitat_description: Grows in slightly saline or calcareous soil.
distribution_description: Found from south-eastern W.A. eastwards to northern Eyre Peninsula in S.A.
notes: A species similar to (and probably intergrading with) S. obliquicuspis.

habit_description: Rounded perennial to 20 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves erect, linear, c. 10 mm long, appressed-villous, fleshy

habit_description: Rounded perennial branching from base, c. 25 cm high, glabrous to pilose

habitat_description: Grows in heavy soil.

habit_description: Perennial to 30 cm high

habit_description: Rounded perennial to 20 cm high

seed_description: Seed and radicle vertical
habitat_description: Occurs frequently in slightly saline loam or alluvial soil.
distribution_description: Found from the Lake Eyre region of S.A. SE to western N.S.W.

habit_description: Erect woody perennial to 30 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves linear to narrowly elliptic, 4--10 mm long, appressed-villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Stamens 4

seed_description: Seed horizontal
distribution_description: Found in central Australia and E to southern Qld and northern N.S.W.
notes: Similar to S. parviflora but distinguished by its different indumentum and by the fewer stamens and spines.

habit_description: Small woody perennial to 30 cm high

flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth sparsely villous | Stamens 4

habit_description: Annual or short-lived perennial to 20 cm high
stem_description: Branches sparsely and shortly pilose when young, otherwise glabrous

habit_description: Intricately branched rounded perennial to 30 cm high, glabrous except axillary pubescence

notes: Closely related to S. blakei from which it differs in the shape and ribbing of the perianth tube, and the direction of the spines.

habit_description: Small dense shrub to 30 cm high

habitat_description: Usually grows in heavy slightly saline soil.

habit_description: Erect, perennial to 30 cm high, silky-pilose all over

seed_description: Embryo and radicle erect
distribution_description: Found in the central and northern desert areas of W.A, extending into N.T. and Qld.

habit_description: Divaricately branched perennial to 30 cm high

flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth 4-lobed, woolly | Stamens 4

habit_description: Rounded perennial to 25 cm high

habit_description: Much-branched perennial c. 30 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves alternate, succulent, semiterete c. 15 mm long, appressed-villous to silky
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth silky-villous | Stamens 5

habitat_description: Usually grows in heavy soil or in sand overlying clay.

habit_description: Perennial herb, woody at base, c. 30 cm high

habitat_description: Occurs in subsaline situations.
distribution_description: Found in the drier areas of subtropical W.A.

habit_description: Spreading perennial
leaf_description: Leaves semiterete, c. 10 mm long, villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth villous | Stamens 5

seed_description: Seed and radicle erect
habitat_description: Grows in Gidgee (Acacia cambagei) country on more or less stony lateritic soil.
distribution_description: Found in central Qld.

habit_description: Rounded shrub c. 30 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves crowded towards branch apices, linear, bluntly trigonous, c. 30 mm long, 3 mm wide, silky
flower_description: Flowers in pairs | Perianth pubescent, 5-lobed | Stamens 5

seed_description: Seed horizontal | radicle centrifugal
habitat_description: Occurs in kopi on margins of gypsum salt lakes.
distribution_description: Found in the desert of central W.A.
notes: This species differs from Sclerolaena symoniana in having the fruiting perianth appendages only slightly dissected, not fimbriate.

habit_description: Erect perennial to 30 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves slender, semiterete or trigonous, 1.5--3 cm long, somewhat sigmoid with recurved apex, silky
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth velvety | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth partly embedded in branch axis, velvety | tube disc-shaped, c. 1 mm high, 3 mm wide | limb conical, erect to 3 mm high | spines 2 + 2 | the abaxial spines laterally placed and ascending, slender, 2--3 cm long, the radicular adaxial spines to 1 cm long or with one sometimes reduced to a tubercle
seed_description: Seed horizontal | radicle ascending
habitat_description: Grows on sandplains inland of Carnarvon.
distribution_description: Found in north-western W.A.

habit_description: Dense rounded perennial to 20 cm high, glabrous except slight pubescence in leaf axils
stem_description: Branches marked by slightly raised leaf scars
leaf_description: Leaves fusiform, 3--5 mm long, fleshy, passing at base into a very short flattened petiole
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth glabrous except slight pubescence on lobes | Stamens 3

seed_description: Seed and radicle erect
habitat_description: Grows in loamy soil of eucalypt woodland.
distribution_description: Found in the central southern area of W.A. from Southern Cross north to Leonora and east to c. 200 km E of Kalgoorlie extending into S.A..

habit_description: Small rounded shrub c. 0.4 m high, glabrous except axillary pubescence
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth glabrous except ciliate tepals | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth hard, glabrous | attachment oblique, circular, slightly hollowed | tube oblong, slightly broader at apex, c. 2.5 mm long, dorsiventrally compressed, faintly ribbed | limb erect with tip inflexed, c. 1 mm high | spines 2 + 1 or 2 + 2, an opposite pair laterally placed and ascending, 3--7 mm long, a radicular spine curved adaxially, 1--2 mm long, usually with a collateral tubercle or small spine
seed_description: Embryo erect
habitat_description: Grows usually in heavy somewhat saline soil.
distribution_description: Found from north-western W.A. eastwards through N.T. and northern S.A. to western Qld and north-western N.S.W.

habit_description: Perennial to 20 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves linear, c. 10 mm long, fleshy, silky, pilose
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth tomentose | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth very closely white-tomentose, somewhat ribbed on abaxial face | tube subglobular, gibbous, c. 2.5 mm high and wide including the deeply hollowed base | adaxial surface very convex | abaxial surface almost flat | attachment elliptic, c. 3 mm long | limb incurved and inconspicuous | spines 2, lateral, slender, to 7 mm long, divergent, sometimes very reduced | radicular tubercle inconspicuous, adjacent to a spine
seed_description: Seed oblique to erect or rarely horizontal
distribution_description: Found in southern N.T., south-western Qld and northern S.A.

habit_description: Intricately branched perennial to 60 cm high, glabrous
leaf_description: Leaves semiterete to slender, clavate, acute, c. 10 mm long, fleshy
flower_description: Flowers solitary, glabrous except woolly inside of perianth lobes | Stamens 4
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth persistent, very thick-walled, woody within, firmly spongy outside | attachment truncate, circular, 6--8 mm diam. | tube very shortly cylindrical, c. 3 mm high, 6--8 mm wide extending upwards as a thick-walled cup, c. 3 mm high from the corners of which arise four ascending spines, c. 10 mm long
seed_description: Seed horizontal, thick | radicle erect
habitat_description: Occurs along creeks and on stony plains.
distribution_description: Found in north-western W.A. between Roebourne and Nullagine.

habit_description: Intricately branched dwarf shrub to 40 cm high, glabrous except woolly pilose leaf axils
leaf_description: Leaves clavate and c. 5 mm long to slender and semiterete to 10--15 mm long, acute
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth glabrous except woolly ciliate tepals | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth hard, erect and oppressed to branch, persistent | attachment very oblique | tube semicylindrical, dorsiventrally compressed, c. 3 mm high | limb erect, woolly-ciliate | spines 3+2, spreading to recurved, slender, 5--15 mm long, the inner of the radicular pair shorter
seed_description: Seed and radicle erect
habitat_description: Often grows in heavy slightly saline soil.
distribution_description: Found in southern N.T., south-western Qld, western N.S.W., north-eastern S.A. and north-western Vic.

habit_description: Bushy intricately-branched annual or perennial, glabrous
leaf_description: Leaves slender, subterete or very narrowly fusiform, obtuse, mostly 5--10 mm long, rarely to 15 mm long
flower_description: Flowers solitary, glabrous | Stamens 4
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth hard, glabrous | attachment circular | base truncate, horizontal | tube shortly cylindrical, c. 1.5 mm high, 2 mm wide | apex convex
seed_description: Seed horizontal | radicle ascending
habitat_description: Grows on sandplains or in sandy swales between dunes.
distribution_description: Found in southern N.T. and adjacent regions of W.A., S.A., Qld and N.S.W.

habit_description: Woody perennial c. 25 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves semiterete, 10--20 mm long, fleshy, pilose
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth pilose | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth pilose all over, readily detached | attachment basal, circular, concave, 0.4--1.2 mm diam. | tube turbinate, dorsiventally compressed, 1.5--3 mm long | limb erect, membranous | spines 3, rarely 4, two erect and lateral, c. twice length of tube and one (or 2 adjacent collateral) adaxial either erect and equal to lateral spines or divaricate and shorter
seed_description: Seed and radicle erect
distribution_description: Found in central and northern W.A., N.T., S.A., central and western Qld, western N.S.W., and north-western Vic.
notes: Some variants of this species closely resemble S. densiflora which may, however, be distinguished by the square apex to its fruit on which there are 5 spines, 2 of which are close together and collateral. As delimited here S. lanicuspis may encompass a number of distinct taxa.

habit_description: Shrub to 1 m high, tomentose all over with shortly dendritic hairs
leaf_description: Leaves slender, semiterete to clavate, 10--30 mm long, often recurved at apex, fleshy
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth tomentose
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth hard, tomentose | attachment basal, elliptic, c. 3.5 mm long | tube very shortly turbinate, c. 2 mm high and 3 mm wide at apex | limb erect, cylindrical, shortly exceeding tube | spines 2, divergent, 5--10 mm long | radicular tubercle prominent
seed_description: Seed horizontal | radicle ascending
habitat_description: Grows in heavy slightly saline soil.
distribution_description: Found in eastern S.A. and far western N.S.W. with isolated records from north-western W.A., southern N.T. , central Qld and north-western Vic.
notes: Similar to Sclerolaena bicornis var. horrida from which it differs in having a dendritic indumentum and a turbinate perianth tube.

habit_description: Rounded glabrous perennial to 60 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves slender, trigonous in T.S., 2--3 cm long
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth glabrous outside, woolly within | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous outside | attachment broad and expanded | the base somewhat spreading around branch | tube cylindrical, narrowing towards apex, c. 5 mm high and wide at base | wall very thick, somewhat spongy on outside, woody within | limb conical, c. 2 mm high, erect or inflexed at tip | spines 2(rarely 4) + 1(2), slender, ascending, lateral pair 20--30 mm long, adaxial radicular pair with one 5--10 mm long, the other minute or up to 2 mm long (or the longer radicular spine absent), one or two long abaxial spines sometimes present or these represented by a small tubercle
seed_description: Seed and radicle erect
habitat_description: Occurs frequently in stony soil on hills.
distribution_description: Found in southern N.T., northern and eastern S.A., south-western Qld and north-western N.S.W.

habit_description: Shrub to 0.5 m high, pilose in leaf axils, otherwise glabrous
leaf_description: Vegetative leaves narrowly fusiform, 5--8 mm long, fleshy, narrowed into a short flattened petiole | Floral leaves congested towards apex of branchless | lamina ellipsoidal, c. 3 mm long | petiole expanded around base of flower, adaxially silky pilose
flower_description: Flowers solitary, unisexual | Perianth urceolate, glabrous, membranous | lobes erect, united, membranous, undulate and ciliate on margin | Male flower | stamens 5, pistillode with slender sparsely woolly style and short lobes | Female flower | staminodes absent | ovary glabrous | style stout, c. 1.5 mm long, woolly pilose | stigmas 2, slender, c. 2.5 mm long
fruit_description: Infructescence a condensed spike which eventually breaks from plant | Fruiting perianth urceolate, dorsiventrally compressed, 3.5--5 mm high, 2.5--4 mm wide, papery, glabrous, glossy, adaxial side flat, abaxial side convex | limb erect | attachment vertical, firmly attached to axis | spines 5, or 1 to 4 of the spines paired to give up to 9, slender, divaricate or descending, sometimes curved, 3--5 mm long, one on adaxial face, the others lateral and abaxial
seed_description: Seed depressed | radicle ascending
habitat_description: Occurs on gneissic plain in slightly saline soil.
distribution_description: Found in W.A. c. 300 km NE of Carnarvon.

habit_description: Decumbent villous perennial
leaf_description: Leaves erect, linear to very narrowly oblong, c. 6 mm long, crowded towards branch apices
flower_description: Flowers solitary, glabrous | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth sub-globular, glabrous | attachment basal, horizontal | base rounded, concave | tube depressed-cylindrical to shortly barrel-shaped, 10-ribbed, c. 1 mm high, 1.5 mm wide | apex truncate | spines 4 + 2, c. 0.5 mm long, recurved at apex, regularly placed at margin of apex with radicular pair close together
seed_description: Seed horizontal
dispersal_description: Current name is Sclerolaena brachyptera
vegetative_reproduction_description: Similar to Sclerochlamys brachyptera in vegetative characters, but the fruit lacks the 5-angled wing of the latter species
distribution_description: Occurs in W.A. between Mt Magnet and Leonora.
notes: Similar to Sclerochlamys brachyptera in vegetative characters, but the fruit lacks the 5-angled wing of the latter species. Current name is Sclerolaena brachyptera.

habit_description: Annual or short-lived perennial branching from base, to 20 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves very narrowly ovate to very narrowly oblong, 5--10 mm long, villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth villous | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth villous | attachment basal and oblique, minute | tube turbinate, somewhat dorsiventrally compressed, 1.5--3 mm long | apex truncate, slightly concave, but with erect membranous limb in centre | spines 2, lateral, ascending, 0.5--1.5 mm long, a pair of adjacent minute radicular tubercles also present or these developing short spines
seed_description: Seed and radicle erect
habitat_description: Grows on rocky hillsides.
distribution_description: Found in north-eastern W.A., southern N.T. and western Qld.

habit_description: Sprawling perennial to 60 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves very narrowly oblong to linear, 5--20 mm long, fleshy, woolly-villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth villous | Stamens 4

seed_description: Seed horizontal | radicle slightly ascending
habitat_description: Grows in slightly saline sandy soil.
distribution_description: Found in northern central Australia near the W.A.-N.T. border.

habit_description: Rounded annual or perennial to 1 m high, intricately and divaricately branched, glabrous to villous or woolly
leaf_description: Leaves flat, linear to narrowly oblong or elliptic, mostly 5--15 mm long
flower_description: Flowers solitary, glabrous to villous or minutely woolly | Stamens 4

seed_description: Seed oblique to horizontal
distribution_description: In N.T., S.A., Qld, N.S.W. and Vic.
notes: There are three varieties.

habit_description: Plant glabrous or almost so, glaucous
leaf_description: Leaves flat, linear to narrowly elliptic, mostly 5--15 mm long, rarely to 25 mm long
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous
habitat_description: Often associated with creeks.
distribution_description: Found in eastern Australia from central Qld south to northern Vic. and eastern S.A. Also N.S.W and N.T.

habit_description: Plant sparsely appressed-hirsute at least when young
leaf_description: Leaves elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 5--10 mm long
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth sparsely woolly when young
distribution_description: Found from south-eastern Qld to northern Vic. and south-eastern S.A.
notes: This variety grades into var. muricata.

leaf_description: Leaves flat, linear to narrowly elliptic, villous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth sparsely woolly
distribution_description: Found from south-eastern Qld, south to northern Vic. and south-eastern S.A.
notes: Resembles S. johnsonii which has terete leaves and a fruiting perianth with a horizontal base, and horizontal spines.

habit_description: Erect perennial c. 30 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves linear, 10--15 mm long, appressed-hirsute with minutely scabridulous hairs
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth 5-lobed, sparsely pubescent | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth sparsely pubescent | tube broadly turbinate, c. 3 mm high and as wide at apex, faintly ribbed | attachment flat, horizontal, circular, c. 1.2 mm diam. | apex convex | limb inconspicuous | spines 4 + 2 radiating and slightly ascending, the 4 major spines 2.5--4 mm long, the radicular pair to 1 mm long and arising from a short spur that is decurrent as a rib
seed_description: Seed horizontal | radicle ascending
distribution_description: Found in south-central N.S.W. and north-central Vic.

habit_description: Small shrub c. 30 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves linear to narrowly elliptic, 6--10 mm long, obtuse, fleshy, closely woolly to oppressed pilose | the hairs minutely scabridulous
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth shortly and closely woolly | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth closely woolly | attachment basal, narrowly elliptic, c. 4 mm long, shortly spurred along stem above and below tube | tube broadly oblong, c. 2 mm high | limb erect but inconspicuous | spines 2, obliquely spreading in different vertical planes, the radicular spine inclined abaxially and the other adaxially, c. 5 mm long, tomentose towards base | radicular tubercle small at base of abaxial spine
seed_description: Seed and radicle erect
habitat_description: Often grows in calcareous soils.
distribution_description: Found in south-central and eastern W.A., south-western N.T., S.A., western N.S.W., and far north-western Vic.
notes: This species evidently grades into both Sclerolaena brevifolia and S. patenticuspis.

habit_description: Rounded perennial to 20 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves slender, semiterete, 7--15 mm long, silky villous, fleshy
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth densely woolly villous | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth closely woolly | tube oblong, c. 3 mm high and wide, curved upwards, dorsiventrally compressed, expanded into a hollow base with elliptic attachment c. 5 mm long | limb short, erect, obscured by indumentum | spines 2, lateral, parallel and erect, 1--3 mm long, somewhat obscured by indumentum | radicular tubercle prominent, adjacent to one of the spines
seed_description: Seed and radicle oblique
habitat_description: Often occurring in clay on stony plains or hillsides.
distribution_description: Found from southern N.T. SE through north-eastern S.A. to north-western N.S.W. and south-western Qld.

habit_description: Erect woody perennial to 30 cm high, sparsely appressed-hirtellous
leaf_description: Leaves narrowly ellipsoidal, 2--3 mm long or slender and subterete to 6 mm long, fleshy
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth hirtellous | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth hard, very shortly cylindrical or broadly turbinate, smooth or ribbed, c. 1 mm high and 1.5 mm wide, sparsely appressed-hirtellous to glabrous, glossy | apex truncate | base rounded, sometimes hollowed | attachment circular | limb depressed and inconspicuous | spines 4 + 2, 1--2 mm long, the radicular pair often shorter than the others, radiating
seed_description: Seed horizontal
distribution_description: Widespread in the drier central and southern portions of Australia.

habit_description: Rounded perennial c. 20 cm high
stem_description: Branches pubescent with short curled cottony hairs
leaf_description: Leaves linear to semiterete, 5--10 mm long, villous with simple hairs
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth shortly villous | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth shortly and sparsely pilose | attachment oblique, circular or elliptic | tube shortly oblong, c. 1.5 mm high and wide, sometimes spreading at base | the adaxial surface concave | abaxial surface flat or convex | limb erect, c. 1 mm high | spines 2, laterally placed, ascending in nearly the same vertical plane, 4--7 mm long, rarely very reduced or absent | radicular tubercle very small and on adaxial side of one of the spines
seed_description: Seed and radicle erect
distribution_description: Found in central N.S.W. and north-western Vic., extending W to central and south-eastern W.A and north into N.T.
notes: A rather polymorphic species, some variants of which come close to S. obliquicuspis. E.H. Ising, Transactions of the Royal Society of South Australia 88: 84 (1964), noted a form found principally in the Nullarbor Plain in which one or both spines were weakly developed or were represented merely by small tubercles. In this variant the development of the spines is very variable even on the same plant.

habit_description: Perennial herb to 30 cm high, very sparsely pubescent with short cottony hairs to hirtellous
leaf_description: Leaves narrowly ellipsoidal to almost linear, c. 4 mm long, fleshy
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth sparsely pubescent | Stamens 3
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth hard, sparsely pubescent | attachment circular, c. 3 mm diam., truncate, often on a slightly raised scar | tube depressed-globose with a broad base, c. 1.5 mm high and 2.5 mm wide | apex convex | limb a narrow ridge | spines 4 + 2, c. 2 mm long, spreading, the radicular pair shorter and unequal arising from a short radicular spur
seed_description: Embryo horizontal
distribution_description: Found in southern-central and central-eastern Qld.

habit_description: Rounded glabrous perennial c. 30 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves semiterete, 5--10 mm long, acute, succulent
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth glabrous, 3-lobed | Stamens 3
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth cylindrical, c. 3 mm high, 2 mm broad, slightly constricted above middle (at apex of tube proper) | base truncate | spines 2 + 2, horizontal to recurved, radicular pair c. 0.5 mm long, the others 1--2.5 mm long, all united at base into a cup-shaped structure continuous with tube
seed_description: Seed and radicle erect
habitat_description: Grows in coastal and inland slightly saline claypans.
distribution_description: Found in north-western W.A.

common_name: Star Bluebush, Star Copperburr, Starred Bluebush, Star-fruit Bassia, Starred Saltbush.
habit_description: Straggly shrub to 0.5 m high
leaf_description: Leaves linear, 5--10 (-15) mm long, woolly-villous
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth subglobular, hard, c. 2.5 mm diam., glabrous except woolly-ciliate margins to lobes | wing rigid, c. 3 mm diam. including spines | margin from crenate-dentate to c. 12-spined
habitat_description: Usually in heavy seasonally waterlogged soil.
distribution_description: Found in southern Queensland, central and western New South Wales, eastern South Australia, and northwestern Victoria.
notes: Evidently closely related to Sclerolaena walkeri, Sclerochlamys brachyptera and Maireana microcarpa but differing in the development of the perianth wing.

habit_description: Small shrub c. 50 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves slender, semiterete, 10--15 mm long, somewhat sigmoid (at least when young) with the apex recurved, densely tomentose
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth tomentose | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth tomentose | tube cylindrical, c. 2 mm high and wide, somewhat dorsiventrally compressed | base oblique | attachment elliptic | limb erect, c. 1 mm long | spines 2 + 1 or 2, tomentose, the lateral pair to 4 mm long, divergent, the radicular spines 1 or 2, adaxial, c. 1 mm long
seed_description: Seed erect
distribution_description: Only known from the type collection from north-western W.A. Check this.
notes: The sigmoid leaf-shape (similar to that found in S. forrestiana) gives this species a distinctive aspect. Possibly a hybrid involving S. forrestiana.

habit_description: Rounded shrub c. 30 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves linear, trigonous, to 30 mm long, 2--3 mm wide, silky, succulent
flower_description: Flowers in pairs | Perianth pubescent, 5-lobed | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth hard, sparsely pubescent | base solid, truncate, c. 1.5 mm high and wide | attachment circular, c. 2 mm diam. | tube shortly cylindrical, c. 1 mm high, bearing two series of appendages | antetepaline appendages 5, erect, lanceolate, 2--3 mm long, spiny, intertepaline appendages 4--12 recurved, fan-shaped, c. 3 mm long, fimbriate with pungent spines
seed_description: Seed horizontal | radicle centrifugal
habitat_description: Occurs on sandy margins of salt lakes.
distribution_description: Found in south-western N.T. and adjacent W.A. and in north-western S.A.
notes: This species differs from Sclerolaena fimbriolata in having fimbriate margins to the fruiting perianth appendages.

habit_description: Rounded perennial c. 50 cm high, usually dioecious
leaf_description: Leaves opposite or subopposite, suborbicular (when short) to semiterete, 5--15 mm long, thick and fleshy with a broad sessile base, shortly appressed-villous | the hairs slightly scabridulous
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth sparsely pilose | Male flower | stamens 5, pistillode with stigmas slender and long-exserted | Female flower | stamens absent | pistil with stigmas slender and long-exserted
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth thin and weakly crustaceous, straw-coloured | tube oblong, c. 3 mm long and 2 mm wide, very compressed dorsiventrally, glabrous, curving upwards, expanded into a broad spongy hollow base c. 3 mm diam. | limb shortly pubescent, erect, forming a short crest | spines 2, lateral, parallel and erect, to 1 mm long, sometimes with a small radicular spine adjacent to one of the lateral, or spines absent
seed_description: Seed and radicle erect
distribution_description: Found between Lake Torrens and the Flinders Ranges, S.A., also further north, around Lake Eyre.

habit_description: Sprawling intricately-branched woody perennial, glabrous
leaf_description: Leaves terete, c. 10 mm long, fleshy, narrowed at base into a short petiole
flower_description: Flowers solitary, glabrous or slightly pubescent above | Perianth 4-lobed | Stamens 4
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth hard, glabrous | attachment circular, truncate, sometimes expanded | tube shortly cylindrical, 2 mm high and wide | limb erect, conical | spines 4, equal, regularly arranged around apex of tube, spreading, c. 4 mm long
seed_description: Seed oblique | embryo erect
habitat_description: Occurs principally in heavy soil on land cleared of brigalow (Acacia harpophylla).
distribution_description: Found in south-eastern Qld and north-eastern N.S.W.

habit_description: Small erect woody perennial to 30 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves mostly erect, linear, c. 10 mm long, fleshy, villous
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth sparsely villous, 4-lobed | Stamens 4
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth hard, glabrous | tube very broadly turbinate, c. 2 mm high and 3.5 mm wide, truncate at apex and base, 4-angled, ribbed | apex cusion-shaped, 4-angled or the angles extending into short stout spines (the radicular spine usually not developed)
seed_description: Seed horizontal
habitat_description: Grows on rocky loam.
distribution_description: Found in central area of W.A.

habit_description: Shrub to 1 m high, glabrous except pubescence in leaf axils
leaf_description: Leaves slender, terete, 10--20 mm long
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Perianth glabrous or sparsely puberulous | Stamens 5
fruit_description: Fruiting perianth glabrous standing almost at right angles to branch or ascending | base horizontal, expanded | tube shortly cylindrical, c. 2 mm high and wide | limb conical | spines 3, symmetrically placed around apex of tube, slender, spreading, c. 10 mm long
seed_description: Seed and radicle horizontal to slightly oblique
distribution_description: Found in N.S.W. and south-eastern Qld, eastern S.A. and north-western Vic.

habit_description: Open perennial to 30 cm high, glabrous except axillary hairs
leaf_description: Leaves semiterete, c. 5 mm long, fleshy

ecology_description: Wurmbea inflata has exposed nectaries, which might suggest fly (Dipteran) pollination, although they are not contrastingly coloured as is the case in a number of species. Field observations showed that flies are avid visitors to the flowers of W. inflata and have been observed to probe the nectaries. They are large enough to make contact with the anthers and stigmas and their behaviour is such that pollen transfer is likely. At least two species were observed to visit flowers. However, other visitors have frequently been seen which also are likely pollinators, including two daytime species of Lepidoptera, and two species of bee (Hymenoptera), suggesting that this and perhaps other species of Wurmbea do not have specialised pollinator relationships. See Macfarlane & Case (2007) and references therein for further details on pollination in Wurmbea.

habitat_description: On Christmas Island it grows well among the large, limestone blocks behind Flying Fish Cove, and in other sites where disturbance has exposed the limestone and large trees or shrubs cannot become established. Naturalised or persisting in disturbed sites, old habitation sites, abandoned gardens, near settlement. See Weeds of Australia Fact Sheet. notes: This striking, ornamental climber is probably native to Christmas Island but fruit has not yet been collected. It spreads by root suckers as well as by seed. Pollination depends upon the presence of a long-tongued insect pollinator which may be absent from Christmas Island. Quisqualis indica L. was treated by Byrnes (1977: 64--65) but, though widely cultivated in northern Australia and sometimes persisting in old gardens, there was no evidence that it was naturalised at the time Pedley (1990) prepared the Flora of Australia Volume 18 Combretaceae treatment, hence was included only in the key to genera with a note by Pedley (1990: 256). A difficult plant to control because of its root suckering habit (Dunlop et al. 1995).

ecology_description: The fruit is often eaten by fruit bats, and on Christmas Island is dispersed by land crabs which eat the outer coat (Du Puy & Telford 1993: 244). Cooper & Cooper (2004: 128) report the fruit is eaten by Palm Cockatoos, Cassowaries and Spectacled Flying Foxes. The fruit/seed is also sea-dispersed (propagules adapted to float and tolerate immersion in sea water, allowing them to be dispersed long distances by ocean currents); illustrated by Claussen (2005: 135). One of the more common disseminules found (as flotsam) on Ashmore and Cartier beaches; described and illustrated by Pike & Leach (1997: 132, 140).
habitat_description: A characteristic tree of sandy and rocky beaches; littoral rainforest, beachfront vegetation. On Christmas Island common especially on coastal and upper terraces, often in dense, marginal forest, where it can become one of the largest trees, with massive plank buttresses. On Cocos (Keeling) Islands grows in strand forest in coralline sand, on West and Home Islands, but not common. (Du Puy & Telford 1993: 244).
distribution_description: Ranges from southeast Asia, through Malesia to Polynesia and has been extensively planted throughout the tropics. In Australia it occurs in the extreme northeast of Arnhem Land, Northern Territory, and from islands of Torres Strait to about Mission Beach near Tully, Queensland. Du Puy & Telford (1993: 244) report it is probably native to southeast Asia, extending from India, Indo-China and Malesia to northern Australia and the Pacific islands.
notes: For treatment of Terminalia catappa on Christmas and Cocos (Keeling) Islands see Du Puy & Telford (1993: 243--244). H.N. Ridley, Journal of the Straits Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society 45: 190--191 (1906) noted many very large specimens on Christmas Island, often of greater size than in other localities. It is also unusual for this species to occur naturally above the littoral zone. The leaves are deciduous, turning first yellow and then bright red before falling. (Du Puy & Telford 1993: 244).
