fruit_description: Mature fruit ovoid, with or without obscure angles and short beak, 1.5--2.5 cm long, 0.8--1.6 cm diam., succulent, glabrous, puberulous or tomentose, yellow-green, immature fruit prominently longitudinally ridged, beaked
habitat_description: In usually open communities, often in skeletal soil derived from sandstone, though occasionally associated with coastal dunes.
distribution_description: Although Pedley (1990) cites Terminalia hadleyana subsp. hadleyana (= Terminalia hadleyana) as "restricted in the western Kimberley, Western Australia; close to the coast", the Australian Plant Census (accessed 1 September 2021) lists Terminalia hadleyana occurring in Western Australia, Northern Territory and Queensland.

flowering_time_description: Flowering time somewhat irregular, recorded June-November (also March under cultivation); fruit collected August-March
fruiting_time_description: Flowering time somewhat irregular, recorded June-November (also March under cultivation); fruit collected August-March
phenology_text: Flowering time somewhat irregular, recorded June-November (also March under cultivation); fruit collected August-March.
habitat_description: Grows particularly on sand dunes or on sand flats, and occasionally on clay, in open pindan woodland of Acacia ampliceps, A. colei, A. eriopoda, Carissa lanceolata, Corymbia dampieri, C. zygophylla, Denhamia cunninghamii, Lysiphyllum cunninghamii and Ventilago viminalis, over tufting grasses of Triodia bitextura and T. schinzii.
distribution_description: Restricted to the Dampier Botanical District, Western Australia.

habit_description: Shrub or tree to 10 m high, deciduous
stem_description: Branchlets thick, glabrous or with a few scattered hairs
leaf_description: Leaves usually crowded | lamina broadly ovate, elliptic, oblong or obovate, 8--25 cm long, 6--16 cm wide, 1--2 times as long as wide, truncate or shortly attenuate at base, obtuse at apex, discolorous, glabrous, domatia small | petiole 15--50 mm long
inflorescence_description: Spike open, usually longer than leaves
flower_description: Flowers 4--8 mm long, 4--6 mm diam | Calyx pubescent outside, glabrous inside | lobes triangular, c. 2 mm long and wide | Staminal filaments 2--3 mm long | Disc villous | Style glabrous
fruit_description: Mature fruit ovoid, usually shortly beaked, 1.5--3.5 cm long, 1--2 cm diam., succulent, tomentose, yellow-green, immature fruit prominently laterally ridged, beaked
habitat_description: In usually open communities in a variety of substrates including stabilised coastal dunes.
distribution_description: Occurs from about Broome and the western Kimberley, Western Australia, to the western part of the Gulf of Carpentaria, Northern Territory.
notes: Several specimens of a taxon seemingly related to Terminalia latipes subsp. latipes have been collected a little S of Darwin, Northern Territory. As well as having similar densely pubescent fruit its branchlets have a dense, chocolate-brown indumentum and the undersides of the leaves are hairy especially along the main veins. Specimens studied so far are not good enough to allow the taxon to be formally described. (Pedley 1990: 286).

habit_description: Tree to 10 (-15) m high, deciduous
leaf_description: Leaves crowded | lamina obovate, 4.5--12 cm long, 3--7.5 cm wide, 1.2--1.8 times as long as wide, attenuate at base, obtuse at apex, discolorous, glabrous, domatia absent or rare, small | petiole 5--20 mm long
inflorescence_description: Spike dense, c. same length as leaves
flower_description: Flowers 5--6 mm long, c. 6 mm diam | Calyx glabrous | lobes triangular, c. 2 mm long and wide | Staminal filaments 2--3 mm long | Disc villous | Style glabrous
fruit_description: Mature fruit ovoid or globular, usually compressed with distinct longitudinal angles, not beaked, 2--3 cm long, 1.5--2 cm diam., succulent, smooth, green, immature fruit compressed, with a continuous wing to 5 mm wide
habitat_description: Usually found on rocks close to the sea. Rainforest, littoral rainforest, coastal vine thickets, open forest.
distribution_description: Occurs in coastal areas of central Queensland.

common_name: As synonym Terminalia sericocarpa: Sovereignwood, Damson, Damson Plum, Bandicoot.
habit_description: Tree to 30 (-40) m high, deciduous
leaf_description: Leaves not crowded | lamina obovate, rarely elliptic, 6--13.5 cm long, 3--6 cm wide, 1.7--3 times as long as wide, cuneate or attenuate at base, obtuse or shortly obtusely acuminate at apex, discolorous, shiny above, sparsely pubescent, becoming glabrous or almost so on one or both surfaces, domatia small | petiole 4--12 mm long
inflorescence_description: Spike dense or open, shorter or longer than leaves
flower_description: Flowers 3--4 mm long, c. 5 mm diam | Calyx sericeous outside, usually glabrous inside | lobes triangular, c. 2 mm long and wide | Staminal filaments 2--3 mm long | Disc villous | Style villous
fruit_description: Fruit ovoid, slightly compressed, obscurely angled, 1.3--1.8 cm long, c. 1 cm wide, sparsely sericeous or glabrous, succulent, red or purple, immature fruit compressed, apiculate, sericeous
dispersal_description: Fruit eaten by many bird species, Spectacled Flying-foxes and Cuscus (Cooper & Cooper 2004: 130)
ecology_description: Fruit eaten by many bird species, Spectacled Flying-foxes and Cuscus (Cooper & Cooper 2004: 130).
habitat_description: Usually found in drier types of rainforest, on rainforest margins and banks of large streams. Evergreen and semi-deciduous monsoon vine forest, often emergent above canopy (Wightman & Andrews 1989: 84). Rainforest, monsoon forest, vine thickets, gallery forest, sclerophyll forest (Cooper & Cooper 2004: 130).
distribution_description: Extends from the northern part of the Kimberley, Western Australia, across Arnhem Land to Groote Eylandt, Northern Territory, and from Cape York to about Rockhampton, Queensland.

habit_description: Tree to 10 (-18) m high, deciduous
leaf_description: Leaves crowded | lamina obovate, 5--15 cm long, 2.5--8 cm wide, c. 1.4--3 times as long as wide, attenuate at base, obtuse or obtusely acuminate at apex, discolorous, becoming almost glabrous, domatia often present and conspicuous | petiole 2--25 mm long
inflorescence_description: Spike open, usually longer than leaves
flower_description: Flowers 3--5 mm long, c. 6 mm diam | Calyx tube appressed pubescent outside | lobes triangular, c. 2 mm long and wide | Staminal filaments c. 3 mm long | Disc villous | Style glabrous
fruit_description: Mature fruit ovoid or ellipsoidal, sometimes shortly beaked, 1.2--2 cm long, 0.8--1.5 cm diam., succulent, smooth, purple or black, immature fruit similar in shape or somewhat compressed
dispersal_description: Fruit eaten by many bird species (Cooper & Cooper 2004: 129)
ecology_description: Food plant for the larval stages of the Common Oakblue Butterfly (Common & Waterhouse 1981, per Zich et al. 2020). Fruit eaten by many bird species (Cooper & Cooper 2004: 129).
habitat_description: Common in low closed-forest on stabilised dunes and occasionally on sandstone on the coast.
distribution_description: Occurs from Rockhampton to Cape York, Queensland, extending a small distance south along the western side of Cape York Peninsula.
notes: One of the specimens cited in the original description of T. muelleri was collected by Brown from 'islands of Carpentaria'. The species has been collected since from the western side of Cape York Peninsula as far south as Mapoon, but not from islands of the Gulf of Carpentaria. Brown's specimen at K has no collection data at all. It could well have come from one of Brown's collecting localities on the east coast of Queensland.

habit_description: Shrub or tree to 15 m high, deciduous
leaf_description: Leaves | lamina obovate, elliptic or oblong, 1.5--6 cm long, 0.5--2.5 cm wide, 2--4 times as long as wide, attenuate at base, sometimes decurrent along petiole, obtuse, occasionally retuse at apex, discolorous, glabrous, domatia absent | petiole 3--20 mm long
inflorescence_description: Spike open, longer than leaves
flower_description: Flowers 5--8 mm long, c. 5 mm diam | Calyx often glabrous outside (almost glabrous or thinly pubescent outside), villous inside | lobes triangular, 1.5 mm long and wide | Staminal filaments 2--3 mm long | Disc villous | Style villous in lower part
fruit_description: Fruit a 2-winged nut, glabrous, body 1--2 cm long | wings 1--3 cm wide at widest part, tending to be membranous, rounded
habitat_description: Often in pure stands or associated with Coolibah (Eucalyptus microtheca) and Brigalow in heavy soil.
distribution_description: Endemic in eastern Queensland.
notes: Poisonous to stock. Toxic properties, see McKenzie (2012).

common_name: Blackberry Tree, Marool, Marool (Bardi, Nyul Nyul), Nawulu (Yawuru).
habit_description: Tree to 10 m high, deciduous
leaf_description: Leaves not crowded | lamina elliptic or ovate, 6--13 cm long, 3.5--8 cm wide, 1.3--2, rarely 3 times as long as wide, cuneate and sometimes oblique at base, obtuse or obtusely acuminate at apex, discolorous, often shiny above, scattered appressed hairs below when mature, domatia not numerous, small, well defined | petiole 30--60 mm long
inflorescence_description: Spike open, shorter than leaves
flower_description: Flowers 6--8 mm long, c. 6 mm diam | Calyx glabrous | lobes triangular, c. 2 mm long and wide | Staminal filaments c. 4 mm long | Disc villous | Style glabrous
fruit_description: Mature fruit ellipsoidal, with a distinct beak, 2--2.5 cm long, 1--1.5 cm diam., succulent, smooth, dark red to black, immature fruit with 2 obscure lateral angles
habitat_description: Often subdominant in low closed-forest in sandy soil derived either from old dunes or from sandstone.
distribution_description: Coastal areas of the Kimberley, Western Australia.

habit_description: Tree to 20 m high, deciduous or semideciduous
leaf_description: Leaves sometimes crowded | lamina elliptic or obovate, 7--22 cm long, 5--14 cm wide, c. 1--2 times as long as wide, cuneate or obtuse at base, obtuse at apex, coriaceous, concolorous, pilulose, glabrescent above, domatia sometimes occur | petiole 15--50 mm long
inflorescence_description: Spike rather dense, shorter than leaves
flower_description: Flowers c. 5 mm diam. | male flowers 3--5 mm long | bisexual flowers 5--7 mm long | Calyx pubescent outside, glabrous or somewhat villous inside | lobes triangular, c. 1.5 mm long and wide | Staminal filaments c. 4 mm long | Disc villous | Style villous
fruit_description: Mature fruit cylindrical, with a distinct beak, 2--4 cm long, 0.7--1.5 cm diam., succulent, smooth, purple, immature fruit with usually 2 longitudinal ridges
habitat_description: Usually in sandy soil on stream banks or rarely behind coastal dunes, but also around gilgais in clay soil.
distribution_description: A widespread common species, confined to Australia north of c. 20°S.

habit_description: Tree to 15 m high, deciduous
leaf_description: Leaves | lamina rectangular or obovate, 4--8.5 cm long, (1.5-) 2--5 cm wide, cuneate at base, obtuse or occasionally retuse at apex, discolorous, pubescent | upper surface glabrescent | domatia absent | petiole 8--18 mm long, rarely to 25 mm
inflorescence_description: Spike open or dense, longer than leaves
flower_description: Flowers 3--8 mm long, c. 5 mm diam | Calyx pubescent outside | lobes triangular, 2 mm long, 1.5 mm wide | Staminal filaments 2--4 mm long | Disc villous | Style villous
fruit_description: Fruit a 2-winged nut, pubescent particularly on body, body 1.5--3 cm long | wings 4--12 cm wide, with striate venation
dispersal_description: Seeds eaten by Red-tailed Black Cockatoos (Cooper & Cooper 2004: 130)
ecology_description: Seeds eaten by Red-tailed Black Cockatoos (Cooper & Cooper 2004: 130).
habitat_description: Often growing in deep soil in areas with little topographic relief; woodland, vine thickets.
distribution_description: Ranging from the Cambridge Gulf area, Western Australia, to central Arnhem Land, Northern Territory, with a marked disjunction to the southern part of Cape York Peninsula, Queensland.

habit_description: Tree to 15 (-18) m high, deciduous
leaf_description: Leaves crowded | lamina obovate to obtriangular, (3-) 4--10 cm long, (1.8-) 2.5--6 cm, rarely to 7.5 cm wide, 1.3--2.4 times as long as wide, attenuate at base, obtuse at apex, discolorous, glabrous or sparsely pilose beneath, domatia absent | petiole 4--12 mm, rarely 15 mm, long
inflorescence_description: Spike dense, c. same length as leaves
flower_description: Flowers c. 5 mm diam. | bisexual flowers 6--7 mm long | male flowers 3--4 mm long | Calyx glabrous or occasionally pubescent outside, glabrous inside | lobes triangular, c. 2 mm long and wide | Staminal filaments c. 4 mm long | Disc villous | Style glabrous
fruit_description: Mature fruit globular or ovoid, not beaked, 1--2 cm long, 0.8--1.5 cm diam., succulent, smooth, green, immature fruit compressed, encircled by a prominent wing
habitat_description: Found in dry rainforest communities and as isolated trees on rock, often limestone. Littoral rainforest, gallery forest, vine thickets (Cooper & Cooper 2004: 130).
distribution_description: Occurs from Herberton to about Maryborough, Queensland, near the coast.

habit_description: Prostrate multi-stemmed shrub, with stems to 1 m, occasionally a weakly erect stem to 1 m, deciduous
leaf_description: Leaves not crowded | lamina broadly ovate, oblong or orbicular, 9--17.5 cm long, 7--11 cm wide, 1--1.7 times as long as wide, truncate, cordate or somewhat attenuate at base, obtuse at apex, concolorous, villous when young, retaining hairs on veins beneath, domatia absent | petiole 10--30 mm long
inflorescence_description: Spike rather open, shorter than leaves
flower_description: Flowers c. 6 mm long, c. 6 mm diam | Calyx villous outside, glabrous inside | lobes triangular, c. 2 mm long and wide | Staminal filaments c. 2.5 mm long | Disc villous | Style glabrous
fruit_description: Mature fruit ovoid, sometimes shortly beaked, 1.3--2 cm long, 1--1.5 cm diam., succulent, pubescent, red, immature fruit longitudinally angled, beaked
distribution_description: An uncommon species restricted to Arnhem Land, Northern Territory, and central Cape York Peninsula, Queensland, where it occurs with Eucalyptus tetrodonta .

habit_description: Shrub or small tree to 7 m high, deciduous
leaf_description: Leaves not crowded | lamina ellipitc to obovate, 3.5--7 cm long, 2--3.5 cm, rarely 4.5 cm wide, abruptly contracted into petiole, obtuse at apex, concolorous, sparsely hairy or glabrous, domatia present, inconspicuous | petiole 5--15 mm long
inflorescence_description: Spike open or dense, c. same length as leaves
flower_description: Flowers c. 5 mm diam. | bisexual flowers 6--9 mm long | male flowers 4--6 mm long | Calyx pubescent outside | lobes triangular, acuminate, 1.5 mm long, 2 mm wide | Staminal filaments c. 4 mm long | Disc villous | Style with a few long hairs at base
fruit_description: Fruit a nut, 2--3 cm long, c. 1.5 cm wide, including the wing, glabrous
habitat_description: Grows in sandy or gravelly soil in open eucalypt communities.
distribution_description: Confined to northern Northern Territory.

habit_description: Tree to 10 (-16) m high, deciduous
leaf_description: Leaves usually crowded | lamina obovate or occasionally oblong or elliptic, usually 5--13 cm long, 3--7.5 cm wide, 1.3--2 times as long as wide, cuneate or shortly attenuate at base, usually recurved margin, obtuse at apex, discolorous, initially pubescent, at least some hairs on lower surface when mature, domatia rare | petiole 5--35 mm long
inflorescence_description: Spike open, usually longer than leaves
flower_description: Flowers 3--5 mm long, 4--5 mm diam | Calyx pubescent outside, sparsely pilose inside | lobes triangular, c. 2 mm long and wide | Staminal filaments 3--5 mm long | Disc villous | Style villous
fruit_description: Mature fruit ellipsoidal or cylindrical, sometimes shortly beaked, 1--1.5 cm long, 0.5--1 cm diam., succulent, smooth, purple, immature fruit with 2 longitudinal ridges and sometimes winged at tip
dispersal_description: Host to the Cyane Jewel butterfly, whose pupae live in the nests of attendant ants (Beasley 2009: 160) Fruit eaten by Red-tailed Black Cockatoos and Figbirds (Cooper & Cooper 2004: 130)
ecology_description: Host to the Cyane Jewel butterfly, whose pupae live in the nests of attendant ants (Beasley 2009: 160). Fruit eaten by Red-tailed Black Cockatoos and Figbirds (Cooper & Cooper 2004: 130).
habitat_description: Occurs in low closed communities on stabilised dunes and alluvial, often sandy soil and in woodland, sometimes adjacent to grassland. Monsoon forest, vine thickets, littoral rainforest, gallery forest, heathland, woodland (Cooper & Cooper 2004: 130).
distribution_description: Extends from the Macarthur River area, Northern Territory, across northern Queensland, to the Western Division of Papua New Guinea.

habit_description: Shrub to 3 m high, deciduous
leaf_description: Leaves usually crowded | lamina ovate to obovate, 3.5--7.5 cm long, 2.5--4.5 cm wide, 1.4--1.7 times as long as wide, attenuate at base, obtuse at apex, discolorous, shiny above, appressed puberulous, denser beneath, domatia absent | petiole c. 10 mm long
inflorescence_description: Spike open, c. same length as leaves
flower_description: Flowers 4--7 mm long, 3--4 mm diam | Calyx appressed pubescent outside, glabrous inside | lobes triangular, c. 1.5 mm long and wide | Staminal filaments c. 3 mm long | Disc villous | Style glabrous
fruit_description: Mature fruit globular or ovoid, sometimes shortly beaked, 1--2 cm long, 1--1.5 cm diam., succulent, smooth, colour unknown, immature fruit compressed, laterally winged or ridged, shortly beaked
habitat_description: Reported to occur among basalt rocks.
distribution_description: A rare species known only from a few collections, confined to the Nickol Bay area near Dampier, Western Australia.

common_name: Common Yellow Commelina, Yellow Wandering Jew.
habit_description: See Wilson (1993) or Commelina africana in New South Wales Flora Online (accessed 12 May 2026)
distribution_description: Native to Africa. Recorded from the Greenwich area in Sydney, N.S.W.

common_name: Hairy Wandering Creeper, Hairy Wandering Jew, Benghal Dayflower.
habit_description: A creeping perennial herb to c. 30 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves ovate to elliptic, c. 2--9 cm long, to 3 cm wide, obtuse to acute, shortly hairy, narrowed into a short petiole with reddish marginal bristles, and a basal, tubular sheath | lamina subcircular, blue
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence leaf-opposed | bract funnel-shaped, c. 10--12 mm long, flattened, shortly hairy
flower_description: Sepals 3, unequal, free, bluish | Petals 3, unequal, the upper 2 conspicuous, c. 8 mm long including a claw 2 mm long | Stamens 3, with 1 yellow and 2 blue anthers | staminodes 3, with yellow, cruciform anthers | filaments glabrous, blue | Style slender, blue
fruit_description: Capsule pyriform, enclosed by bract
pollination_description: The stems sometimes produce cleistogamous, subterranean flowers within a small, yellowish bract
habitat_description: On Christmas Island common along roadsides, in marginal or disturbed vegetation and in gardens, especially in the east of the island in damp soil.
distribution_description: A widespread, weedy species in tropical and subtropical Africa, SE Asia (from the Middle East to China and Japan, and IndoChina), Malesia to Australia and the Pacific islands, and occasionally in the New World. Naturalised in W.A., Ch. Is., N.T., Qld and N.S.W.
notes: The stems sometimes produce cleistogamous, subterranean flowers within a small, yellowish bract.

habit_description: Erect or trailing to 80 cm, glabrous
leaf_description: Leaves cauline, subpetiolate | petiole 3--8 mm long | sheath apex ciliate | lamina lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 3.5--10 cm long, (1.2-) 2--4 cm wide, acuminate, scabrous adaxially, green
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence a scapose dense panicle to c. 6 cm, hirsute
flower_description: Flowers numerous per branch | Sepals 2--4 mm long, 1--1.5 mm wide, membranous, abaxially hirsute, pink-purple to blue | Petals 3--5 mm long, 1--2 mm wide, pink-purple to bright blue | Stamens with filiform filaments | anthers pink-purple
fruit_description: Capsule ovoid, compressed, 3--4 mm long, c. 2 mm wide
seed_description: Seeds several, 2--2.5 mm long, grey with black horizontal stripes, smooth
habitat_description: Along creeks, wet and swampy sites in rainforest.
distribution_description: A widespread semi-aquatic riparian species apparently extending across Asia and Africa. In Australia it occurs around Rockingham Bay and the Daintree River as well as the Torres Strait Islands.

common_name: Flowering Inch Plant, Moss Inch Plant, Spiderwort.
habit_description: See Tradescantia cerinthoides in New South Wales Flora Online (accessed 12 May 2026)
distribution_description: Native to South America. Sparingly naturalised in S.A. (Adelaide) and N.S.W. (Sydney region, see Hosking et al. 2011: 88).

profile_author: D.J. Du Puy, I.R.H. Telford, P.S. Green, P.G. Kodela
habit_description: Erect herb
stem_description: Stem short, stoutish, to c. 20 cm high
leaf_description: Leaves crowded basally, erect, sessile | lamina linear-lanceolate, 20--35 cm long, long-acuminate, dark green above, purple beneath
inflorescence_description: Inflorescence axillary, circinnate
flower_description: flowers many, scarcely projecting from bracts | Petals ovate, 8--9 mm long, free, white
ecology_description: Garden escape.
habitat_description: Commonly cultivated on Christmas Island and dispersed among garden refuse, now naturalised and spreading over the steep volcanic rocks at Waterfall, tolerating deep shade under the forest canopy. Also occurs along the east coast among limestone pinnacles behind the sea cliff, hidden beneath Scaevola bushes and on one of the rocks in Flying Fish Cove, near Smith Point. On Cocos (Keeling) Island naturalised near the kampong in coral rubble on Home Island. On Lord Howe Island this species has established itself in disturbed forest near houses. In Queensland recorded from littoral rainforest and woodlands near the beach.
distribution_description: A native of tropical and subtropical Central America and the Caribbean, frequently cultivated and often naturalised throughout the tropics. Naturalised in Queensland and on Christmas Island, Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Lord Howe Island.

common_name: Shell Vine, Conch Vine, Scarlet Shell Vine, Danis Vine.
leaflet_count_description: Leaves compound, usually 1--5-foliolate (usually 3--5 leaflets), 10--40 cm long
habit_description: Vine, twining

inflorescence_description: Panicles to 40 cm long, ferruginous-pubescent

fruit_description: Fruit obovoid, sometimes strongly curved, 18--30 mm long, orange to red, striate
seed_description: Seed 1, obovoid to obloid, c. 16--18 mm long, black | aril yellow (to orange)
habitat_description: Rainforest.
distribution_description: There are 2 subspecies; subsp. conchocarpus is indigenous to north-eastern Queensland on Cape York Peninsula; subsp. schumannianus (Gilg) Leenh. occurs in New Guinea.

common_name: Shell Vine, Conch Vine, Danis Vine, Scarlet Shell Vine.
stem_length_description: stems to 20 m or more long
habit_description: Woody liane, sometimes shrubby, with stems to 20 m or more long
inflorescence_description: Panicles 2--20 cm long
flower_description: Flowers strongly scented
fruit_description: Fruit obovoid, 18--26 (-30) mm long, red
seed_description: Seed c. 16--18 mm long
habitat_description: Grows in coastal to montane rainforests, in a variety of soils including those derived from granite and volcanics, to c. 800 m alt.
distribution_description: Endemic to north-eastern Queensland mainly from Cooktown S to Tully-Mission Beach area.

leaflet_count_description: Leaves compound, usually 3-foliolate (sometimes 1--5 leaflets), 7--13 cm long
habit_description: Woody liane
stem_description: stems to 30 m long | stem apices sometimes twining | stems climbing by twining, 'tendrils' and modified branches (B. Hyland 21180V)

flower_description: Sepals c. 2--3 mm long | Petals 5, c. 5--7 mm long, white | calyx remnants persistent at base
fruit_description: Fruit (follicle) ovoid, 12--20 mm long, 6--8 mm wide, yellow or orange, longitudinally striated
seed_description: Seed 1, c. 8--10 mm long, cream, enclosed in red aril
habitat_description: Grows in coastal to montane rainforests, in a variety of soils including those derived from alluvium, granites, metamorphics, basalt and other volcanics, to 700 m alt.
distribution_description: Endemic to north-eastern Queensland, south of Cooktown to c. Mackay.

habit_description: Vine, twiner, climbing or creeping
leaf_description: Leaves alternate | petiole 5--12 cm long | lamina sagittate with a broad sinus and short triangular lobe each side near base, 4--9 cm long, 3.5--7 cm wide, attenuate onto petiole, acute to slightly acuminate, mucronulate, thin-textured
inflorescence_description: pedicel 4--13 cm long | bracts broadly ovate to suborbicular, 1.2--1.5 cm long, cordate
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Sepals ovate, c. 5 mm long, mucronulate | Corolla shortly funnel-shaped, 2.5--3.5 cm long, scarcely lobed, pink with 5 creamy longitudinal bands
fruit_description: Fruit unknown
habitat_description: Most of the few known populations are found in mountain localities, on higher parts including mountain tops, in open, sunny moist areas. The Old Settlement population on Lord Howe Island grows on a slope in amongst introduced Kikuyu grass on the edge of Drypetes/Cryptocarya forest. (Department of Environment and Climate Change (NSW) 2007: 126; Director of National Parks 2010: 81).
distribution_description: Endemic to Norfolk Island and Lord Howe Island.

habit_description: Prostrate herb with a creeping rhizome
leaf_description: Leaves with petiole 1--6 cm long | lamina reniform with a shallow sinus, 1--4 cm long, 1.5--6 cm wide, attenuate onto petiole, entire to slightly and shallowly sinuate-denticulate, rounded to slightly emarginate with a minute apiculum
inflorescence_description: pedicel 2--9 cm long | bracts ovate, 1--1.4 cm long, cordate, obtuse
flower_description: Flowers solitary | Sepals slightly longer than bracts, obtuse, mucronate | Corolla funnel-shaped, 3.5--4 cm long, pink with 5 white longitudinal bands
fruit_description: Fruit ovoid-globose, 1.5 cm long, apiculate
seed_description: Seeds dark brown, smooth
habitat_description: Grows in sand by the sea; coastal dunes, strandlines.
distribution_description: This species is widespread in northern and southern temperate regions of eastern and western Australia (W.A., Qld, N.S.W., Vic., Tas.), Norfolk Island and Lord Howe Island.

common_name: Muskwood, Muskheart, Canary Muskheart, Brown Muskheart, Black Muskheart, Hairy Muskwood (subsp. tomentosum).
habit_description: Tree to 9 m high, sometimes taller (to 20 m), tomentose to glabrescent
leaf_description: Leaves | lamina lanceolate to ovate or elliptic, rarely obovate, often asymmetric, 3.5--20 cm long, 1--9 cm wide, cordate to cuneate base, entire margin, obtuse to acute-acuminate to apex, chartaceous, with 5--10 pairs of veins | petiole 3--20 mm long

flower_description: Calyx hairy like vegetative parts, campanulate, toothed, to 3.5 mm long | Petals 4--8, linear, dilated and cohering at base, to c. 15 mm long, hairy, creamy white to pale yellow | Stamens about as long as petals | Style to 8 mm long, hairy or glabrous | stigmas 2 or 3 | ovary subcylindrical, 1-locular
fruit_description: Drupe ellipsoidal or globose to oblong, 1--3 cm long, 0.5--1.5 cm wide, glabrous or hairy
habitat_description: Rainforest.
